jobs.description:
About The Lawyering Project 

Founded in 2017, the Lawyering Project is a legal advocacy organization that blends traditional impact litigation with movement lawyering to promote reproductive health, rights, and justice throughout the United States. Laws that undermine reproductive health, rights, and justice deprive people of moral agency, rob us of control over our bodies, and compound other forms of oppression like racism, sexism, and poverty. Our mission is to eliminate these laws and the harmful impacts they have on people’s lives. We are especially focused on laws that limit the availability or affordability of abortion care; contribute to disparities in reproductive health outcomes; embody gender-based stereotypes; or discriminate against people based on their reproductive decisions.

We have three legal programs: Litigation, Access & Innovation, and Pro Bono Initiatives. Our Litigation Program leverages the courts to eliminate barriers to reproductive health services and promote equity in access to care. Our Access & Innovation Program provides legal advice and technical assistance to healthcare providers, researchers, abortion funds, and organizations that facilitate access to abortion care.

Our Pro Bono Initiatives Program operates the Abortion Defense Network, a collaborative effort by nonprofit organizations, private law firms, and government officials aimed at ensuring everyone threatened with liability for providing or supporting abortion care in post-Roe America has access to high-quality, values-aligned lawyers. 

For further information, visit and .

About The Internship

The Lawyering Project is seeking legal interns to support its legal programs during the summer of 2027. The legal internship is remote, and legal interns may choose to work from a minimum of ten weeks to a maximum of twelve weeks from May-August 2027.

We are looking for individuals who possess strong research, writing, and analytical skills. Ideal candidates will be able to effectively manage multiple tasks, collaborate with colleagues, and contribute to a positive and supportive work environment. All interns will have the opportunity to gain practical experience in a variety of legal tasks.

The essential duties and responsibilities for this internship include, but are not limited to:

  • Conducting legal and factual research, analysis, and writing; 
  • Cite-checking and copy-editing legal documents; 
  • Assisting with court filings; 
  • Assisting with client advising;
  • Providing additional support to the Lawyering Project’s legal programs, as needed; and
  • Cultivating an organizational culture that aligns with the Lawyering Project’s core values 

Requirements

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE 

The summer legal intern must be currently enrolled in a law school located in the United States.  Current 2Ls (students who will be rising 3Ls in the summer of 2027) are strongly encouraged to apply.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES 

The summer legal intern must have:

  • A demonstrated commitment to social justice and an interest in reproductive health, rights, and justice
  • Skill in legal research, writing, and analysis
  • Ability to analyze complex legal issues, meet deadlines, work well under pressure, and contribute to a collaborative team environment and a diverse, equitable, and inclusive work culture

APPLICATION DEADLINE

Applications will be accepted and reviewed on a rolling basis, with a priority deadline of October 1.

APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS

  • Resume
  • Cover Letter
    • As part of your application for the summer legal intern position, please include a cover letter that describes your experiences with legal research, writing, and analysis.
    • If you have participated in any legal clinics, please provide details about your role and the skills you developed or if you have worked on a law journal, mention the responsibilities you had and how this experience has prepared you for a legal internship.
    • Lastly, in a section of your cover letter, please describe (in no more than 150 words) why you are interested in supporting the Lawyering Project's work to improve access to reproductive healthcare.
  • Writing Sample
    • Please upload a writing sample (5-10 pages) demonstrating your legal writing and research skills.
  • Three References
    • Please provide three professional references, including the person’s name, organizational affiliation, title, and your relationship to the reference.

Benefits

COMPENSATION

The Lawyering Project will provide legal interns with a stipend of $625 per week (up to a maximum of $7,500 for 12 weeks), minus any funding that an intern receives from their law school. We ask all interns to apply for summer internship funding if their law school offers it.

All legitimate communication from our recruitment team will come from an official email address via email, we will not text you about a role you have not applied to or shown interest in. We will not perform any interviews via text or Zoom chat.
CALSTART does not ask for any fees or personal information such as social security numbers or bank details during the recruitment process.
About Us:

CALSTART is a mission-driven industry organization focused on transportation decarbonization and clean air for all.

For over 30 years, it’s been CALSTART’s mission to develop, assess, and implement large-scale, zero-emission transportation solutions to mitigate climate change and support economic growth. CALSTART works with businesses, organizations, governments, and communities to create real-life impact toward clean air and equitable access to clean transportation for all. CALSTART provides scientific, technical and policy support for regulatory development and clean technology and infrastructure acceleration.

About The Role:

The OEMs & Equipment Project Manager supports CALSTART's Dealer Training & Engagement Team by managing vehicle, equipment, manufacturer, and dealer related activities across the on road and off road Voucher Incentive Programs administered by CALSTART. Reporting to the Deputy Director of Dealer Training & Engagement, this role works closely with original equipment manufacturers, dealers, internal program teams, and government partners to coordinate vehicle and equipment additions, updates, removals, deactivations, eligibility changes, dealer affiliations, and other catalog related functions. The position helps ensure that program systems, public facing information, and internal records remain accurate, current, and aligned with program requirements.

The ideal candidate brings experience with commercial vehicles, zero emission technologies, or on and off road equipment, along with strong project management, data management, analytical, and communication skills. Daily responsibilities include tracking approval and eligibility documentation, maintaining records in Salesforce and website authoring platforms, analyzing vehicle and equipment data, preparing reports, supporting process improvements, and developing clear procedures for recurring workflows. This role will also help streamline and automate vehicle and equipment intake, year end vehicle deactivation, OEM notifications, reporting, and related administrative processes. The position offers an opportunity to work directly with emerging clean transportation technologies, build productive relationships with manufacturers and dealers, and improve the systems and processes that support transition to zero emission vehicles and equipment.

Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Manage vehicle, equipment, OEM, and dealer related workflows across CALSTART administered on road and off road Voucher Incentive Programs, including additions, removals, deactivations, eligibility updates, dealer affiliations, and other program changes.
  • Serve as a primary point of contact for original equipment manufacturers and participating dealers, providing clear, accurate, and timely communication regarding program processes, documentation requirements, system updates, and next steps.
  • Review and track vehicle and equipment approval or eligibility documentation, coordinate required follow up, and ensure information is accurately reflected across Salesforce, public facing websites, internal tracking tools, and related program systems.
  • Lead projects to standardize, streamline, and document recurring OEM and equipment workflows, including approval letter intake, catalog updates, OEM notifications, year end vehicle deactivation, and dealer or manufacturer change processes.
  • Maintain and analyze vehicle, equipment, OEM, and dealer data to identify trends, monitor workflow status, support decision making, and prepare recurring or ad hoc reports for program leadership and internal partners.
  • Develop and maintain standard operating procedures, process maps, templates, trackers, and training materials that improve accuracy, consistency, efficiency, and continuity across Voucher Incentive Programs.
  • Partner with the Dealer Training & Engagement Team to translate policy, equipment, and system changes into clear guidance, training resources, and communications for dealers and OEM representatives.
  • Collaborate closely with Voucher Processing, Policy, Technology, Data & Analytics, Marketing and Communications, program leadership, and government agency partners to resolve issues and ensure coordinated implementation of program changes.
  • Identify opportunities to reduce manual work and improve data quality through automation, system enhancements, and improved use of platforms such as Salesforce, website authoring software, Monday.com, and other program management tools.
  • Support the successful launch and ongoing administration of new Voucher Incentive Programs, vehicle categories, equipment types, technologies, and program requirements by coordinating readiness activities across internal and external stakeholders.
  • Manage multiple concurrent projects and time sensitive requests while maintaining organized records, clear priorities, dependable follow through, and consistent communication with stakeholders.
  • Contribute to organizational goals by improving the accuracy of public facing program information, strengthening OEM and dealer relationships, reducing processing delays, and supporting the adoption of zero emission vehicles and equipment.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in transportation, engineering, environmental studies, business administration, public policy, project management, data analytics, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
  • At least five years of relevant experience in transportation, vehicle or equipment manufacturing, clean energy, incentive program administration, project management, or a related field, including experience independently managing projects and stakeholder relationships.
  • Working knowledge of on road vehicles, off road equipment, commercial fleets, original equipment manufacturers, dealerships, or zero emission transportation technologies.
  • Strong project management, data management, and analytical skills, including the ability to manage multiple workstreams, maintain accurate records, identify trends or discrepancies, track deliverables, and prepare clear reports.
  • Proficiency with Salesforce or a comparable customer relationship management system, along with experience using website authoring or content management software, project management platforms, spreadsheets, and other data tracking tools.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, organization, judgment, and problem solving skills, with the ability to interpret technical or program requirements, communicate clearly with internal and external stakeholders, work independently, and improve complex or manual processes.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Advanced degree or professional certification in transportation, engineering, environmental studies, public policy, business administration, project management, data analytics, or a related field.
  • Experience administering government funded incentive, rebate, grant, or voucher programs, particularly programs supporting clean transportation, commercial vehicles, or off road equipment.
  • Familiarity with zero emission vehicle and equipment technologies, including battery electric, fuel cell electric, charging, hydrogen fueling, or related infrastructure considerations.
  • Experience working directly with original equipment manufacturers, dealers, fleets, regulatory agencies, or public sector partners in a transportation or equipment focused environment.
  • Advanced experience with Salesforce, website content management systems, Monday.com, Microsoft Excel, data visualization tools, workflow automation, or system integration projects.
  • Experience leading process improvement initiatives, developing technical or dealer facing training resources, and translating regulatory or technical requirements into clear operational procedures.
  • Ability and willingness to travel occasionally for meetings, trainings, industry events, vehicle or equipment demonstrations, and other program related activities. The role may require extended periods working at a computer and occasionally moving or handling materials used for meetings or events.
We understand that not everyone will match the above qualifications 100%. If your background isn't perfectly aligned but you feel you would be a great addition to the team, we'd love to hear from you.
We're a tight-knit team of world-class innovators, business minds, and change agents who believe passionately in our mission and put our team ahead of self. We are committed to the continued development and growth of our employees and invest in your success!
We care about your personal well being as much as your professional success and offer generous benefits to full time employees including: 100% company paid comprehensive health benefits for Medical, Dental, Vision, Short Term Disability, Long Term Disability and Life Insurance, Retirement plan with generous company contributions, FSA for Health and Dependent Care, 3 weeks of vacation time in the first year of employment, 11 paid company holidays, paid sick time, paid family leave, and more!
Our inclusive environment focuses on making decisions based on merit without regard to race, color, hair texture, gender, religion, age, nationality, social or ethnic origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, LGBTQIA+ status, marital status, pregnancy, disability, genetics, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Solenis is a 2025 Best Managed Company Gold Standard honoree.

For additional information about Solenis, please visitwww.solenis.com or follow us on social media.

Executive Talent Partner - Industrial Water Commercial Sales

Location : United States (flexible / regional focus)

This Role Is For Industry Insiders

Solenis is seeking a highly connected Industrial Water professional to lead commercial talent acquisition efforts for one of the industry's most important growth businesses.

This role is specifically designed for individuals who have built careers within the industrial water treatment industry, either as:

  • Industrial Water Sales Representatives

  • Strategic Account Managers

  • Business Development Leaders

  • Regional Sales Managers

  • Commercial Leaders

  • Executive Recruiters specializing in Industrial Water talent

If your background is primarily general corporate recruiting, HR, or talent acquisition without significant Industrial Water industry experience and relationships, this position is likely not a fit.

Why This Role Exists

The Industrial Water market is relationship-driven. The best commercial talent is rarely active in the job market and is often recruited through trusted industry connections.

Success in this role depends on your ability to leverage an established network of Industrial Water sales professionals, commercial leaders, and industry influencers to identify and attract high-performing talent.

This is not a sourcing-heavy recruiting role. It is a market-facing position focused on industry engagement, relationship building, and commercial talent strategy.

What You'll Do

Serve as a Strategic Advisor to Commercial Leadership

  • Partner directly with Industrial Water business leaders to support growth initiatives and critical hiring priorities

  • Develop talent strategies aligned with territory expansion plans, customer growth opportunities, and commercial objectives

  • Provide ongoing market intelligence regarding competitors, hiring trends, compensation, and talent availability

Leverage Industry Relationships

  • Utilize your existing Industrial Water network to identify and engage top-performing commercial professionals

  • Build relationships with passive candidates across the industry

  • Develop talent maps of key competitors and adjacent industry players

  • Maintain a robust pipeline of future sales and commercial leadership talent

Evaluate Commercial Talent

  • Assess candidates' sales effectiveness, technical knowledge, customer relationships, and business development capabilities

  • Evaluate consultative selling skills and industry credibility

  • Present talent recommendations and market insights to leadership teams

What We're Looking For

Required Background

7+ years of experience within the Industrial Water Treatment industry in either:

  • Commercial Sales

  • Business Development

  • Account Management

  • Sales Leadership

  • Executive Search / Recruiting focused specifically on Industrial Water talent

Industry Network

  • Deep, established network of Industrial Water sales, account management, and commercial leadership professionals

  • Demonstrated ability to access passive talent through industry relationships

  • Strong understanding of the competitive Industrial Water landscape

Commercial Expertise

  • Proven understanding of Industrial Water sales cycles, territory management, and solution-selling approaches

  • Ability to engage experienced sales professionals as a credible peer

  • Strong business acumen and understanding of commercial performance drivers

Ideal Candidate Profiles

We are particularly interested in:

  • Former Industrial Water sales professionals seeking a people-focused career opportunity

  • Former sales managers with extensive industry relationships

  • Executive recruiters specializing in Industrial Water or Water Treatment talent

  • Commercial professionals from leading Industrial Water organizations who possess broad industry networks and strong market credibility

What Makes Someone Successful

The most successful candidate will not be defined by recruiting experience alone. They will be known throughout the Industrial Water industry, possess trusted relationships with top commercial performers, and have the credibility to attract talent that drives business growth.

Industry relationships are the most important qualification for this role.

jobs.description:
About Us:

Allocated Bullion Exchange (ABX)

Allocated Bullion Exchange (ABX) is the world’s leading electronic institutional exchange for allocated physical precious metals. The ABX brings global trading, price discovery, and clearing facilities into one standardised and secure online trading environment via our groundbreaking exchange trading platform, MetalDesk.

The exchange introduces a new, centrally cleared, transparent, and cost-effective allocated exchange system and standard for the industry by offering precious metal market participants an exchange where they are able to trade, deliver or store physical precious metal in 7 global locations. ABX gives market participants across the world direct access to one integrated and consolidated global wholesale bullion market. We have enhanced market efficiency, introduced inclusiveness and accessibility, and provided relevant real-time price discovery.

ABX has modernised, Globalised, & Integrated the precious metal markets by redefining the way physical bullion is traded. We connect all major global liquidity centres and break down the barriers to entry to the global wholesale market for all market participants.

About the Role:
This role will report to the Chief Compliance Officer, with a dotted line reporting to the Deputy Head of Compliance.

The successful candidate will work closely with business, technology, marketing, and legal teams to conduct compliance assessments and provide compliance and risk mitigation requirements for the organisation.

We are looking for a Deputy Senior Manager to strengthen our day-to-day compliance operations, acting as the key point of contact and escalation lead for business-as-usual (BAU) matters, while supporting the broader compliance framework.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone with a keen interest in Compliance who is looking to gain hands-on experience in a fast-paced and evolving industry.

Note: This position is open exclusively to Malaysian citizens. Applicants from other countries will be disqualified during the initial screening stage.

** Please do not apply if you do not have experience in utilising on-chain investigative tools such as Chainalysis, Elliptic, or any other such equivalent tools. Experience in using such tools is mandatory.

Key Responsibilities:

Business-as-Usual (BAU) Compliance Oversight

• Act as the overall Individual Contributor (IC) and escalation point for all BAU compliance operations.

• Make informed decisions on matters that do not require direct escalation to the CCO or Deputy Head of Compliance.
• Review and update global compliance procedures and policies to ensure compliance with regulations.

• Prioritise and manage case queues.

Payments Compliance

• Review and resolve Payments Cases, ensuring compliance with internal policies and regulatory requirements.

• Coordinate with internal teams and external partners to address payment-related compliance issues efficiently.

Monitoring and Escalations

• Manage escalations from ongoing transaction monitoring, ensuring prompt investigation and resolution.

• Evaluate and escalate Chainalysis KYT (Know-Your-Transaction) alerts and cases where blockchain analytics suggest potentially suspicious activity.

• Assist with law enforcement requests, including handling subpoenas, court orders, and official information requests in coordination with senior compliance leadership.

• Assist in managing external party requests (including banks, partners, and regulators), ensuring compliance with legal and contractual obligations.

Decision-Making and Escalation Management

• Serve as the key decision-maker for non-critical compliance escalations.

• Apply sound judgment to assess when issues must be escalated to senior leadership.

• Ensure consistency, fairness, and compliance in all decisions.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Law, Finance, Business, Compliance, or related fields.
  • 5-6 years of experience in financial services, fintech, or cryptocurrency compliance operations.
  • Experience in leading a team
  • In-depth knowledge of AML/CFT frameworks, KYC/KYB/KYT processes, blockchain analytics, and payments compliance.
  • Experience assisting with law enforcement inquiries and external partner requests is a strong advantage.
  • Ability to prioritise and manage multiple high-volume case queues.
  • Excellent analytical, communication, and decision-making skills.
  • High ethical standards and professional integrity.

What We Offer:

  • Flexible working arrangements
  • Competitive salary
  • Ongoing professional development
  • Welcoming and supportive culture
  • Diverse, global team

Como Senior Python Engineer, serás responsável pelo desenho, desenvolvimento e manutenção de serviços backend robustos e escaláveis, trabalhando com arquiteturas modernas e plataformas cloud.

  • Desenvolver e otimizar modelos de dados para aplicações escaláveis;

jobs.excerpt: What Makes Us Stand Out:Granum is the leading software company devoted to serving landscapers and arborists across North America, providing intuitive, industry-specific solutions designed to help them improve and grow their businesses while impressing their customers.
jobs.description:
What Makes Us Stand Out:

Granum is the leading software company devoted to serving landscapers and arborists across North America, providing intuitive, industry-specific solutions designed to help them improve and grow their businesses while impressing their customers. Granum brings together three of the most trusted software names in the industry — LMN, SingleOps, and Greenius — into one powerful software ecosystem. More than just a software company, Granum works alongside its clients to implement systems for estimating, scheduling, crew training, invoicing, and payments, blending technology with hands-on onboarding and human support. The company's mission is to help industry professionals unlock their potential and achieve their most important goals, all united by the belief that its clients’ success is not just a milestone, but a shared mission.

As a team, we’re on a mission to reshape an age-old industry, and we’re looking for people who thrive on challenging and meaningful work. Our environment is highly collaborative, innovative, and supportive, with a shared commitment to having fun while making an impact. We live by our core values: We Before Me, Bias to Act, The Extra 1%, Accountable to Outcomes, Unconditional Transparency, and Forgiveness. If this resonates with you, we’d love to meet you and explore how you can help us build the future of the green industry!

Our culture and growth has been recognized with multiple awards, it’s a great time to join!

  • Comparably 2024 #23/100 Best (small/ medium sized companies) Leadership Teams
  • Comparably 2024 #63/75 (small/ medium sized companies) Happiest Employees
  • #9 Atlanta Business Chronicle's 2024 Best Places to Work (Our second year in a row!)
  • #6 of Built In’s 2024 Best Places to Work: Top 50 start-ups in Atlanta (Our second year in a row!)
  • Inc Magazine’s 2023 Best Places to Work
  • Inc. 5000: #131 of 2024 Southeast Regional America’s Fastest Growing Companies. (Our third year in a row!)
  • Inc 5000 America's fastest-growing private companies (Our third year in a row!)
  • Certified Great Place to Work Canada 2024

Granum unites three trusted brands—SingleOps, LMN, and Greenius—into one powerhouse software ecosystem for landscapers and arborists across North America. We combine intuitive, industry-specific tech with hands-on partnership and real human support. The mission: help green-industry businesses improve, grow with confidence, and focus on the work that matters.

About Our Platforms
Our customers run their businesses on one (or more) of three purpose-built platforms. SingleOps helps tree care and arborist businesses save time and stay organized, from first estimate to final payment: estimating, tree mapping, scheduling, invoicing, payments, and client comms in one place. LMN helps landscape, snow, and tree care companies budget, estimate, schedule, dispatch, cost jobs, and run payroll with precision. Greenius helps crews learn the right way to do the job, with 150+ online courses that improve safety, efficiency, and retention. Depending on the territory and accounts you own, you may sell one platform, a combination, or all three. The throughline is always the same: efficient operations, empowered crews, and customers who stick around for life.

The Role
You're a hunter-first, full-cycle closer who loves the chase, the story, and the win, and who wants more than a territory. You want a hand in shaping how Granum goes to market. Instead of waiting on inbound, you engineer your own demand: you map your patch, set the attack plan, pressure-test outbound plays, and refine them as you go. You'll prospect owners and ops leaders across the green industry, run smart discovery, deliver crisp demos tied to outcomes and ROI, build real relationships, and close, partnering along the way with world-class SDRs, Sales Engineers, Marketing, and Onboarding to create a consistent, "wow" buyer experience. You operate like an entrepreneur inside Granum: you see whitespace, go after it, and pull in resources when it helps you win. This is an environment for hunters, experimenters, and owners, not caretakers.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the full cycle end-to-end: prospecting, discovery, demo, solution design, proposal, negotiation, and close. No handoffs once the opportunity lands.
  • Design and run your outbound engine: build targeted account lists, craft sequences, and run focused call blocks across outbound, inbound, events, and referrals, then keep 3–4x coverage against quota.
  • Run consultative discovery tailored to the account's pains: estimating, scheduling/dispatch, routing, job costing, payroll, invoicing, crew training, or safety and retention, and translate them into outcomes and ROI.
  • Deliver value-led, outcome-focused demos that feel like a consultative working session, not a feature walkthrough, connecting the right platform(s) to time savings, revenue lift, and better customer experiences.
  • Build and execute a territory plan; prioritize ICP accounts and multi-thread with owners, operators, and ops leaders.
  • Pilot and iterate outbound plays: test new messaging, channels, and patterns, and share what's working so we can codify and scale it.
  • Leverage AI to multiply your output: research, call prep, objection handling, follow-up writing, and post-call summaries, and help refine best practices.
  • Forecast with discipline, keep a clean house in Salesforce, and maintain impeccable pipeline hygiene.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Marketing, Product, and Sales Leadership on campaigns, field feedback, and new channels, and coordinate with Onboarding for smooth, on-time handoffs.
  • Represent Granum's partner-first approach and brand values in every interaction, and show up as the owner of your business.

What You’ll Bring

  • 2–5+ years of quota-carrying SaaS experience (SMB/mid-market) with a documented track record of new-logo wins, including meaningful self-sourced pipeline.
  • A hunter's mindset and competitive edge: you get energy from the chase, not just from managing an existing book of business.
  • Discovery chops, storytelling flair, and sharp negotiation; executive presence with owners and operators, including tough conversations on pricing and change management.
  • A builder's mentality: comfortable operating with less structure, giving feedback on what's missing, and helping shape the playbook as we grow.
  • Process discipline and CRM proficiency (Salesforce) with a modern sales toolset; you plan your week using data, not vibes.
  • Hands-on experience using AI in your workflow, for writing, research, call prep, or analysis, and hunger to do more.
  • Self-starting, coachable, and curious: you seek out feedback, act on it quickly, and go looking for the next experiment without being asked.
  • Genuine curiosity about green-industry operations and the appetite to learn domain-specific workflows quickly.

Nice to Have

  • Field service or vertical SaaS experience where deals are tied to operational workflows.
  • Direct exposure to the green industry (tree care, arboriculture, landscape, snow, PHC) or adjacent blue-collar tech.
  • Familiarity with SPICED, MEDDICC, or SPIN, and comfort running mutual action or close plans.

How We’ll Measure Success

  • New ARR and logo attainment vs. quota, with a meaningful portion sourced from your own outbound efforts.
  • Pipeline creation and coverage: self-sourced and total.
  • Stage conversion rates, sales velocity/cycle time, and forecast accuracy.
  • Demo quality and multi-threading depth in ICP accounts.
  • Clean CRM hygiene and on-time, high-quality handoffs to Onboarding.

Location and Travel

  • North America-based, flexible location. Occasional travel for industry events and customer meetings as needed (think: quality face time, not weekly flights).

Compensation:

  • Canada-based candidates: CAD 60,000 - 75,000 base + 50,000 - 60,000 OTC (commissions are uncapped)

  • US-based candidates: USD 55,000 - 65,000 base + 55,000 - 65,000 OTC (commissions are uncapped)

Reasons why you would love it here!

  • Join a team culture that’s all about collaboration, support, and having fun while making a real impact every day.
  • In the U.S., we offer comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with multiple plan options, plus additional add ons like HSA/FSA accounts, disability and life insurance, and more.
  • In Canada, we provide an employer-funded HSA-based benefits plan with drug, dental, and mental health coverage - giving you a flexible way to manage your healthcare needs.
  • We're committed to your financial future, with 401(k) matching for U.S. employees and RRSP matching for those in Canada.
  • We invest in your growth through tailored career development conversations and support for tools, courses, and resources to help you thrive.
  • And when it comes to work-life balance? We offer unlimited Paid Time Off, paid company holidays, and a company-wide winter break from December 24 to January 1 - so you can truly recharge.

Granum does not sponsor work authorization needs; candidates must have proper work authorization to work for any employer in Canada or the U.S, without sponsorship from the company.

About Us

Sophos is a cybersecurity leader defending 600,000 organizations globally with an AI-driven platform and expert-led services. Sophos meets organizations wherever they are in their security maturity and grows with them to defeat cyberattacks. Its solutions combine machine learning, automation, and real-time threat intelligence with frontline human expertise from Sophos X-Ops to deliver advanced, 24/7 threat monitoring, detection, and response.
Sophos offers industry-leading managed detection and response (MDR) alongside a comprehensive portfolio of cybersecurity technologies — including endpoint, network, email, and cloud security, extended detection and response (XDR), identity threat detection and response (ITDR), and next-gen SIEM. Together with expert advisory services, these capabilities help organizations proactively reduce risk and respond faster, with the visibility and scalability needed to stay ahead of evolving threats.
Sophos goes to market with a global partner ecosystem, including Managed Service Providers (MSPs), Managed Security Service Providers (MSSPs), resellers and distributors, marketplace integrations, and cyber risk partners, giving organizations the flexibility to choose trusted relationships when securing their business. Sophos is headquartered in Oxford, U.K. More information is available at .

Sophos is seeking a Senior Marketing Manager, Lead Lifecycle & Conversion to join our Global Growth Marketing team and own the strategy for how prospects progress through the buying journey – from initial engagement and qualification through to opportunity and revenue.

This role will bring together lifecycle strategy, nurture, buying signals, lead management and conversion optimization to create more connected, relevant experiences for Sophos prospects. Working across Growth Marketing, Marketing Operations, SDR, Sales and Revenue Operations, you will identify where prospects stall or disengage and develop programs that improve progression, conversion and pipeline outcomes.

This is not a traditional nurture marketing role. We are looking for someone who can think across the entire funnel, use data and buying signals to understand customer behaviour, and build a lifecycle strategy that turns engagement into measurable business outcomes.

What You Will Do

    Own the Lead Lifecycle

    • Own and continuously evolve Sophos' global lead lifecycle strategy, from initial engagement through MQL, SAL, opportunity and revenue.
    • Map and optimize prospect journeys across key buying stages, identifying friction, leakage and opportunities to accelerate progression.
    • Establish clear lifecycle performance metrics and use funnel data to prioritize opportunities for improvement.
    • Develop strategies for leads that are not yet sales-ready, ensuring valuable prospects continue to be developed rather than lost from the buying journey.

      • Build Intelligent Buying Journeys

      • Evolve Sophos' nurture strategy from traditional, linear programs towards dynamic journeys driven by buyer behaviour, engagement, intent and account signals.
      • Define the appropriate next-best engagement for prospects based on where they are in their buying journey.
      • Partner with Content, Product Marketing, ABX and regional teams to ensure prospects receive relevant experiences throughout the lifecycle.
      • Develop re-engagement and recycling strategies to reactivate prospects and accounts that have stalled or disengaged.

        • Drive Funnel Conversion

        • Analyze performance across the funnel to identify where prospects are progressing, stalling or dropping out.
        • Develop and test interventions designed to improve conversion, lead velocity and pipeline contribution.
        • Partner with Marketing Operations and Revenue Operations to continuously improve lifecycle stages, lead scoring, qualification, routing and recycling.
        • Build a strong feedback loop with SDR and Sales teams to understand lead quality, disposition and progression.

          • Connect Signals, ABX and Sales Engagement

          • Connect individual prospect behaviour with account-level engagement and intent signals to create a more complete view of buying readiness.
          • Partner with ABX to coordinate lead and account journeys and identify opportunities to accelerate high-intent accounts.
          • Work with SDR teams to ensure sellers receive the right leads at the right time, with the context and buying signals needed to engage effectively.
          • Identify opportunities to use AI, automation and predictive signals to improve personalization, prioritization and journey orchestration.

            • Measure & Optimize

            • Define and report against lifecycle KPIs including MQL-to-SAL conversion, SAL-to-opportunity conversion, lead velocity, recycled lead conversion, pipeline and revenue contribution.
            • Develop actionable insights that identify opportunities to improve funnel performance.
            • Establish a culture of continuous testing, learning and optimization across the prospect lifecycle.
            • Communicate lifecycle performance, insights and recommendations to Growth Marketing and GTM stakeholders.

What You Will Bring

    • 7+ years of B2B marketing experience, ideally across lifecycle marketing, demand generation, growth marketing or marketing operations.
    • Strong understanding of complex B2B buying journeys, preferably within SaaS, enterprise technology or cybersecurity.
    • Demonstrated experience developing lifecycle, nurture or demand programs that drive measurable pipeline and revenue outcomes.
    • Strong understanding of lead management, scoring, qualification, routing and recycling.
    • Experience using CRM, marketing automation and ABM/intent platforms such as Salesforce, Marketo/Eloqua and 6sense or equivalent.
    • Strong analytical capability, with experience using funnel and conversion data to identify problems and drive action.
    • Experience partnering with Sales, SDR, Marketing Operations and Revenue Operations teams.
    • Ability to influence and drive change across a complex, global organization without direct authority.
    • Commercial mindset with a strong understanding of pipeline, conversion and revenue metrics.
    • Strong communication skills with the ability to translate complex data and customer journeys into clear recommendations.
    • Hands-on experience using AI within marketing workflows, with an interest in how AI can improve journey orchestration, personalization and conversion.

Who we are

At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

The Samsara Governance, Risk, and Compliance team keeps our organization and customers safe by managing risk across our vendor and partner ecosystem. As a Third-Party Risk Management Analyst, you will own security risk assessments for critical Samsara vendors and partners. You will oversee the complete lifecycle—from tiering and onboarding to ongoing reassessments and remediation. In this role, you will partner closely with Legal, Procurement, and system owners across the business to ensure every vendor relationship meets our security standards.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
  • You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. Youwill be surrounded by a high-calibre team that will encourage you to do your best.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead end-to-end third-party security risk assessments — using both qualitative and quantitative methods — for Samsara's vendors and partners, and recommend risk ratings and tiering in line with Samsara's Vendor Risk Management Policy.
  • Own the vendor reassessment cadence and track remediation of any security gaps throughout the full lifecycle of the vendor.
  • Partner with Legal, Procurement, and system/relationship owners to review vendor contracts and onboarding requests submitted through Zip, ensuring security requirements (e.g. incident notification, data training, compliance, etc.) are in place before a vendor goes live.
  • Escalate unresolved vendor risk to Security leadership, legal, procurement, and business owners as necessary.
  • Support internal and external audits of the vendor risk program (e.g. ISO, SOC, FedRAMP).
  • Build and maintain the metrics, dashboards, and reporting that give Security leadership visibility into Samsara's third-party risk posture and program performance.
  • Support the GRC team's efforts to bring automation and AI-enabled tools into vendor risk workflows, such as using AI to triage vendor security questionnaires, flag high-risk contract terms, and incorporate industry learnings into the lifecycle.
  • Mentor junior TPRM resource(s) to ensure Samsara’s TPRM program is matching the pace of innovation and velocity of Samsara.
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 5+ years of experience in third-party/vendor risk management, GRC, or information security compliance.
  • Experience using automation, scripting, or low-code workflows to help scale a vendor risk program.
  • Hands-on experience running vendor security assessments and administering a vendor tiering program.
  • Experience partnering with Legal and Procurement on vendor contract security and privacy terms (e.g., Security addendums, DPAs, etc.).
  • Must reside in the US, outside the San Francisco Bay Area, New York City, and Washington, D.C. metro areas.

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Familiarity with implementing and/or operating a risk assessment framework such as NIST CSF, ISO 27001, or SOC 2.
  • Experience with a GRC or vendor risk management platform (e.g., Vanta, ServiceNow, OneTrust, Archer, or similar).
  • A relevant certification such as CTPRP, CISA, CRISC, or CISSP.

Please note that base pay offered may vary depending on factors including your city of residence, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual Base Salary
$110,670—$167,400 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Belonging at Samsara

The Junior Automation Security Engineer builds and supports practical automations that make security controls easier to operate, validate, and scale. This is a hands-on engineering role for a curious builder who can write clean Python, work confidently in GitHub and GitHub Actions, and learn how Terraform and AWS services fit together. The engineer will use approved internal AI tools to accelerate research, prototyping, and documentation, while developing simple, secure agents and workflow automations under senior guidance.

What You Will Do

Security Automation & Python

  • Build and maintain Python scripts, CLIs, API integrations, and scheduled jobs that reduce repetitive security and operational work.
  • Automate evidence collection, configuration checks, alert enrichment, ticket creation, reporting, and basic remediation workflows.
  • Write unit tests, logging, error handling, and concise documentation so automations are safe to operate and easy to support.

GitHub, CI/CD & Infrastructure as Code

  • Contribute to repositories using pull requests, code review, branching, issue tracking, and dependency hygiene.
  • Create and maintain GitHub Actions workflows for linting, testing, scanning, packaging, and controlled deployment tasks.
  • Read, update, and test Terraform modules and plans with guidance; help identify insecure cloud configuration patterns before release.

AWS & Cloud Security Foundations

  • Work with core AWS concepts including IAM, VPC, CloudTrail, CloudWatch, S3, Lambda, EC2, Secrets Manager, and AWS Organizations.
  • Help automate cloud inventory, access reviews, configuration validation, tagging checks, and security findings triage.
  • Follow least-privilege, secrets-management, logging, and change-control practices in all automation work.

AI-Assisted Engineering & Agents

  • Use approved internal AI coding and productivity tools responsibly for code exploration, test generation, documentation, and prototyping.
  • Practice AI-assisted or “vibe coding” in a disciplined way: validate generated code, protect confidential data, and submit reviewed changes.
  • Help develop narrowly scoped internal agents that call approved tools, retrieve permitted knowledge, and keep a human approval step for impactful actions.
  • Learn core AI security risks, including prompt injection, over-permissioned tools, data leakage, and unsafe agent behavior.

Collaboration

  • Partner with security, platform, cloud, SOC, and engineering teams to turn recurring problems into reliable automations.
  • Participate in incident follow-up, backlog refinement, peer review, and knowledge sharing.

Required Qualifications

  • Working proficiency in Python and REST APIs; able to read, debug, and improve scripts written by others.
  • Hands-on experience with Git and GitHub; familiarity with CI/CD concepts and GitHub Actions.
  • Fundamental understanding of AWS services, IAM, networking, logging, and infrastructure-as-code concepts.
  • Basic experience with Terraform or a strong willingness to learn it through real repository work.
  • Comfort learning unfamiliar tools, asking sound technical questions, and documenting work clearly.
  • Security mindset: understands the importance of least privilege, secrets handling, code review, and change control.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Security tooling, SIEM/SOAR, vulnerability management, ticketing, or cloud operations experience.
  • Exposure to container technologies, Docker, Kubernetes, or policy-as-code.
  • Experience using enterprise AI tools, LLM APIs, RAG, MCP, or agent frameworks in a controlled environment.
  • AWS Cloud Practitioner, AWS Solutions Architect Associate, Security+, or comparable learning path.

How Success Is Measured

  • Useful, tested automations reduce manual effort and are adopted by their intended teams.
  • GitHub Actions and Terraform changes are reviewed, traceable, and meet agreed security checks.
  • Cloud configuration findings are surfaced accurately and remediated efficiently.
  • AI-enabled workflows stay within approved data, access, and human-approval boundaries.

Level Expectations

  • Delivers scoped work with guidance and grows into independent ownership of well-defined automations.
  • Escalates ambiguity or risk early and uses established patterns rather than inventing unreviewed controls.
  • Builds breadth across Python, GitHub Actions, Terraform, AWS, and secure AI practices.

Job Description:

Position Summary

RMI seeks a program finance and operations lead to join our collaborative and ambitious community of operators. This role will report to a Program Finance and Operations Manager and sit within RMI’s Strategic Operations Department. You’ll spend your day-to-day embedded within a program team advancing the global energy transition. You’ll partner closely with senior staff to support effective, high-performing teams and contribute to a culture of collaboration, inclusion, and growth — enabling RMI to maximize its impact in the global effort to advance the energy transition. This role focuses on execution and coordination, with opportunities to build toward ownership and strategic influence over time

The Program Finance and Operations Lead sits at the heart of RMI programs teams, serving as a trusted connector between the program and the rest of the Institute. You’ll maintain visibility into program operations — providing analysis and insights to managers and principals on project and grant strategy and helping to translate strategy into clear, executable plans. You’ll support problem solving efforts, coordinate across teams, and contribute to continuous improvement efforts that directly impact the program.

We warmly welcome applications from individuals of all diverse backgrounds and cultures and encourage candidates who may not meet every qualification to apply.

Application Instructions: Please ensure you have read the entire job description before applying. This role requires submission of a resume and cover letter, addressing the following:

  • Why do you want to work at RMI?

  • In what ways are you qualified to contribute to RMI's mission?

Thoughtful, specific responses to these questions are an important part of our review process. Candidates who do not provide compelling answers or submit incomplete materials may not be considered.

Application Deadline: Wednesday September 9th at 11:59pm CT.

Major Roles and Responsibilities

The Program Operations Lead ensures the team they work within runs efficiently and delivers strong, mission aligned results. You’ll support operational excellence by tracking alignment across strategy, resources, and execution so that the team can focus on delivering impact. This includes tracking progress toward objectives, managing budgets, supporting internal knowledge sharing, and ensuring reporting to funders and staff is clear, compliant and consistent.

You’ll support cross-workstream coordination and knowledge sharing to help the team operate as a connected, learning organization—facilitating collaboration across workstreams and with partners to translate insight into impact.

Detailed responsibilities are listed in the following section.

Key Responsibilities:

Operating rhythm and cultural stewardship:

You will support the team’s operating rhythm — preparing materials, tracking follow-ups, and helping leadership conversations translate into coordinated action.

  • Support Program Finance and Operations Manager, managing directors and principals in maintaining operating cadence and rhythm of business, supporting alignment with business cycles

  • Facilitate internal coordination with other programs and operations on shared resources and objectives, providing frequent updates to leadership. This may include but is not limited to cross team projects and shared organizational outcomes

  • Model RMI’s values in team settings and support preparation and follow up for group discussions to ensure clarity and alignment

  • Support annual employee engagement planning and implementation efforts in coordination with program leadership

Financial management:

You will support end-to-end budgeting and financial management — coordinating budget cycles and forecasts, maintaining accurate data, and preparing routine financial updates for leaders.

  • Coordinate the development of program budgets including annual budgeting, proposal budgeting, financial reforecasting, revenue planning, expense planning, and workforce planning.

  • Provide routine updates and analysis to managing directors, principals, managers, and at times the CFO on the team’s finances

  • Coordinate independently with RMI’s Finance and Development teams to ensure program budgets and funding pipelines are accurate

  • Analyze budgeting data and prepare summaries and recommendations for principals and managers regarding fundraising, staffing and financial management

  • Track project and grant balances and flag variances or risks to leadership

Revenue Management:

You will track and analyze the funding pipeline — helping leadership anticipate risk, prioritize opportunities, and align commitments with capacity.

  • Track and report on the funding pipeline and providing timely status updates to managing directors, principals and managers on potential funding gaps and other risks

  • Support and sometimes facilitate the development of proposals and reports for donors and non-philanthropic projects (clients, governments). Includes maintaining documentation of compliance requirements and programmatic materials that will be leveraged to do so

  • Coordinate with RMI’s Development team and program staff to ensure funding pipeline opportunities are up to date in Salesforce

  • Assist with donor communications and management as needed

People:

You will support hiring, onboarding, and talent processes — ensuring materials, coordination, and data enable the team to scale effectively.

  • Support the hiring process in coordination with RMI’s People team including job postings, resume reviews, and sometimes interviews

  • Partner with program team and People team to facilitate new hire onboarding and training plans

  • Maintain and update team onboarding materials in collaboration with program and department colleagues for accuracy and effectiveness

  • Facilitate the program team in leveraging available training and learning and development opportunities

  • Facilitate and coordinate team events and retreats that strengthen connections and shared purpose

Procurement, contracting and invoicing:

You will coordinate contracts, vendors, and invoicing processes — reducing risk, ensuring compliance, and keeping projects moving without administrative drag.

  • Facilitate and aid in coordination of current contracts, creation of new contracts and relationships with current and future program contractors, including in-country team members

  • Support contract review process to ensure alignment with RMI operational and financial best practice

  • Partner with Accounts Receivable or Accounts Payable in reviewing invoices and aligning invoicing terms and invoicing process for both providers and clients

  • Work with the Program Assistant to ensure vendor and supplier bills are submitted correctly and in a timely manner. Work with project managers to do the same for client invoices

  • Coordinate procurement processes for the program in collaboration with RMI’s procurement office

  • Support the Program Assistant in the submission monthly international employee expense invoices

Project management:

You will maintain project systems and reporting — maintaining accurate structures, surfacing performance insights, and giving leaders visibility into progress and constraints.

  • Maintain project data in RMI’s systems and support project managers in creating new projects when needed

  • Provide consultative support to Project Managers in reviewing and approving timesheets and expense reports for the program

  • Track RMI-standard performance indicators and prepare summaries for program leadership review

  • Maintain the program’s SharePoint homepages and file system, including compliance with non-disclosure agreements and clauses

Internal RMI coordination:

You will support coordination between the program and central teams — communicating program needs, maintaining documentation, and contributing to RMI-wide standards.

  • Support coordination between program teams and RMI’s cross-functional departments, elevating questions and needs as appropriate.

  • Contribute to RMI-wide process improvement efforts and participate in centrally led initiatives as assigned

  • Monitor compliance with RMI policies and escalate inconsistencies or misunderstandings to managers or program leadership.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 3-6 years of experience in operations, finance, consulting or related analytical roles in for-profit or nonprofit environments

  • Organizational skills required for successful operations of 50 person teams and complicated funding compliance

  • Experience supporting senior leadership with analysis, reporting and operational coordination

  • Outstanding analytical skills

  • Experience contributing to operational change in fast-growing organization

  • Ability to communicate with and manage diverse stakeholder groups within a remote or distributed environment, fostering clarity and trust

Location

We are a remote-ready company with team members around the globe. Our beautiful and welcoming offices are available for meetings or focused work, whether you are traveling through or living nearby. Our U.S. offices are in New York City; Washington DC; Oakland, California; Boulder, Colorado, and Basalt, Colorado. This role can be located from anywhere in the continental United States.

We provide you with the essential IT equipment plus a one-time home technology payment and a monthly work from home/commuter allowance to ensure you have a comfortable home office set up and necessary supplies.

We value opportunities to connect in person. We occasionally gather for shared time together like retreats and learning experiences. Be prepared to travel for occasional in-person meetings; all travel costs are covered. Some roles may require more travel, which will be discussed during the hiring process.

Compensation

At RMI, we prioritize fairness in our pay practices. Salaries are determined based on a mix of experience and market benchmarks. The salary range of this position is $77,732 - $95,800. The expectation is not for new team members to be hired with a starting salary at the top of the band, but to have a salary that adequately compensates for experience and expertise while countering pay inequality and upholding internal parity. In addition to base salary, this position includes an annual bonus target of 5% and eligibility for merit-based increases, which are tied to both individual and organizational performance. This role may be hired at multiple levels.

Benefits

  • We offer an array of benefits including:

  • Medical, dental, vision insurance

  • 403b retirement match with immediate vesting

  • Group life, AD&D, and short- and long-term disability

  • Optional voluntary life, AD&D and accident plans

  • Health savings or flexible spending accounts

  • Fertility and hormonal health support

  • Mental health and wellness support

  • Comprehensive leaves of absence (including generous parental leave)

  • Generous paid time off and sick leave

  • Paid sabbatical leave

  • Regional holidays with at least one extended break in each geography

  • Work from home and home technology allowances

  • Learning & development opportunities (LinkedIn Learning and an annual individual professional development budget)

  • Potential for bonuses and merit increases

  • Discount marketplace (gym memberships, pet insurance, etc.)

  • Hybrid / remote work options

  • Team retreats and geographic meetups

  • Rewards and recognition programs

Diversity

We know that the diversity of our teams makes us stronger as an organization, and RMI is dedicated to the principles of equal employment opportunity as outlined in U.S. federal law. We prohibit discrimination against applicants, interns, and employees on the basis of any legally recognized basis, including but not limited to: age (40 and over), race, color, sex, pregnancy (including lactation, childbirth, or related medical conditions), religion, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, genetic information (including testing and characteristics), sexual orientation, gender expression/identity, uniformed service member status, veteran status, citizenship status, or any other applicable status protected by applicable law.

We are a female-founded scale-up, currently made up of around 100 AltoVitians. Our fully-remote team hails from 26 different countries and collectively speaks 29 languages. Today is a particularly exciting time to join our team, we closed our Series A financing round in late 2022 and will be starting the Series B rounds in the coming year. This next chapter won’t always be a smooth ride, but it will be filled with innovation, excitement and opportunities, so if you are ready for the challenge (and the fun!) of growing with us, we would love to hear from you.

AltoVita is a multi-award winning accommodation platform that enables enterprises to consolidate accommodation programmes through the power of proprietary technology paired with a human centric approach.

AltoVita’s unique offering sets us apart in the market, providing a network of 10 million+ verified and vetted properties are all duty of care compliant, backed by a four-tier quality control process; located in over 35,000 cities & 165 countries world-wide. With our award-winning enterprise software and human-centric approach, we deliver smart and sustainable solutions to global talent mobility & business travel managers worldwide.

Our Client Development team plays a vital role as trusted advisors and partners to our clients. Embodying our consultative philosophy, this dedicated team proactively shares new market insights, analyzes data, and empowers our clients with the tools and knowledge to make informed decisions, ensuring our clients are always equipped to make the best choices for their corporate housing needs.

  • Frequent travel (North America + LATAM)

AltoVita is a fully remote team. Although we have regular touch-points throughout the week, organise off-sites in several locations, trust is essential for us to work effectively as a team. Our founders empower us to make decisions autonomously, and in turn expect that we also empower our direct reports.

jobs.title: Manager, Data and Analytics

jobs.description:
KIPP Foundation’s Analytics team supports the use, analysis, presentation, and application of high-quality data and research regarding KIPP schools, teachers, students, and families. These data enable KIPP to drive improvement in results, monitor progress toward outcomes and leading indicators, and inform learning and storytelling. The Analytics team supports a network of high-performing schools by providing key stakeholders with data needed for constant learning, decision-making, marketing, and development. The ideal Manager, Data & Analytics is a storyteller, highly detailed and process-oriented, and is always trying to find ways to improve existing processes, analyses, and products. In addition, this team member is a strong communicator, relationship-builder, and proactive self-starter who centers equity in their work and relationships. 

The Analytics team is hiring 3 Manager to focus primarily on one of these areas: (1) K-8 academic initiatives, (2) High school and postsecondary education, or (3) Talent and leadership development.

This position reports directly to the Director, Data & Analytics, and collaborates with teammates within the Data & Technology team, and other program teams in the KIPP Foundation and KIPP Network.

Responsibilities

The Manager, Data & Analytics responsibilities include, but not limited to, the following:

  • Support the design and execution of reporting and analysis (40%)

  • Cleaning, compile, and analyze data across content areas to support reporting and analysis

  • Support the design, implementation, and maintenance of reports, dashboards, and other products to make data accessible and understandable to KIPP Foundation and network stakeholders

  • Generate actionable insights for key stakeholders and communicate results in a variety of formats, including memos and written, visual, and verbal presentations

  • Serve as a thought partner to the KF program teams to identify

  • Support data collection, quality assurance, verification, and systems initiatives (40%)

  • Support annual data collection, quality assurance, and verification processes to ensure on-time collection, processing, and delivery of high-quality data to KIPP Foundation and network stakeholders

  • Support the development of business, functional, and technical requirements to support data collection, quality assurance, and verification processes and data warehousing

  • Support day-to-day activities of the Data & Analytics team (20%)

  • Support KIPP Foundation, regions, schools, and community members with data needs, including grant submissions, secondary research, and ad-hoc data requests

  • Support with planning and execution for annual, network-facing events, including network retreats

  • Support with planning, facilitating, and contributing to D&A team culture and equity development

Skills and Mindsets

  • Mission and Student Focus: Demonstrates passion and commitment to KIPP’s mission and possesses the desire and ability to uphold KIPP’s core values (Focus on Excellent Results, Collective Impact, and Courageous Action).

  • Self Management: Demonstrated record of co-creating ambitious goals with their managers – and driving toward desired outcomes; Effectively monitors progress toward goals for multiple workstreams; Leverages understanding of an organization’s operating model, structure, and core operational process to effectively drive work to achieve goals; effectively works through direct reports and peers to follow through on commitments, ensuring others do the same. 

  • Work Management: Effectively drives work they own through clear action planning. Manages time effectively around competing priorities. Skilled in creating and executing project plans through partnership with stakeholders and effective delegation to achieve intended results on time. Skilled in knowledge management.   

  • Problem Solving: Generates solutions outside of their direct work and shrinks problems to solve independently. Shows initiative in generating and recommending ideas and solutions within their own workstreams. Anticipates risks and develops proactive solutions that support their team.

  • Collaboration: Leads successful stakeholder management, accounting for varied perspectives when gathering feedback. Builds coalition by prioritizing end-user experiences. Builds trusting relationships and effective communications. Able to identify and remove barriers to working across teams..

  • Continuous Learning: Engages in the work of personal development at work, knowing that personal development is ongoing and vital to their personal and professional success; hold themself accountable to evolving, growing, learning, and unlearning in ways that improve results for students, adults, and the larger community.

  • Data-Driven Actions and Decisions: Effectively uses data to inform work streams; accurately synthesizes key findings from data analyses and can effectively communicate the data synthesis to inform actions, decisions, and solutions.

Experience and Qualifications

  • Minimum of 2 years of experience in a role focused on quantitative reporting and analysis, data management, and quality assurance

  • Experience with SQL or other programming languages/statistical software (e.g., Python, R, SAS, Stata)

  • Experience developing dashboards and data visualizations using BI tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI, Looker)

  • Excellent written and oral communication skills with an ability to present data and findings in various accessible formats for non-technical audiences

  • A customer service mindset with a goal to assist program teams with their data needs

  • Familiarity with data quality assurance processes

  • Bachelor's degree in data science, Statistics, Information Technology, Social Sciences, or a similar discipline; advanced degree is a plus but not required

  • Deep commitment to both racial and educational equity: supports building an organization that reflects the community that KIPP serves and holds self and others on team accountable for centering equity

Preferred:

  • Experience working in a K-12 and/or higher education setting

  • Experience with statistical methods

  • Experience with the following (or similar) technologies: Salesforce, Jira, Zendesk

Work Conditions

  • Travel: up to 5% (up to 10 days per year)

  • Full, exempt role

Location

It is preferred, but not mandatory for this role to be based out of a KIPP Foundation office. This role has the option of working from a remote office full-time. KIPP Foundation offices are in NYC and Chicago.

Compensation and Benefits

In compliance with local law, we are disclosing the compensation, or a range thereof, for roles in locations where legally required. Actual salaries will vary based on several factors, including but not limited to external market data, internal equity, and relevant experience. The salary range for this position is $$83,200-99,000. In addition, KIPP Foundation provides a variety of benefits to employees, including: 

  • 25 holidays for + 18 days additional flexible PTO days (flexible PTO increases to 23 days for years 3 and 4 and to 28 days for years 5+).

  • 100% paid parental leave

  • 100% coverage of the premium for employee and 75% for employee + family’s medical/dental/vision plans.

  • Wellness benefits such as fitness reimbursements, discounted tickets to theme parks/attractions, backup care support for children and adults/elders, and our employee assistance program

  • Finance Security benefits include such as a 401K retirement plan with 4% match, employer-sponsored legal plans, life/disability insurance, and flexible spending accounts

KIPP Foundation embraces the opportunity to build a workforce that reflects the diversity of the students and communities with whom we work and the world that’s around them. Being an equal opportunity employer means that we take seriously our responsibility to consider qualified candidates on the basis of merit, without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, mental or physical disability, and genetic information, marital status, citizenship status, military status, protected veteran status or any other category protected by law.

About the Organization

KIPP Public Schools is a national network of tuition-free public charter schools that prepares students with the skills and confidence to create the future they want for themselves, their communities, and us all. We are a network of 279 schools, nearly 16,500 educators, and nearly 210,000 students and alumni.

Our mission: Together with families and communities, we create joyful, academically excellent schools that prepare students with the skills and confidence to pursue the paths they choose—college, career, and beyond—so they can lead fulfilling lives and build a more just world.

Our vision: Every child grows up free to create the future they want for themselves and their communities.

The KIPP Foundation is a nonprofit organization that supports KIPP public charter schools across the country. The KIPP Foundation helps to develop outstanding educators to lead KIPP schools; provides tools and resources for excellent teaching and learning; promotes innovation; and facilitates the exchange of insights and ideas across KIPP and other public schools and organizations.

About Our Values:

Excellent Results for Students: We value results over effort and know that our work is not finished until all students thrive. We maintain high expectations for self, team, and students. We drive outcomes by operating with agility, removing barriers, differentiating support, and prioritizing student-centered solutions—especially for those at the margins.

Collective Impact: We are one team. We win together. We embody a one-team mindset by working collaboratively across teams, aligning goals, and leveraging the strengths of all teammates. We build trust-based relationships and ensure inclusive decision-making by engaging those closest to the work. We provide clarity through simple, repeatable systems and goals that enable transformational outcomes.

Courageous Action: Our belief in what we can achieve is unwavering, fueling our optimism and commitment to overcome any challenge. We demonstrate an unwavering belief in students' potential and a commitment to addressing systemic inequities. We approach challenges with resilience, a solutions-focused mindset, and adaptability. We foster a psychologically safe environment centered on trust and accountability where feedback is encouraged. We leverage data to reflect on progress, own setbacks, celebrate successes, and continuously improve to maximize impact.
