jobs.description:
About Menlo

Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it. Our mission is to make humanoid labor economically viable, turning software into physical labor at scale. We build across the full stack: hardware architecture, locomotion, autonomy, simulation, and infrastructure. We move fast, ship to real robots, and open-source everything we can. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place.

The Role

We are looking for a Researcher, Locomotion to push Asimov from walking to running, recovering, and moving through the real world with the confidence of something alive. Asimov 0 was built to learn locomotion and Asimov 1 to learn whole-body control, and you will own the policies that make that motion robust on real hardware. You will not stop at a clip in simulation. You will get your work onto a physical biped and keep pushing until it holds up under contact, disturbance, and terrain we did not train for.

What You'll Do

  • Design, train, and ship reinforcement learning policies for bipedal and whole-body locomotion on Asimov

  • Own the sim2real pipeline end to end, building on our zero-shot sim2real work so a first run on hardware is never really a first run

  • Push balance, gait, and recovery behavior past the demo stage into something that survives pushes, slips, and uneven ground

  • Build and refine reward design, domain randomization, and training environments in MuJoCo

  • Close the loop between simulation and hardware with real telemetry from real robots, then feed what breaks back into the next policy

  • Work shoulder to shoulder with hardware, controls, and manipulation researchers, since whole-body control does not respect team boundaries

  • Open-source what you can and write up what you learn so the community can build on it

What We Look For

  • Deep hands-on experience with reinforcement learning for continuous control, legged locomotion, or whole-body control

  • A track record of getting learned policies onto real robots, not only into papers or simulators

  • Strong command of a physics simulator such as MuJoCo, Isaac, or similar, including reward shaping and domain randomization

  • Fluency in Python and modern RL tooling, and comfort in a ROS2-based control stack

  • A bias for shipping: you would rather see a policy stumble on real hardware this week than look perfect in sim next month

  • Clear thinking about why a policy fails, not just whether it does

Nice to Have

  • Published work in locomotion, legged robotics, or sim2real transfer

  • Experience with model predictive control or classical locomotion methods alongside learning-based approaches

  • Contributions to open-source robotics or RL projects

  • Experience bringing up new hardware and debugging the messy gap between a model and a motor

Why Join Menlo

You will own locomotion for a humanoid that thousands of developers are building on in the open. Your policies will ship to real robots, not slides, and the community will see them walk. If you want your research to leave the lab and stand up on its own two feet, this is the place.

A Note on AI

You don't need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect everyone at Menlo to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement. When that's the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don't treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.

Equal Opportunity and Accommodations

We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you're excited about a role but don't meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. Menlo Research is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristic. Menlo provides reasonable accommodations during the application process. If you need one, please let your recruiter know.

jobs.excerpt: Company OverviewWestaim and CC Capital have joined forces to strategically transform Westaim from a holding company into a global alternative credit asset manager with a unique, integrated insurance platform, branded as The Westaim Corporation.
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Westaim and CC Capital have joined forces to strategically transform Westaim from a holding company into a global alternative credit asset manager with a unique, integrated insurance platform, branded as The Westaim Corporation. This partnership supports a long-term vision to deliver innovative, customized financial solutions across alternative credit and insurance, creating scalable growth and meaningful client impact.

Ceres USA Holdings, LLC, part of the insurance platform within The Westaim Corporation strategy, is the parent company of Ceres Life Insurance—a fast-growing, technology-driven annuity carrier startup. Ceres is focused on redefining retirement security by combining modern technology, top-tier talent, and strategic partnerships to deliver exceptional annuity solutions and advisor experiences.

Ceres is committed to a client-centered culture that leverages innovation, AI, and digital marketing to strengthen brand awareness, advisor engagement, and customer experience.

Position Summary

The Head of Internal Controls is responsible for designing, implementing, and continuously enhancing Ceres Life's enterprise-wide internal control framework. As the organization continues to grow, this role will establish scalable financial and operational controls that protect company assets, strengthen governance, support regulatory compliance, and improve business processes across the organization.

Working closely with Finance, Operations, Technology, Compliance, Legal, and executive leadership, the Head of Internal Controls proactively evaluates business processes, identifies control gaps, develops remediation plans, and drives a culture of accountability and operational excellence. This role serves as the organization's subject matter expert on internal controls and provides independent oversight to ensure risks are appropriately identified and mitigated while enabling efficient business operations.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Internal Controls

  • Develop, implement, and maintain the enterprise internal control framework aligned with company strategy, regulatory expectations, and industry best practices.
  • Establish standardized control methodologies, documentation standards, and governance processes across all business functions.
  • Create and maintain enterprise-wide risk and control matrices (RCMs), process narratives, and control documentation.
  • Continuously evaluate the effectiveness of financial, operational, and technology controls and recommend enhancements.

Financial & Operational Controls

  • Design preventive and detective controls supporting accounting, treasury, investments, operations, technology, and corporate functions.
  • Partner with Finance leadership to strengthen financial reporting controls and accounting processes.
  • Evaluate business processes to improve efficiency while maintaining appropriate control standards.
  • Lead control redesign initiatives as new products, systems, and business capabilities are introduced.

Risk Assessment & Control Monitoring

  • Perform enterprise control risk assessments across critical business functions.
  • Develop monitoring programs to assess ongoing control effectiveness.
  • Track control deficiencies and oversee timely remediation efforts.
  • Report key control metrics, trends, and emerging risks to executive leadership.

Audit & Regulatory Support

  • Serve as the primary liaison for internal and external auditors on internal control matters.
  • Coordinate audit responses, documentation requests, and remediation activities.
  • Ensure the organization remains prepared for regulatory examinations and compliance reviews.
  • Monitor evolving regulatory expectations affecting the insurance industry and recommend control enhancements accordingly.

Process Improvement

  • Partner with business leaders to identify opportunities for automation, standardization, and process improvement.
  • Evaluate new business initiatives, systems implementations, and operational changes to ensure appropriate controls are incorporated from inception.
  • Promote continuous improvement through scalable control design and operational efficiencies.

Policy & Documentation

  • Develop and maintain internal control policies, procedures, and governance documentation.
  • Establish documentation standards supporting consistency across departments.
  • Ensure policies remain current with organizational growth and regulatory expectations.

Leadership & Collaboration

  • Build strong relationships across Finance, Operations, Compliance, Legal, Technology, and executive leadership.
  • Provide guidance and education on internal control principles and accountability.
  • Foster a culture of ownership, transparency, and continuous improvement.
  • Lead future growth of the Internal Controls function as the organization expands.

Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Risk Management, or a related field required.
  • Master's degree or MBA preferred.

Experience

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in internal controls, internal audit, accounting, enterprise risk, or financial governance.
  • Experience within life insurance, annuities, financial services, banking, or other regulated financial institutions strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and implementing enterprise internal control frameworks.
  • Experience supporting external audits, regulatory examinations, and complex financial environments.
  • Experience working in high-growth organizations is highly desirable.

Preferred Certifications

  • CPA
  • CIA
  • CISA
  • CRMA
  • Other relevant governance, audit, or risk management certifications

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Deep knowledge of COSO Internal Control Framework and enterprise control best practices.
  • Strong understanding of financial reporting, operational risk, and regulatory compliance.
  • Experience with risk and control assessments, process documentation, and remediation planning.
  • Ability to influence executive leadership and drive cross-functional initiatives.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Proven ability to balance strong governance with business agility.
  • High level of integrity, professionalism, and sound judgment.
  • Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and experience with governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) tools is preferred.

Why Join Us?

  • Be part of a fast-growing, technology-driven insurance company transforming the future of retirement and annuity solutions.
  • Work in a collaborative, entrepreneurial environment where innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement are valued.
  • Make a meaningful impact by helping build and scale a modern insurance platform that delivers exceptional advisor and client experiences.
  • Collaborate with talented professionals across the organization while leveraging technology, digital tools, and innovative solutions to drive business success.
  • Enjoy a competitive compensation package, comprehensive health benefits, paid time off, and opportunities for professional growth and career advancement.
Salary: 250,000-290,000

jobs.excerpt: About Generation:At Generation, we believe in the power of employment to change lives.
jobs.description:
About Generation:

At Generation, we believe in the power of employment to change lives. We are a global nonprofit organization that supports adults to achieve economic mobility through employment. Generation trains and places adult learners of all ages into careers that are otherwise inaccessible, working in partnership with governments, employers, and other system actors. We also conduct original research and share data insights on high-priority global workforce transition topics to inform decision-making by workforce system stakeholders. Launched in 2015, Generation comprises a global hub (Generation You Employed, or GYE) and a network of in-country affiliates. To date, the network has 150,000+ graduates and 23,000+ employers across 50 professions and 17 countries.

When learners join Generation, 91% are unemployed, of which nearly half are long-term unemployed. Three months after completing our program, graduates have an 78% job placement rate, rising to 88% within six months. Of our employed graduates, 79% are hired by repeat employers who have previously hired Generation graduates, and 89% are in jobs directly related to the profession for which we have trained them. Employed graduates immediately earn an average of 3-4X their previous earnings. Two to five years after graduation, 77% of our alumni from upper-middle income countries continue to meet their daily financial needs and 63% can save for the future. To date, Generation’s global graduates have earned more than $1.9 billion in wages. Generation graduates typically have a secondary school background, 52% are female, 28% have dependents, and the majority identify with underrepresented communities in their country.

About the role:

  • Location requirements: Remote (with reliable WiFi), based in Colombia, with availability to travel within Colombia and attend in-person events with employers and partners
  • Start date: September 2026
  • End date: August 2027
  • Type contract: 12-month fixed term contract

What you’ll do:

The Curriculum & Instruction (C&I) Coordinator ensures program readiness, supports the selection of instructional teams, and delivers onboarding and upskilling support for instructors and mentors to enable effective and high-quality training execution for Generation Colombia. This role also oversee curriculum adjustments as programs are implemented.

1) Staffing & Selection

  • Execute instructor selection activities by supporting screening profiles, coordinating interviews, and documenting selection outcomes.
  • Deliver instructional team readiness activities in collaboration with the C&I global team, including completing required onboarding steps for instructors and mentors.
  • Execute instructor onboarding and upskilling activities by facilitating onboarding sessions, sharing training materials, and supporting instructors in developing the capabilities required to deliver Generation’s online curriculum.

2) Curriculum, learning & teaching operations

  • Support the implementation of the Learning and Teaching vision, reflecting it in all stakeholder interactions, priorities and processes.
  • Conduct day-to-day program delivery in collaboration with the Program Coordinators, and serve as the point of escalation for learner issues during training according to established protocols (e.g., attendance, punctuality, engagement, assessment/learning outcomes, professionalism), and work with instructors and mentors to problem-solve learner issues, escalating them as needed to the Program & Operations Lead.
  • Support cohort-level program execution by maintaining regular communication with instructors, mentors, learners, and internal stakeholders to track progress toward course completion, learning outcomes, and job readiness targets.
  • Execute curriculum readiness activities by supporting curriculum updates, validating materials, and completing instructional readiness checks prior to cohort launch
  • Support the Global C&I Team in implementing new resources and providing feedback on existing tools and curriculum resources.
  • Track and document TSP performance against contractual, academic, and operational KPIs, producing regular performance summaries.
  • Validate TSP compliance with agreed curriculum delivery standards, schedules, and reporting requirements through structured reviews.
  • Execute regular performance review check-ins with TSP teams to assess progress, identify risks, review instructional quality, and document instructor performance.
  • Identify and escalate TSP-related risks and performance gaps by documenting issues and supporting the definition of corrective action plans.
  • Execute classroom observation and academic review activities by scheduling sessions, collecting evidence, and documenting feedback and findings with the TSP.
  • Validate alignment with Generation’s learner success standards by reviewing TSP instructional practices and documenting gaps and improvement opportunities.

3) knowledge and data collection

  • Set up and maintain program data tracking mechanisms in collaboration with the Program Coordinator to collect and analyze data to ensure instructors and learners are being supported in a timely manner
  • Facilitate structured program reflection sessions by preparing inputs, capturing insights, and documenting agreed improvement actions
  • Support the use and frequent updates of the learner management system by completing data updates in line with standard operating procedures and agreed reporting cadence, in collaboration with the Program Coordinators.
  • Document and share instructional best practices by compiling materials and distributing insights with country and global teams.

4) Ongoing support and professional development

  • Design and execute instructor professional development activities of all Generation programs to help them improve the delivery of the Generation methodology and instructional practice
  • Collect, analyze, and document instructor onboarding and training data before, during, and after delivery to identify lessons learned and define additional support needs for instructors.
  • Facilitate instructor communities of practice and structured reflection sessions by organizing sessions, preparing materials, and documenting key insights to support continuous learning.

About You:

  • Bachelor's degree in any field with a solid academic record.
  • 3-5 years of work experience leading and managing education-related programs, desirable if has some teaching experience in online environments
  • Experience managing relationships and communicating with diverse stakeholders, such as training delivery partners, donors, or employers
  • Interest or experience in providing coaching or professional development to adults and/or instructors to meet targeted goals for performance
  • Experience in using a Learner Management System (LMS) or equivalent and analyzing the data to draw conclusions and plan strategically
  • Professional demeanor, excellent organizational and interpersonal skills
  • Strong communication skills, feedback-oriented, and showing a coach-growth mindset. (Intermediate English level)
  • High degree of independence with the ability to also be a team player
  • Entrepreneurial, creative, solutions-oriented, and proactive mindset required. Experience in a start-up environment is preferred
  • Ideal candidates will have experience working with educational institutions, and/or have knowledge of current trends in adult learning and the players in the skills training landscape in Colombia
  • Passionate about providing educational opportunities that empower others to enter a life-changing professional career. Believes in the potential of the participants in Generation Colombia programs and keeps their needs front and centre.
  • The candidate should be open to traveling to Generation sites as per the needs of the program

***Please apply with your English resume, thank you***

jobs.title: Product Manager, Core Experience
jobs.excerpt: In just five years, Stora has become the platform behind more than 30% of UK self storage locations, and we're scaling globally from here.
jobs.description:
In just five years, Stora has become the platform behind more than 30% of UK self storage locations, and we're scaling globally from here. Operators have processed over £150m in automated payments through us, and see an average of 32% business growth after they switch.

We're doing this in a market that's wide open. Europe has over 10,000 self storage sites and is growing fast, yet it sits years behind the US on maturity and is still barely touched by good software. The UK is our stronghold. The rest of Europe is where we're heading next.

Stora is the operating system for modern self storage: online bookings, payments, facility management, reporting, and automation in one platform. We started as operators ourselves, and that's still how we think. If you want to own a product operators depend on every day, in a company genuinely rethinking how it builds, this is it.

Why this role matters

We have a strong product team, great engineers, and a growing product. The bottleneck isn't ideas or execution capacity. It's people who can hold the full picture at once.

What the business needs, what the customer actually experiences, what's technically feasible, what to cut when time is short, and knowing when to slow down. Making good calls across all of it. That's the job.

We've shortened the loop between insight and shipped product by stripping out the layers that slow good judgement down. The quality bar didn't move. This role exists to keep doing that. It carries real ownership from day one, and the scope grows as Stora does.

The surface you'd own

This is the product operators live in every day, and the storefront their own customers book through. You're designing for two users at once: the operator running the business, and the end customer renting the unit. Getting that B2B2C experience right is a genuine craft problem. It's a broad, central surface, and it's heavy on UX.

Concretely, the surface includes:

  • Core workflows: customers, units, tenancies, access

  • Roles, permissions, account structure

  • Operational reporting: occupancy, utilisation, activity

  • The internal data layer: event tracking, core models, metric definitions

  • The growth surface: storefront, checkout, the lead → booking funnel

If an operator uses it daily, or relies on it to understand their business, it sits with this team.

How we actually work

We've changed how product gets built at Stora. This is how we operate now.

Designers work directly in the codebase. Engineers and product people work closely together from the start. We use AI genuinely: to explore, prototype and move faster. The work gets closer to reality, sooner.

If you're at a company that talks about moving faster but runs the same process it did three years ago, this will feel different. We're not done evolving how we work, and this person will have real scope to shape that.

What you'll do

  • Own a problem space end-to-end, from understanding the customer need to something live in the product

  • Work across both sides of the experience: operator back office and end-customer storefront

  • Work directly with engineering leads. Close collaboration, not handoff

  • Make scope calls. Know what to cut, what's fundamental, what can wait

  • Work with or without a designer, depending on the problem. What matters is the outcome

  • Stay close to customers, talk to operators, understand how they run their businesses, bring that into every decision

  • Shape how we work. The process isn't fixed. If something's slowing things down, fix it

What you'll bring

  • Real product experience at a SaaS company. You've owned features or problem spaces end-to-end and shipped things people use. Roughly 2+ years, though we care more about the evidence than the number

  • A builder by instinct. You make things: side projects, tools, a company you tried to start. We'd rather see someone who ships than someone who only plans

  • A design or engineering past works too. You may have come from design, engineering, or somewhere else entirely. Designers and people who've started their own things tend to do well here

  • Great product taste. You can tell the difference between a solution that works and one that just ships

  • You define it yourself. You don't need everything defined to make progress

  • Real design sense. Strong enough to contribute or push back, which matters a lot on a surface this UX-heavy

  • AI-native. You use AI as a natural part of how you think and work. Not waiting to be shown how

This role is not for you if

  • You need a detailed brief before you can start

  • You've only ever worked inside someone else's process and haven't shipped anything of your own

  • You think good product work stops before it ships

  • You go quiet when a problem is ambiguous instead of pushing into it

Why Stora

  • A category-defining surface to own. Self storage software is wide open, and the core experience is the heart of it. You set the direction here, you don't inherit it.

  • Work that ships, and that you feel. We've stripped out the layers between insight and shipped product. What you build reaches operators in weeks, not quarters.

  • A team that builds differently. Designers in the codebase, AI used for real, process that bends when it should. Small team, outsized impact.

What we offer

  • Competitive salary

  • Share options

  • Remote across the UK & Europe, or hybrid from our Belfast office

  • 35 days holiday

  • Private health insurance (for you + family)

  • Company pension plan

  • Apple hardware

  • Learning & development support

Next steps

When you apply, we'll ask for a link to something you've made — a product, a side project, a repo, a tool you built because something annoyed you. It doesn't need to be polished, successful, or related to storage. We just want to see that you build. Please include one.

We're reviewing applications as they come in and will be in touch quickly if it looks like a match.

jobs.title: Director of Revenue Strategy & Growth
jobs.excerpt: A Snapshot of Curvion Blue:Curvion is a high performance RevOps & sales augmentation agency that installs and deploys enterprise-grade, AI-driven revenue engines and selling systems for our clients.
jobs.description:
A Snapshot of Curvion Blue:

Curvion is a high performance RevOps & sales augmentation agency that installs and deploys enterprise-grade, AI-driven revenue engines and selling systems for our clients. Think of a lead generation based marketing agency…. But focused on sales! We design and install complete sales systems from sales processes and GTM strategy to CRM setup all the way to fully outsourced sales engagements. Then we enhance those systems with AI enabled tools and battle tested playbooks, and finally, we provide highly trained sales talent to help our clients execute so their revenue engine runs faster, scales efficiently, and performs consistently. In short, we build and power modern, AI-driven sales systems that help companies grow with clarity and control.

Position Overview

What exactly is a Director of Revenue Strategy & Growth? In simple terms, think of an exceptionally strong B2B seller and revenue strategist who understands that describing themselves simply as a "salesperson" would significantly undersell their capabilities.

We are building an entirely new B2B revenue line at Curvion, and we are looking for someone capable of helping build it from the ground up and ultimately growing into the executive responsible for leading it.

This person will initially have three primary responsibilities: acquire high-value B2B accounts, lead the Revenue Architecture and strategy work we sell to those clients, and help architect the sales and revenue function required to scale the division.

Our flagship entry point into B2B is the Curvion Blue-Print, an initial consulting and Revenue Architecture engagement designed to help companies establish the foundation required to scale a sophisticated revenue function.

The work spans seven interconnected areas: Revenue Planning & Economics, GTM & Deal Flow Architecture, Sales Role Architecture, Sales Enablement, RevOps & Technology, Recruiting, and Sales Management & Performance. We diagnose what exists, determine what needs to change, design the future-state revenue architecture, and help clients build the infrastructure required to execute it.

Because of this, we aren't looking for a traditional Account Executive who simply knows how to run discovery, demo a predefined solution, and close.

We need someone who understands the subject matter deeply enough to sell through expertise.

You should be capable of sitting across from a founder or CEO, understanding their business model, asking sophisticated questions about their revenue organization, identifying problems they may not see themselves, and developing a strategic point of view about what needs to change. After closing the engagement, you should be excited to roll up your sleeves and help lead the actual strategy work.

You do not need to have been a CRO before.

You may come from enterprise sales, business development, revenue consulting, GTM strategy, RevOps, sales leadership, or another combination of experiences that has given you unusually broad exposure to how B2B revenue organizations actually work.

What matters is that you have the commercial ability to sell it, the strategic horsepower to deliver it, and the leadership potential to eventually build a department around it.

For the right person, this role has a significantly larger destination. As the B2B division scales, we want this individual to build the team around themselves, take increasing ownership of the revenue function, and have the opportunity to grow into Curvion's senior revenue leader. If you are looking for your next AE, individual contributor role this is NOT for you. However if you are looking to leverage your selling capabilities, and are looking for a great opportunity to grow into a revenue leader position where you lead our revenue architecture service along with the team that sells it, then this is worth a conversation.

You SHOULD Apply to This Role If:

  • You have a track record of selling sophisticated, high-value B2B solutions, services, or consulting engagements and are comfortable navigating complex sales cycles with founders and executives.

  • Your strongest sales conversations feel more like strategic consulting than pitching. You naturally diagnose the business, identify gaps, challenge assumptions, and help prospects understand what needs to change.

  • You understand how B2B companies generate revenue beyond simply "getting more leads" and can think across acquisition, conversion, sales capacity, economics, people, process, technology, and performance.

  • You understand revenue planning and can reason through targets, pipeline requirements, conversion rates, sales capacity, headcount, CAC, payback, and the economics underlying a growth plan.

  • You understand how to evaluate GTM strategy, ICPs, channels, funnels, sales motions, pipeline structure, and the path from opportunity creation to closed revenue.

  • You understand how sales organizations should be structured and can think intelligently about roles, compensation, KPIs, expectations, capacity, hiring profiles, and management structure.

  • You have meaningful exposure to sales enablement, including sales process, methodology, talk tracks, playbooks, onboarding, training, and rep development.

  • You understand RevOps and modern revenue technology well enough to participate in sophisticated conversations around CRM architecture, reporting, automation, workflows, data, integrations, and AI.

  • You understand the fundamentals of recruiting, ramping, managing, coaching, and developing salespeople even if you haven't personally owned every one of those functions before.

  • You are capable of taking a messy business problem, breaking it into its component parts, determining what matters most, and developing a clear strategic recommendation.

  • You are equally excited by winning the client and solving the client's problem. Closing the contract isn't where your intellectual curiosity ends.

  • You have leadership horsepower and want significantly more ownership than a traditional individual-contributor sales role can provide.

  • You are hungry enough to personally build the first version rather than waiting for someone else to create the process, playbook, team, and infrastructure for you.

  • You want an opportunity where your responsibilities can grow substantially faster than your title traditionally would.

You SHOULD NOT Apply to This Role If:

  • You are a traditional Account Executive who is most comfortable selling a clearly predefined product through a predefined sales process.

  • Your ability to sell depends heavily on demos, decks, case studies, or product features rather than your ability to diagnose and solve sophisticated business problems.

  • You have very little understanding of what happens inside a revenue organization after the contract is signed.

  • You love selling but have little interest in strategy, consulting, operational design, or actually helping architect the solution.

  • You love strategy but dislike the pressure, accountability, and competitiveness associated with carrying a revenue target.

  • Concepts like pipeline math, sales capacity, GTM architecture, compensation design, RevOps, sales enablement, and performance management feel foreign to you.

  • You need someone else to turn ambiguous problems into a clearly defined list of tasks before you can execute.

  • You want to inherit a team rather than earn the opportunity to build one.

  • You are primarily motivated by having an executive title today rather than building the capability and results required to earn one tomorrow.

  • You prefer environments that are static, predictable, and already fully built.

  • You eat your pizza with ranch.

  • You clap at the end of movies or when a plane lands.

May be flexible on the last two…

Key Responsibilities

  • Help build and scale Curvion's new B2B revenue division from the ground up.

  • Personally own the acquisition of high-value B2B accounts and carry a meaningful new revenue target.

  • Manage sophisticated sales cycles from discovery and diagnosis through solution design, proposal, negotiation, and close.

  • Lead strategic discovery sessions with founders, CEOs, and revenue leaders.

  • Participate directly in and ultimately lead Curvion Blue-Print Revenue Architecture engagements.

  • Analyze client organizations across Revenue Planning & Economics, GTM & Deal Flow Architecture, Sales Role Architecture, Sales Enablement, RevOps & Technology, Recruiting, and Sales Management & Performance.

  • Translate complex business problems into clear strategic recommendations, priorities, roadmaps, and implementation plans.

  • Help develop, productize, and continuously improve Curvion's B2B Revenue Architecture methodology.

  • Identify expansion opportunities where Blue-Print clients can benefit from Curvion's recurring and done-for-you services.

  • Work directly with the CEO on B2B GTM strategy, positioning, offer development, sales strategy, and growth initiatives.

  • Help establish the sales processes, pipeline management, forecasting, reporting, KPIs, and operating cadence required to scale the division.

  • Document and systematize what works so the initial leader-led motion can eventually be executed by a larger team.

  • Participate in recruiting and developing future members of the B2B revenue organization.

  • Take increasing ownership of the revenue function as performance, capability, and the division itself grows.

  • Develop toward ultimately leading the sales team and broader revenue organization.

  • Bonus opportunities

  • Commission pay

  • Uncapped commission

Schedule:

  • Monday to Friday

  • Strong understanding of consulting business operations, including utilization management, revenue forecasting, backlog management, and departmental financial performance.

About the Company

TalentPluto is a Y Combinator-backed startup building the hiring stack for high-growth companies. We run two connected products: a talent network that places engineering, go-to-market, and operations people into fast-moving startups, and an AI recruiting tool that lets a hiring team run candidate search, tiered enrichment, rubric-based scoring, and outbound campaigns directly from their assistant. We work with dozens of venture-backed startups across AI, developer tools, fintech, and healthcare. The team is small and founder-led, and interns work on live problems rather than practice ones.

The Opportunity

This is a design engineering internship, which means the same person decides how something should work and then builds it. You will take ideas that arrive as a sentence or a rough sketch and turn them into interfaces people actually use, owning the visual and interaction decisions along the way rather than waiting for a spec.

We care about craft here in a way that is easy to claim and harder to do: spacing, hierarchy, typography, and the small interaction details that make a product feel considered. Because the team is small and the surface is still being shaped, your judgment about how something should feel carries real weight, and you will see the result in front of users quickly.

Responsibilities

  • Design and build product surfaces end to end, from low-fidelity idea to shipped interface.
  • Own layout, typography, hierarchy, and interaction detail across the surfaces you build.
  • Implement in React, Next.js, and TypeScript, working with the backend services behind each surface.
  • Build and extend shared components so the product stays visually consistent as it grows.
  • Make interfaces work well across screen sizes and states, including the empty and error ones.

Requirements

  • Strong taste for product design, interaction design, and visual detail.
  • Experience building with React, Next.js, TypeScript, or similar frontend tools.
  • Comfort working from low-fidelity ideas and turning them into usable interfaces.
  • Strong understanding of layout, typography, hierarchy, and responsive design.
  • Has shipped design or frontend projects, whether independently, in class, or through prior work.
  • Clear communicator who can work independently in a remote environment.

jobs.title: VP of Revenue & Growth
jobs.excerpt: A Snapshot of Curvion Blue:Curvion is a high performance RevOps & sales augmentation agency that installs and deploys enterprise-grade, AI-driven revenue engines and selling systems for our clients.
jobs.description:
A Snapshot of Curvion Blue:

Curvion is a high performance RevOps & sales augmentation agency that installs and deploys enterprise-grade, AI-driven revenue engines and selling systems for our clients. Think of a lead generation based marketing agency…. But focused on sales! We design and install complete sales systems from sales processes and GTM strategy to CRM setup all the way to fully outsourced sales engagements. Then we enhance those systems with AI enabled tools and battle tested playbooks, and finally, we provide highly trained sales talent to help our clients execute so their revenue engine runs faster, scales efficiently, and performs consistently. In short, we build and power modern, AI-driven sales systems that help companies grow with clarity and control.

Position Overview

What exactly is a VP of Revenue & Growth at Curvion Blue? In simple terms, think of a highly sophisticated revenue leader who combines the capabilities of a CRO, enterprise business development leader, and revenue strategy consultant but still has the hunger and builder mentality to get directly in the trenches.

We are building an entirely new B2B revenue line at Curvion, and rather than building the department from the bottom up and eventually hiring someone to lead it, we are hiring top down. This person will enter as the leader of the function, but in the beginning, they will also be the function.

Their mandate spans three critical areas: acquiring high-value B2B accounts, leading the strategy and architecture work we sell to those accounts, and ultimately building and leading the revenue organization responsible for scaling this division.

Our flagship entry point service into B2B is the Curvion Blue-Print, an initial consulting and Revenue Architecture engagement designed to help companies build the foundation required to scale a sophisticated revenue function. Rather than delivering generic sales consulting, we architect the interconnected components of the revenue engine across Revenue Planning & Economics, GTM & Deal Flow Architecture, Sales Role Architecture, Sales Enablement, RevOps & Technology, Recruiting, and Sales Management & Performance.

This means the person selling the engagement needs to be capable of sitting across from a founder, CEO, or revenue executive, diagnosing their business, understanding where their revenue infrastructure is breaking down, and developing a sophisticated point of view on what needs to change. Just as importantly, they need to be capable of leading the strategic work after the deal closes.

Initially, this person will personally own much of the B2B sales motion, participate directly in client strategy engagements, help productize and refine our Revenue Architecture methodology, and work alongside the CEO to establish this new division. As the business grows, they will recruit, develop, and lead the team around them, transitioning from individual production toward ownership of the broader revenue function.

We are specifically looking for someone who has already operated at a high level across B2B revenue strategy, sales, GTM, and leadership, but hasn't lost the desire to build. If your idea of being a revenue executive is reviewing dashboards while everyone else does the selling and client work, this probably isn't the opportunity for you. If the opportunity to personally build a revenue line and eventually lead the organization you created sounds exciting, keep reading ;)

You SHOULD Apply to This Role If:

  • You have extensive experience building and scaling sophisticated B2B revenue organizations and understand how the different components of a revenue engine work together.

  • You have personally sold complex, high-value B2B services, consulting engagements, technology, or other solutions requiring executive-level discovery, diagnosis, solution design, negotiation, and closing.

  • You can sit across from a founder, CEO, or CRO and confidently diagnose their revenue model, GTM strategy, pipeline, sales organization, economics, systems, and performance challenges.

  • You understand revenue planning and can work backwards from growth targets into pipeline requirements, conversion assumptions, sales capacity, headcount requirements, unit economics, and financial constraints.

  • You understand GTM and deal flow architecture and can evaluate ICPs, acquisition channels, funnel structures, sales motions, conversion paths, and how opportunities should move through the revenue engine.

  • You have experience designing sales organizations including roles, responsibilities, compensation structures, KPIs, expectations, capacity, management layers, and organizational structure.

  • You have a strong understanding of modern sales enablement and know what needs to exist across sales process, methodology, talk tracks, playbooks, training, onboarding, and rep development.

  • You understand RevOps well enough to architect how CRM, data, reporting, automation, workflows, integrations, AI, and the broader revenue technology stack should support the GTM model.

  • You understand what great recruiting, onboarding, ramp, sales management, coaching, forecasting, and performance management look like inside a sophisticated sales organization.

  • You are comfortable moving between strategy and execution. You can spend one hour developing a revenue model with a CEO and the next personally running a sales call or working through a client deliverable.

  • You have built teams before and understand how to eventually turn what you personally execute into processes, methodologies, roles, scorecards, and systems that other people can execute.

  • You are commercially minded. You don't view strategy as an academic exercise—you understand that great Revenue Architecture ultimately needs to produce pipeline, revenue, margin, and enterprise value.

  • You want genuine ownership. The opportunity to build a new B2B division, establish its methodology, generate its first waves of revenue, recruit the team, and ultimately lead the function is significantly more exciting to you than inheriting an already-built department.

  • You still love the game. Despite having leadership experience, selling, strategizing, negotiating, building, and solving difficult revenue problems still energizes you.

You SHOULD NOT Apply to This Role If:

  • You have reached the point in your career where you only want to manage leaders and no longer want to personally sell, strategize, or execute.

  • Your revenue leadership experience has primarily consisted of managing an existing sales organization rather than building one.

  • You require a large existing team, established infrastructure, or fully developed playbook before you can produce results.

  • You are an exceptional sales leader but lack the GTM, RevOps, financial, and strategic depth required to architect an entire revenue function.

  • You are an exceptional strategist but aren't comfortable carrying a quota, selling sophisticated engagements, and being directly accountable for revenue.

  • You struggle to move between executive-level strategy and highly tactical execution.

  • You are uncomfortable challenging founders and executives when the data or strategy suggests they are solving the wrong problem.

  • You want the title and responsibilities of a revenue executive without the accountability that comes with owning the number.

  • You prefer environments that are static, predictable, and already fully built.

  • You eat your pizza with ranch.

  • You clap at the end of movies or when a plane lands.

May be flexible on the last two…

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the growth and development of Curvion's new B2B revenue division.

  • Personally lead the acquisition of high-value B2B accounts during the initial stages of the division.

  • Own complex sales cycles from initial discovery and diagnosis through solution architecture, proposal development, negotiation, and close.

  • Lead strategic discovery and Revenue Architecture engagements with founders, CEOs, revenue executives, and other senior stakeholders.

  • Translate strategic findings into clear revenue architecture recommendations, roadmaps, priorities, and implementation plans.

  • Help productize, refine, and continuously improve the Curvion Blue-Print methodology and B2B service offering.

  • Identify opportunities within Blue-Print engagements to expand clients into Curvion's recurring and done-for-you service lines.

  • Work closely with the CEO on B2B positioning, offer strategy, pricing, sales strategy, revenue targets, and growth planning.

  • Establish forecasting, pipeline management, sales processes, KPIs, reporting, and operating cadences for the new division.

  • Build the playbooks, processes, methodologies, and infrastructure necessary to transition execution from founder/leader-led to team-led.

  • Recruit and develop future sales, strategy, and revenue talent as the division scales (you would work hand in hand with our recruiting department to identify right fit talent)

  • Gradually assume leadership of the broader revenue organization and develop the management infrastructure required to consistently hit company growth targets.

  • Own revenue performance and ultimately be accountable for the number, not simply the activity surrounding it.

Job Type: Full-time

Compensation package:

  • Bonus opportunities

  • Commission pay

  • Uncapped commission

  • Medical, Dental, Vision, 401K

Schedule:

  • Monday to Friday

Work Location: Remote

Compensation Range: $180K - $300K

Who are we and what do we do?

BrowserStack is the world’s leading cloud-based software testing platform, empowering over 50,000 customers—including Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, and Google—to deliver high-quality software at speed. Founded in 2011 by Ritesh Arora and Nakul Aggarwal, the company has grown to support more than two million tests daily across 22 global data centers, providing instant access to 35,000+ real devices and browsers.

With over 1,200 employees and a remote-first approach, BrowserStack operates at the intersection of scale, reliability, and innovation. Its suite of products spans manual and automated testing, visual regression, accessibility, and test management—all designed to simplify the testing process for modern development teams. Behind the scenes, BrowserStack continues to push the boundaries with AI capabilities like smart test case generation and design, flakiness detection, auto-healing and more —helping teams reduce maintenance overhead, debug faster, and catch issues earlier in the development lifecycle.

Recognized for its innovation and growth, BrowserStack has been named to the Forbes Cloud 100 list for four consecutive years. With backing from investors like Accel, Bond, and Insight Partners, the company continues to expand its product offerings and global footprint. The Technical Product Manager owns a product vertical end-to-end, from strategy and outcomes through technical design, delivery, and launch.

We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal. The bar is knowing where AI genuinely improves an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted.

What You'll Own

  • Aligning Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance around clear product decisions and launch requirements.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of product management experience, including ownership of complex technical products from strategy through production.

  • Strong technical foundation across system architecture, APIs, databases, workflows, failure modes and distributed systems.

  • Experience working closely with engineers and ability to review, challenge and contribute to technical designs.

  • Experience in payments, banking, remittance, insurance, trading or another regulated, high-consequence product domain.

  • Strong product judgment and ability to make difficult trade-offs under technical, regulatory and operational constraints.

Nice to have

Outcome

Location

Language

This is a remote position.

DoD SkillBridge Internship:IT/Cybersecurity SkillBridge Internship
SkillBridge Host Company: Apex Systems
SkillBridge Provider: Vets2PM LLC
Location: Remote/Various locations
NOTE: Intern must be willing to live/work in the Washington, DC region, or potentially other Apex locations if hired.

Applicants must be active-duty U.S. Military Members who qualify for the DoD SkillBridge Program.
To Apply:
1. Go toand complete the SkillBridge interest form.
2. Return to this posting and click 'Apply'.
Duration:90–180 days
Overview:
Apex Systems isseeking motivated service members to participate in our IT/Cybersecurity SkillBridge Internship Program. This program provides structured technical training, industry-recognized certifications, and meaningful networking experiences to support a smooth transition into civilian IT careers.
Interns will spend 50% of their time developing technical skills through Apex’s training platform and 50% networking with other transitioning service members who are exploring IT career pathways. These peer conversations help interns build a strong professional network, gain real‑world career insights, and learn from the experiences of other veterans navigating the IT job market.
The overall goal of the internship is to prepare participants for post‑service careers across Apex’s IT practice areas—networking, cloud, cybersecurity, engineering, helpdesk, and more.
Company Website:
Responsibilities:
1. Technical Certification Training (50% of the day)
Participate in self-paced IT and cybersecurity training toward certifications such as:
  • CompTIA Security+
  • CEH
  • CCNA
  • AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner
  • Azure-900
  • CISSP
  • CySA+
  • Linux+
  • CISM
  • CCNP
  • Prepare for and sit for certification exams using Apex’s training resources.
2. Peer Networking & Veteran Engagement (50% of the day)
  • Connect with other transitioning service members who are exploring or entering IT career fields.
  • Participate in peer-to-peer conversations to share experiences, lessons learned, and available resources.
  • Help fellow veterans understand SkillBridge opportunities, IT career pathways, and transition tools.
  • Build a professional network that supports long-term career growth and job exploration.
  • Serve as a resource for new SkillBridge participants by sharing insights on study strategies, certifications, and navigating civilian IT roles.
  • Residents will serve as a liaison between veterans exploring civilian IT roles, and the Apex teams that support hiring and career development.
  • This networking component enables interns to learn from the transition journeys of their peers, strengthen communication skills, and expand their professional footprint within the IT sector.
3. Onboarding & Transition Support
  • Take part in program onboarding, goal setting, and mentorship activities.
  • Attend professional development touchpoints with Apex team members.
  • Complete out-processing activities and interview for full-time roles with Apex Systems or partner employers.
Qualifications
  • Active-duty U.S. military and SkillBridge eligible.
  • Active Secret clearance or higher (minimum).
  • Security+ certification or relevant IT experience with a desire to obtain certifications during the internship.
  • Willingness to work in Washington, DC, or another Apex location post-internship (to be discussed during intake). This WILL NOT be a remote job if hired after the internship.
  • Strong self-discipline and ability to manage a remote, self-paced schedule.
  • Interest in pursuing a career in IT, cybersecurity, or technical support roles.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Motivation to support peers and actively participate in networking.
  • Ability to work independently and manage time effectively.
Benefits
  • Opportunity to earn industry-recognized IT certifications.
  • Hands-on training that aligns with in-demand technical roles.
  • Meaningful professional networking with other transitioning veterans.
  • Mentorship from Apex technical and career-development professionals.
  • Enhanced soft skills including communication, collaboration, and career navigation.
  • Contribution to the broader military/veteran community.
Vets2PM Provides:
  • Mentorship and guidance via regular SkillBridge intern Zoom Meetings.

jobs.description:
Allara is a comprehensive women’s health provider that specializes in expert, longitudinal care that supports women through every life stage. Trusted by over 60,000 women nationwide, Allara makes expert healthcare accessible by connecting patients with multidisciplinary care teams that have a deep understanding of hormonal, metabolic, and reproductive care. Allara provides ongoing support for hormonal conditions like PCOS, chronic conditions like insulin resistance, and life stages like perimenopause, helping patients see improved health outcomes. As one of the fastest-growing women’s health platforms in the U.S., Allara is bridging long-overlooked gaps in healthcare for women.

The Opportunity

We’re hiring board-certified Family Nurse Practitioners who want to focus on what matters most: delivering exceptional care to women with complex hormonal and metabolic conditions. To learn more about our mission and clinical approach, visit.

Location: Fully remote within the U.S.

Your Impact

  • Conduct thorough patient assessments and develop personalized treatment plans via video visits

  • Collaborate with a multidisciplinary care team to deliver the highest standards of care

  • Complete required trainings and uphold Allara's clinical policies, standards, and best practices

  • Educate patients on preventive care and wellness using evidence-based strategies

  • Maintain accurate, up-to-date patient records and complete charting in a timely manner

  • Respond to patient questions and administrative messages with clarity and care

  • Dedicate a full-time focus to patient care, including consultations and medical guidance, with prescribing when clinically appropriate

Primary Clinical focus

  • PCOS, Hypothyroidism / Hashimoto's, Metabolic Syndrome, Menopause / Perimenopause / HRT, PMDD, Obesity / Weight Management, Diabetes, Hyperlipidemia, and Anxiety/Depression (mild to moderate)

Required Qualifications

  • Certification: Active national board certification as a Nurse Practitioner

  • Experience: Minimum of 2 years of consecutive experience as a Nurse Practitioner specializing in women's health and treating chronic conditions

  • Clinical Independence: Proven ability to function as an autonomous provider with strong diagnostic judgment and critical thinking skills

  • Communication: Exceptional written and verbal communication, with an emphasis on compassion and clarity

  • Webside Manner: A natural ability to build trust and connection with patients in a virtual setting

  • Evidence-Based Practice: A genuine commitment to delivering care rooted in current clinical research

  • Technical Proficiency: Comfortable working across multiple platforms including EMR systems, text expanders, Gmail, Google Calendar, Zoom, and scheduling tools

  • Telemedicine Experience: Prior telehealth experience is a plus

  • State License Requirements & Hiring Considerations: Minimum of 3 active unrestricted, and unencumbered state licenses: at least 2 in CA, NY (autonomous), or FL (autonomous), plus 1 or more in additional states based on forecasted hiring needs.

A note on state licensing: All active and pending licenses held at the time of application are collected and reviewed during our process. Hiring decisions reflect current state-level needs, which evolve over time. Applicants may not move forward immediately if there is no active need in their licensed states. We regularly revisit candidates as needs expand and when experience, licensure, and role requirements align.

What Allara Offers

  • Annual base salary range: $120,000 – $130,000, and can increase up to $172,500 - $182,500 through our incentive compensation program.

    • Final base salary & incentive range is commensurate with years of relevant experience.

  • Health and Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision benefits

  • Time Off: Annual vacation, sick days, and holidays

  • CME/WFH: Annual stipend

  • Malpractice Insurance: Comprehensive coverage provided at no cost to you

  • Mission-Driven Work: Help transform the standard of care for women living with conditions that have historically been underdiagnosed and undertreated

  • Collaborative Provider Network: Connect with and learn from a community of skilled, like-minded Allara clinicians

  • Inclusive Culture: Join a supportive, diverse team that values innovation, equity, and belonging

At Allara, we believe in celebrating everything that makes us human and are proud to be an equal-opportunity workplace. jobs.title: SEO Content Specialist
jobs.excerpt: Create and improve search-led content that matches intent and supports conversion, covering both traditional SEO and Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) for AI-driven search and answer engines.
jobs.description:
Create and improve search-led content that matches intent and supports conversion, covering both traditional SEO and Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) for AI-driven search and answer engines. Focus is content quality, structure, refresh cadence, on-page optimisation, and content performance, with consistent use of approved wording patterns, required risk language, and adherence to E-E-A-T (Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trustworthiness) and YMYL (Your Money or Your Life) content standards.

Key responsibilities:

  • Write and update high-intent SEO content (commercial pages, comparison pages, FAQs, education where it supports intent).
  • Write content optimised for GEO (Generative Engine Optimisation), structuring and phrasing content so it can be clearly understood, cited, and surfaced by AI-driven search and answer engines (e.g. ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews), alongside traditional SEO.
  • Maintain a refresh plan: identify decay, update content, and improve coverage gaps.
  • Conduct keyword research to identify content opportunities, search intent, and coverage gaps across markets, feeding findings into the content plan.
  • Grow First Time Trader (FTT) volumes from generic, non-brand keyword terms through SEO content, reducing reliance on brand search and expanding acquisition from new audiences.
  • Apply on-page best practice: headings, structure, internal linking updates, meta inputs, and content QA before publish.
  • Localise (rather than directly translate) content for country-specific websites, adapting to local search intent and market nuances while avoiding content cannibalisation, duplication, and duplicate-content flags across the global site network.
  • Manage and coordinate content across multiple global/country websites, maintaining consistency of structure, tone, and compliance while reflecting local relevance.
  • Write and edit content in line with E-E-A-T (Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trustworthiness) and YMYL (Your Money or Your Life) principles, reflecting the standards required for financial content.
  • Review content performance (rankings, organic traffic, engagement, conversion) and use insights to optimise existing content and improve rankings.
  • Work within compliance constraints and use approved claims and risk language patterns.

Requirements

  • Strong SEO writing and editing, with clear understanding of intent and SERP formats.
  • Ability to follow content templates and create consistent, scannable structures.
  • High attention to detail, accuracy, and deadline discipline.
  • Comfortable with feedback loops and iteration based on performance data.
  • Understanding of GEO principles and how content is surfaced and cited by AI/LLM-driven search and answer engines.
  • Strong keyword research skills, using SEO tools to identify search intent, opportunity, and content gaps.
  • Experience managing content across global/multi-country websites, with a good understanding of avoiding content cannibalisation and duplication.
  • Good working knowledge of E-E-A-T and YMYL content requirements, ideally within a regulated or financial services environment.
  • Performance-led approach; confident reviewing content performance data and optimising content to improve rankings.
  • Experience with Storyblok CMS advantageous.

Performance Measures

  • Content shipped and refreshed to plan, with on-time delivery and low rework rate.
  • Improvement in performance of priority pages (rankings, traffic quality, engagement).
  • Increase in FTTs sourced from generic/non-brand keyword terms, with a growing share of organic conversions coming from non-brand SEO content.
  • Content quality maintained: fewer compliance revisions, fewer factual errors, consistent structure.
  • Refresh cadence maintained with clear tracking of what changed and why.
  • Improved visibility and citation of content within AI-driven search and answer engines (GEO performance).
  • Successful localisation of content across country/language websites with no cannibalisation, duplication, or duplicate-content issues flagged.

Reporting directly to the COO, the Manager, Strategic Operations serves as a force multiplier for the leadership team, ensuring priorities translate into disciplined execution. This role is responsible for maintaining work management platforms, operational playbooks, financial and IT systems. The Manager, Strategic Operations will help build and sustain the operational backbone of the company. You will also work closely with the COO on internal communications, board and investor materials and core organizational workflows. This role requires exceptional attention to detail, strong judgment, and a commitment to high professional standards.

About Epistemix

The most consequential decisions in public health, life sciences, insurance, and enterprise strategy share a common problem: they involve human behavior, network effects, and downstream effects that cannot be safely tested before action is taken. Traditional analytical techniques built on historical data were not built for this. Epistemix was.

We build simulation and data-driven modeling tools that let leaders visualize how strategies will unfold across populations and systems before they commit resources. By clarifying which variables drive outcomes, where leverage exists, and how they interact, we help organizations move from uncertainty to conviction. Getting these decisions right means faster interventions, better-allocated resources, and measurable improvements in human and economic outcomes. We exist to make that possible.

Our platform gives organizations access to realistic, high-resolution population data and the modeling infrastructure to run scenario planning at scale. Together, these capabilities let decision-makers stress-test strategies in a controlled environment before deploying them in the real world across healthcare, consumer industries, insurance, and government. We are approaching our Series B and actively building the team that will define what comes next.

Responsibilities

Operational Infrastructure

  • Organizational Systems: Support the COO in designing and maintaining internal systems that enable the organization to operate effectively. This includes shaping the structure of internal resources, playbooks, and working frameworks so that teams have clear guidance, consistent information, and easy access to the tools they need to execute.

  • Institutional Knowledge: Maintain key internal resources so critical information, decisions, and processes remain visible, searchable, and easy for teams to navigate as the company grows.

  • Execution & Change Management: Partner with the COO to lead internal initiatives, introducing improved ways of working, and supporting teams as new systems or operational practices are implemented. Review and refine internal resources, documentation, and operational frameworks to ensure they are consistent, practical, and aligned with the organization’s evolving needs.

Technology Operations

  • Technology Operations: Oversee the day-to-day operational management of company technology systems, including employee access, licensing, and basic infrastructure coordination. This role will ensure team members have the tools and access they need to work effectively while maintaining appropriate controls as individuals join, transition within, or exit the organization.

  • IT Vendor Management: Manage vendor relationships, prioritize requests, and ensure timely resolution of technology issues while maintaining high standards for responsiveness, reliability, and service quality.

  • Technology Stewardship: Help ensure the organization maintains reliable and well-managed technology systems by coordinating data protection practices, backups, and continuity safeguards. This role will help ensure the company’s information assets remain secure, organized, and protected.

Financial Operations

  • Financial Alignment: Serve as a key operational partner to the COO in maintaining financial visibility across the organization. Coordinate closely with the accounting team to track priorities, monitor open items, and ensure financial processes and operational decisions remain aligned.

  • Budget Discipline: Assist the COO in supporting the organization’s commitment to disciplined financial management by monitoring spending across teams and ensuring financial practices remain consistent with company priorities.

  • Expense & Travel Oversight: Oversee the company’s expense and travel processes to ensure they operate smoothly and in line with company standards. Maintain clear records, coordinate approvals where appropriate, and help ensure spending remains transparent, organized, and aligned with company expectations.

Leadership Operations & Strategic Coordination

Help ensure materials, updates, and deliverables are organized, timely, and aligned with company priorities. Respond to inquiries from board members and investors in a timely and professional manner.

  • Events & Organizational Milestones: Coordinate the planning and execution of key company moments including leadership offsites, company gatherings, and industry events. Ensure events are thoughtfully organized and aligned with the company’s broader strategic and cultural objectives.

  • Special Projects: Support high-priority initiatives led by the COO and leadership team by stepping in to advance urgent or complex workstreams, gathering information across teams, and ensuring important initiatives continue to move forward.

  • 2+ years of experience within a Series A or Series B stage company preferred.

  • Deep experience in building complex databases, interconnected wikis, and project management hubs in Notion or similar software.

  • Comfortable with accounting, budget tracking, and platforms like Ramp.

Why Join Epistemix?

jobs.description:
Peek is the operating system powering the experiences industry - from museums and attractions to tours and activities. With over $7B in bookings, Peek’s AI-powered platform has helped thousands of merchants to increase revenues, save time, and deliver seamless guest experiences. Customers include MoMA, Whitney Museum, Seattle Aquarium, Bryant Park & Looping Group. The company has raised over $150 million from institutional investors Westcap, Goldman Sachs, and SpringCoast Partners. Learn more at .

As a remote-first company recognized by Forbes as one of America's Best Startup Employers and by Built In as a 2025 and 2026 Best Place to Work, we are a global team of "Peeksters" who "Obsess Over Our Customers," "Accomplish Big Things," "Collaborate With Purpose," and "Get Better Every Day.

The Role

We’re hiring a Manager, Organic Growth to own the strategy and execution of SEO, AEO, and GEO across PeekPro, ACME Ticketing, and Connect&GO.

This is a builder’s role. You will inherit three distinct brands with three distinct audiences, overlapping topical territory, and no unified organic strategy connecting them. Your job is to define that strategy, then run it — deciding which brand should rank for what, where consolidation creates authority and where it creates cannibalization, and how a single portfolio of content earns visibility across both traditional search results and AI-generated answers.

The mandate is demand, not traffic. Experience operators researching software rarely convert on first touch; they compare, they read, they research, and they come back weeks later. You will be measured on organic-sourced pipeline and closed-won revenue across all three brands — not on rankings or sessions alone.

You’ll partner closely with Growth, Content, Product Marketing, and Engineering.. You are the connective tissue between them and the subject matter expert within the team.

What You’ll Do

Own the number

  • Carry the organic pipeline target across all three brands. Build the forecast, report against it monthly, and be accountable for organic-attributed opportunities, demos, and closed-won revenue — not just clicks.

Define the multi-brand organic strategy

  • Build the portfolio-level keyword and entity map: which brand owns which topics, which terms are contested, and where the three sites should complement rather than compete.

  • Set the roadmap for site architecture, internal linking, taxonomy, and content across all three properties — including domain consolidation, migrations, and redirect strategy.

  • Develop vertical-specific organic plays for distinct operator segments (tours and activities, museums, zoos and aquariums, water parks, FECs, escape rooms, and more), each with its own language, buying process, and competitive set.

Lead AEO and GEO

  • Own how Peek’s brands appear in AI-generated answers — ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, Copilot. Build the measurement approach for a channel most teams still cannot measure.

  • Establish the standards that make our content machine-readable and citable: structured data, entity consistency, answer-first formatting, and comparison content that holds up when an LLM summarizes it.

  • Develop a point of view on how zero-click and agentic search reshape the operator buying journey, and translate that into strategy — then keep revising it as the landscape moves.

Build authority off-site

  • Identify and activate high-value authority targets across the experiences, attractions, travel, and hospitality-tech ecosystem — industry associations, trade publications, review platforms, partner and integration directories.

  • Work with PR, Partnerships, and Content to earn links and mentions that measurably move organic visibility, and quantify that lift.

  • Own our presence on the third-party review and comparison sites (G2, Capterra, and category equivalents) that both buyers and LLMs treat as authoritative.

Guide the technical foundation

  • Set technical SEO requirements and priorities, and partner with Engineering and Web to get them shipped — crawlability, indexation, Core Web Vitals, JS rendering, structured data, international and multi-domain handling.

  • Run continuous audits across three codebases and CMS setups; triage what actually affects revenue and make the case for prioritization against competing roadmaps.

  • Own migration risk. When domains, subfolders, or brand architecture change, you are the person who makes sure we don’t lose what we’ve built.

Direct content intelligence and CRO

  • Feed the Content team clustered keyword, entity, and intent insight — what to write, for which brand, for which vertical, and why.

  • Audit and prune the existing content library across three brands: consolidate, refresh, redirect, or retire.

  • Partner with Web and Lifecycle on conversion — landing page experience, offers, and forms — so improved visibility turns into qualified demos.

  • Evaluate programmatic and templated page opportunities (by vertical, geography, use case, and integration) and build them where they earn their keep.

Educate and evangelize

  • Be the internal expert. Bring the rest of Marketing, Product, and leadership along on how search is changing and what it means for how we go to market.

What You’ll Need

Must-haves

  • 4–7 years in SEO or organic growth, with meaningful time in B2B SaaS or another considered-purchase, multi-touch environment.

  • A revenue-first mindset. You are comfortable being measured on pipeline, you can build and defend a forecast, and you don’t hide behind traffic metrics.

  • A real point of view on AEO and GEO. You’ve tested how brands surface in AI answers, you can explain what you learned, and you know the difference between a durable strategy and a trick.

  • Technical fluency. You can diagnose crawl, indexation, rendering, and site-architecture issues yourself, write a clear technical brief, and hold your own in a conversation with engineers.

  • Analytical rigor. Comfortable in GA4, Google Search Console, Looker Studio, etc. You can build an attribution view, spot when the data is lying, and model the impact of a bet before you make it.

  • Tool depth. Strong hands-on command of Ahrefs and/or Semrush, Google Search Console, and Screaming Frog. Familiarity with an AI-visibility tracking tool (Profound, Peec, or similar) is a plus.

  • Comfort with ambiguity. Three brands, recent acquisitions, incomplete data, and a category being rewritten in real time. You find that energizing rather than paralyzing.

Nice to have

  • Experience with multi-brand, multi-domain, or post-acquisition SEO

  • Programmatic or template-driven SEO at scale, or managing large directory-style page sets.

  • Background in travel, tourism, attractions, hospitality tech, or another operator-facing vertical SaaS category.

  • Local and multi-location SEO, or Knowledge Graph and entity optimization work.

The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Maestro, an AI-native inventory-planning intelligence venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

Maestro is an autopilot planning intelligence for SMB operators managing physical inventory complexity without a planning team. It connects across channels and ERPs, handles routine decisions silently, and surfaces exceptions with context and a recommended action before they become revenue losses. The institutional memory that today lives only in a planner's head gets externalized, structured, and queried in plain language.

We didn't just build a thesis; we validated it directly with the market. We have spoken with founders, VP E-Commerce leaders, merchandise planners, and multi-channel operators at DTC and specialty retail brands across the US. The market signal is clear:

  • Autopilot is the vision: Every named competitor generates recommendations that humans still have to act on manually. No product at this revenue tier is building toward full autonomous execution of the planning lifecycle. Maestro's product vision is full autopilot: the system owns the buy decision, allocation, and markdown trigger end-to-end. But buyers earn that trust incrementally, starting with routine decisions handled silently and exceptions surfaced with context.
  • The pain is in the dollars, not the dashboards: Documented annual losses across just five buyer accounts total $1.25–1.5M+. Buyers currently spend $0–500/month on software; the entire planning budget is tied up in headcount. The payback case is immediate, and ROI demonstration, not feature demos, will be the critical sales motion.
  • Institutional memory failure is systemic and unresolved: One SVP with 30 years of domain expertise described relying entirely on personal recall to flag which materials, colours, and styles underperformed last season. When he leaves, that knowledge disappears, and no tool captures it today. Every buyer interviewed described a version of this problem.

Market Context

We are targeting a large, structurally underserved segment: SMB operators managing multi-channel physical inventory complexity at $5M–50M revenue — importers, distributors, Amazon aggregators, and specialty retailers. The beachhead SAM is estimated at $200M–$225M across approximately 15K–16K brands in the US and Canada. Excel is the universal incumbent! 5/5 buyers in our discovery sprint were on spreadsheets, with zero dedicated planning tools in use. EBITDA across the $10–50M DTC cohort is compressed to 7.25% in 2025 with revenue declining ~4.6% YoY. Planning waste attacks the margin stack directly.
