Before you apply: Thoughtful use of AI is encouraged. If you use it to support your application, please make sure it helps communicate your experience clearly and accurately. Authenticity and originality will help you stand out.

The Work You’ll Do

At the heart of this role is owning and growing strong, strategic customer relationships across Australia and New Zealand.

You’ll:

  • Own a portfolio of university partners, building trusted relationships from day-to-day contacts to senior decision-makers and developing a deep understanding of their goals, challenges, stakeholders, and what success looks like for them.
  • Help partners get meaningful, lasting value from Acuity, using customer insight, data, and your understanding of their context to guide conversations and recommend the right path forward.
  • Stay ahead of what your customers need, identifying risks early, navigating challenges thoughtfully, and bringing the right people from across Acuity together when needed.
  • Spot opportunities to deepen and grow partnerships through greater adoption, new use cases, additional products, referrals, or connections elsewhere within an institution.
  • Work closely with our Growth team to develop opportunities across the region, bringing your customer relationships and local market knowledge into how we grow.
  • Spend meaningful time in the market, meeting partners in person, visiting campuses, and representing Acuity at conferences and industry events.
  • Bring what you’re learning back into Acuity, sharing customer and market insight that helps us better support our partners and make smarter decisions about the region.

What You’ll Help Make Possible

Partnerships that deepen over time.
Our strongest customer relationships go beyond successful adoption. They’re built on trust, shared understanding, and meaningful outcomes. You’ll help create the conditions for those partnerships to last, deepen, and open new possibilities over time.

Growth built on trust.
Some of our strongest growth in the region has come through advocacy, referrals, and word of mouth. You’ll help turn great customer relationships into greater adoption, new use cases, introductions across institutions, and opportunities to support more of the higher education community.

A stronger local presence.
Having someone on the ground changes what’s possible. Partners can see and spend time with us more easily, Acuity can participate more actively in the higher education community, and our investment in the region becomes increasingly visible.

Acuity getting smarter about the region.
Being close to the market means seeing things others might miss: what partners are talking about, how institutions are changing, where new needs are emerging, and the important differences between Australia and New Zealand. Your perspective will help shape how we support customers, evolve our approach, and decide where to invest.

Strong partnerships creating new possibilities.
By helping partners get more value from Acuity, deepening relationships across their institutions, and understanding where their needs are evolving, you’ll help create opportunities for those partnerships to grow over time.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first year, we’d hope to see:

Partners who trust you and value your perspective. You understand their world, know the people who matter, and have built relationships that go beyond regular check-ins. Customers see you as someone who can help them think through challenges, opportunities, and what comes next.

A healthy, growing portfolio. Your customers are realising meaningful value, risks are surfaced and addressed early, and you’re creating the conditions for strong retention, deeper adoption, and expansion over time.

A meaningful presence in the region. You’ve met our partners in person, built connections across the higher education community, and become a familiar and credible face for Acuity in Australia and New Zealand.

Growth emerging from strong relationships. You’re spotting opportunities within and beyond your portfolio, generating introductions and referrals, and working with the Go-To-Market team to turn the right opportunities into something more.

A stronger foundation for what comes next. You’re bringing useful market insight back into Acuity, advocating for what the region needs, and helping us learn what works so we can make better decisions about how we support customers and grow our presence over time.

How You’ll Work Across Acuity

You’ll be part of our Customer Success team, reporting to our Senior Manager, Customer Success and working alongside CSMs who support university partners across Acuity.

You’ll partner closely with our Go-To-Market team as you identify opportunities within existing relationships, develop referrals and new connections, and help turn regional insight into new business. You’ll also work across Product, Research, Marketing, Support, and other teams to bring the right expertise and resources to our partners when they need it.

Because you’ll be based in Australia while many of your colleagues are in Canada and Europe, you’ll often be the person closest to what’s happening in the market. We’ll rely on you not just to share what you’re seeing, but to advocate for what your customers and the region need.

That could mean bringing a Research expert into an important customer conversation, making the case for locally relevant Marketing support, connecting Product to an emerging customer need, or asking Growth to lean into an opportunity you’re seeing.

You won’t be expected to have every answer or do everything yourself. There’s plenty of expertise to draw on across Acuity. But you’ll need to be proactive and persistent about accessing it: ask questions, make clear asks, follow up, and keep the right things moving even when the people or resources you need are on the other side of the world.

Part of your role will be connecting those worlds: bringing local context into Acuity, bringing Acuity’s expertise to the region, and making sure Australia and New Zealand have a strong voice as our presence there grows.

What You’ll Bring

Success in this role is as much about how you operate as what you know. You’ll bring the judgment, curiosity, relationship skills, and ownership we look for in great Customer Success, along with the resourcefulness and resilience to help build our presence in the region.

You’re likely to thrive here if you:

  • Build trusted, strategic customer relationships. You have several years of Customer Success, Account Management, or similar experience owning complex, long-term customer relationships, and know how to build credibility across an institution, from day-to-day partners to senior decision-makers.
  • Own the health and commercial success of your portfolio. You’ve been accountable for customer outcomes, adoption, retention, and renewals, know how to identify and address risk early, and understand what it takes to keep a portfolio healthy over time.
  • See growth as part of great Customer Success. You’re commercially minded and have experience growing existing accounts through deeper adoption, new products or use cases, referrals, or expansion elsewhere within an organisation. You can recognise and develop an opportunity without turning every customer conversation into a sales conversation.
  • Know the Australian higher education landscape. You’ve worked with Australian higher education institutions and understand how universities operate, including their decision-making structures, stakeholder networks, admissions cycles, and the rhythms and nuances of the sector.
  • Operate independently without operating in isolation. You’re comfortable using your judgment, making decisions, and moving work forward autonomously, while knowing when to seek input, challenge your thinking, or bring others into the conversation.
  • Are persistent and resourceful. You ask for what you need, follow up when something matters, find another path when the first one doesn’t work, and keep momentum through ambiguity, setbacks, or competing priorities.
  • Work effectively across teams and boundaries. You know how to bring people together to solve customer problems and move opportunities forward, even when you don’t directly own the people or resources you need.
  • Stay curious and adaptable. You ask good questions, learn quickly, connect ideas across different institutions and customer needs, and adjust your approach as you learn.

Experience with admissions, assessment, education technology, health sciences, or the systems and organisations that support Australian higher education would be particularly valuable, but isn’t essential.

How We Support You

Our Australian team members are employed through our Employer of Record, Deel, with access to Acuity benefits and programs alongside Australian employment entitlements.

Transparent compensation. A base salary of $115,000–$126,000 AUD, plus a $10,000 AUD annual retention bonus and additional incentives when customer referrals lead to new business. A 12% employer superannuation contribution is provided through Deel.

Learning that grows with you. $3,000 AUD annually for professional and personal development.

Shared success. Eligibility to participate in Acuity Insights’ Employee Share Option Plan, with grants based on role and level.

Time to rest and reset. In addition to your annual leave entitlement, there’s flexibility to take additional time off when you need it, plus monthly Acuity Days and a two-week company-wide closure each December.

Health and wellbeing. Access to private health insurance or an allowance to support mental health and wellbeing. Specific availability and terms will be confirmed during the offer and Deel onboarding process.

Remote-first work. Work remotely from Australia, with company-provided tools and hardware and up to $150 AUD per month toward a co-working space where needed.

A note on working across time zones

Acuity is a Canadian-founded, remote-first company, with many of your colleagues based in North America and Europe. Some flexibility to start earlier or finish later on occasion will create overlap for team meetings and collaboration, and we’ll be thoughtful about making that sustainable.

What Happens After You Apply

We review every application carefully and don’t use AI to evaluate candidates. Our interviews are two-way conversations designed to help us understand your experience and goals, while giving you plenty of opportunity to understand the role, team, and Acuity.

Our process typically takes 2–4 weeks and includes an intro conversation with Talent, a conversation with the hiring manager, and conversations with future collaborators across Customer Success and Go-To-Market. If it’s a match, we’ll move to reference checks and a formal offer.

Life at Acuity Insights

We’re a remote-first team of 140+ people, built around trust, autonomy, flexibility, and a sustainable pace. We work thoughtfully across a distributed team, creating space for deep work alongside intentional connection.

Acuity Insights has been named one of Canada’s Top Small & Medium Employers for the second consecutive year, reflecting our commitment to building an environment where people can do meaningful work and grow over time.

About Acuity Insights

Acuity Insights builds products that help higher education institutions make better decisions about people, from admissions through to development.

Our work is grounded in a simple idea: people are more than their grades, and potential can be understood and developed, not just measured. Our Casper situational judgment assessment has been completed by over 1 million applicants and is backed by nearly 20 years of research.

Today, we’re evolving our products to better connect assessment, insight, and development, helping institutions identify potential and support its growth over time.

jobs.title: Co-Founder & CEO - AI Healthcare Revenue Recovery
jobs.excerpt: The OpportunityFutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Reclaim, an AI-native denial management and revenue recovery venture.
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Reclaim, an AI-native denial management and revenue recovery venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

We are entering a $16B+ Total Addressable Market with a gaping $ 7.5B–$10B whitespace, targeting the highly underserved mid-market segment. Currently, 30–40% of denied medical claims go uncontested because practices lack the staff and capital to contest them. This systemic failure leaves between $50,000 and $300,000 in legally earned revenue permanently abandoned at each practice every year.

Reclaim AI resolves denied and aged claims end-to-end, embedding outcome-based contingency pricing—meaning practices pay zero upfront, and we only take a cut of the dollars we successfully recover, for our target ideal customer profile (practices with $80K+ in annual recoverable claims).

Market Context

We didn’t just read market reports; we spent weeks interviewing billing managers, practice owners, revenue cycle leaders at health systems, and even digital operations leaders at major insurance companies. The dysfunction we uncovered is staggering, creating a massive opportunity for a disruptor:

  • The pain is so severe, practices are building their own tech: The frustration of payer opacity is so deep that medical billers are hiring part-time software engineers to build in-house robotic process automation (RPA) scrapers just to check claim statuses.
  • Massive, emotional write-offs: Staff carry immense guilt over these administrative losses. One small-practice assistant admitted, "I feel like we probably had to write off probably close to a million dollars" simply because they couldn't keep up with the manual follow-ups.
  • The "Payer-Side Inversion" Opportunity: We discovered that insurance companies are drowning in the exact same claims dysfunction they generate. One major payer we interviewed reported a backlog of 31,000 contested claims that consumed 80% of their staff's operational capacity, forcing emergency hires just to manage the disputes.
  • The Competition is Distracted: Well-funded Tier-1 competitors are charging $15K+ upfront licensing fees and fighting over enterprise health systems. The competitive window to capture the mid-market with a contingency-priced autonomous agent is wide open.

About FutureSight

FutureSight is a leading venture builder that co-creates world-class software companies with values-driven entrepreneurs from inception to exit. We are a team of founders, operators and designers with experience successfully bringing software to market at scale.

You’ll co-create with a proven studio team, led by John Carbrey (4x entrepreneur, $100M ARR), Krista LaRiviere (3x exited, E&Y Top Women Entrepreneur), Alan Smith (Strategyzer co-founder, $120M in products built), Prathna Ramesh (former MD of Maple Leaf Angels, $275M in follow-on capital), and Johnny Tong (0-to-1 builder, acquired by SAP and Stripe) bring a rare combination of operator exits, institutional investing, and AI product depth.

The Partnership

  • Founder equity with meaningful ownership from inception
  • Pre-seed capital committed by FutureSight for early hires and MVP development, with potential for follow-on funding
  • Venture building resources, including embedded design, engineering, growth, and fundraising support from day one
  • Investor and advisor network across vertical AI and early-stage capital markets
  • A true co-creation model in which you operate as CEO with FutureSight's cross-functional team as your partner

What You’ll Own

As Co-Founder & CEO, you will set the venture's direction and lead its execution.

  • Strategy — Refine the ICP, pricing model, and product positioning
  • Customer Development — Lead pilots with practice owners and revenue cycle leaders, convert them to paid engagements, and build the go-to-market motion
  • Product — Partner with the FutureSight product and engineering team to ship V1 and iterate on user feedback
  • Capital — Lead the seed raise, supported by FutureSight's network and traction
  • Team — Recruit and lead the founding team, and establish the cultural foundation of the company

Co-Founder Profile

  • Domain & Workflow Depth: You have direct exposure to healthcare revenue cycle, medical billing, or denial management. You understand the nuanced differences in denial codes, know why administrative denials (like credentialing gaps) are uniquely painful, and intuitively understand the fragmented systems (e.g., Tebra, eClinicalWorks, Availity) that billers are forced to use
  • Previous founding experience at a venture-backed company
  • Demonstrated success in B2B AI or B2B SaaS go-to-market, including sales and customer engagement
  • Fundraising fluency, with the ability to develop investor narratives and close capital
  • Proven ability to attract, develop, and retain top talent
  • Clear-eyed understanding of the risks and demands of co-founding a venture-backed company

How to Apply

Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, and a brief note on why this venture aligns with your goals as a founder. We will move quickly for the right candidate.

FutureSight is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences.

jobs.description:
Overview:

As our team continues to grow, we are seeking a part-time Safer Gambling Agent to strengthen our responsible gambling initiatives. This role will be responsible for ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements, promoting player protection, and developing strategies that support a safe and responsible gaming environment. The ideal candidate will have strong knowledge of safer gambling practices, regulatory frameworks, and customer risk management, along with the ability to collaborate across teams to drive a culture of responsible gaming throughout the organisation.

This is a remote, part-time role, requiring work 3 nights per week from 10pm - 6am. The role requires a dedicated home workspace and undivided attention throughout each shift. This is a busy, hands-on role and cannot be performed alongside other responsibilities.

Summary of the position:

We are seeking an enthusiastic and detail-oriented individual who works well both independently and as part of a team. This role will sit within the Safer Gambling Team, supporting the effective day-to-day delivery of our safer gambling policies, procedures, and customer protection initiatives under the guidance of the Safer Gambling Manager.

The successful candidate will be a confident and empathetic communicator, capable of engaging with customers sensitively on responsible gambling matters and conveying regulatory requirements clearly. They will handle customer interactions professionally, assess customer risk indicators, and take appropriate action in line with internal procedures and regulatory obligations.

A key part of this role is the delivery of high-quality, empathetic customer interactions, ensuring that customers who may be experiencing gambling-related harm are identified early, engaged with appropriately, and supported in line with regulatory expectations and QuinnBet's safer gambling framework.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Implement safer gambling policies and procedures in line with regulatory expectations and internal procedures
  • Maintain compliance with UKGC, Irish, and Gibraltar frameworks in all customer-facing activity
  • Conduct proactive and reactive customer interactions to identify and act on behavioural, affordability, and financial risk indicators
  • Review customer accounts and activity to identify patterns of concern, applying appropriate interventions including deposit limits, cooling-off periods, self-exclusion referrals, and GAMSTOP signposting
  • Complete affordability assessments and responsible gambling interactions in line with UKGC financial risk thresholds, escalating to the Safer Gambling Manager or Team Lead where enhanced review is required
  • Handle customer contacts relating to safer gambling, responsible gaming concerns, and self-exclusion requests in a professional, non-judgmental, and empathetic manner
  • Support the handling and resolution of safer gambling-related customer queries and complaints, escalating to the Safer Gambling Manager or team lead where appropriate
  • Maintain accurate and complete case records in the case management system, ensuring all customer interactions are documented with a recorded outcome, rational and next action
  • Receive quality assurance feedback from the Quality team and act on it promptly, working with the Safer Gambling Manager and Team lead to develop and improve performance
  • Support onboarding and continuous training by sharing knowledge and contributing to a consistent team approach
  • Support internal audits, regulatory reviews, and licensing requirements by maintaining audit-ready case files and documentation

Education and Experience Required.

  • A minimum of one year's experience in a related role, preferably in the gaming, financial services, or customer-facing compliance sector
  • Demonstrable understanding of UKGC safer gambling regulations, guidance, and expectations, or a willingness to develop this knowledge rapidly
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to prioritise and deliver in a fast-paced and dynamic environment with a high degree of personal accountability, integrity, and trust
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to assess customer risk indicators and apply sound, consistent judgment
  • High level of integrity, accountability, and discretion when handling sensitive customer information
  • Recognised relevant qualification is desirable; the company will support further certification if required
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in fluent English

What We Offer

  • Competitive renumeration
  • Ongoing professional development and training support
  • Opportunity to shape the Safer Gambling culture in a fast-growing, values-driven company
  • Support in obtaining relevant certifications and qualifications

Job Title: Experienced Clinical Research Associate Sponsor-dedicated

Job Location: Athens, Greece

Job Location Type: Home-based

Job Contract Type: Full time

Job Seniority Level:

Job Overview
Perform monitoring and site management work to ensure that sites are conducting the study(ies) and reporting study data as required by the study protocol, applicable regulations and guidelines, and sponsor requirements.

Essential Functions
• Perform site monitoring visits (selection, initiation, monitoring and close-out visits) in accordance with contracted scope of work and Good Clinical Practice.
• Work with sites to adapt, drive, and track subject recruitment plan in line with project needs to enhance predictability.
• Administer protocol and related study training to assigned sites and establish regular lines of communication with sites to manage ongoing project expectations and issues.
• Evaluate the quality and integrity of study site practices related to the proper conduct of the protocol and adherence to applicable regulations. Escalate quality issues as appropriate.
• Manage the progress of assigned studies by tracking regulatory submissions and approvals, recruitment and enrollment, case report form (CRF) completion and submission, and data query generation and resolution. May support start-up phase.
• Ensure copies/originals (as required) site documents are available for filing in the Trial Master File (TMF) and verify that the Investigator's Site File (ISF) is maintained in accordance with GCP and local regulatory requirements.
• Create and maintain appropriate documentation regarding site management, monitoring visit findings and action plans by submitting regular visit reports, generating follow-up letters and other required study documentation.
• Collaborate and liaise with study team members for project execution support as appropriate.
• If applicable, may be accountable for supporting development of project subject recruitment plan on a per site basis.
• If applicable, may be accountable for site financial management according to executed clinical trial agreement and retrieve invoices according to local requirement.

Qualifications
• High School Diploma or equivalent Degree in scientific discipline or health care preferred.
• Requires at least 2 years of year of on-site monitoring experience.
• Equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be accepted in lieu of degree.
• Good knowledge of, and skill in applying, applicable clinical research regulatory requirements.
• i.e., Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and International Conference on Harmonization (ICH) guidelines.
• Good therapeutic and protocol knowledge as provided in company training.
• Computer skills including proficiency in use of Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint and use of a laptop computer and iPhone and iPad (where applicable).
• Written and verbal communication skills including good command of Greek and English language.
• Organizational and problem-solving skills.
• Effective time and financial management skills.
• Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with coworkers, managers, and clients.

About Sharesource:

We are a BCorp company whose purpose is to democratize opportunities for individuals from developing countries. With our brand and culture empowering our partners to attract and keep the most qualified members, we share the knowledge to unleash potential and grow scaling teams for Australian and Canadian businesses.

What are we looking for?

We are seeking a motivated, organised and people-focused Scheduler / Rostering Officer to join our growing Home Care team. The successful candidate will be responsible for managing the day-to-day rostering and staffing function, ensuring our clients receive high-quality, person-centred care from appropriately matched care staff.

This is a fast-paced role requiring excellent communication, strong attention to detail and the ability to coordinate multiple priorities in a timely manner. You will work closely with clients, care workers, care partners and management to ensure services are delivered efficiently, consistently and in accordance with client care plans, available funding and organisational requirements.

What are you expected to do?

  • Manage the rostering function using Visual Care.

  • Coordinate, negotiate and schedule daily staffing allocations to ensure all short shifts are appropriately covered.
  • Maintain and regularly update casual employee rosters.
  • Monitor roster changes, cancellations, leave and staff availability, responding promptly to staffing requirements.
  • Coordinate suitable staff to meet client needs, preferences and service requirements
  • Ensure services are scheduled within available client funding and approved budgets.
  • Coordinate the provision of quality, person-centred care in accordance with client needs, service/care plans and available funding.
  • Communicate effectively with care workers, clients, families and internal team members regarding roster changes and service requirements.
  • Assist with resolving last-minute staffing issues and finding suitable replacements when required.

  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date rostering and staffing records.

  • Provide high-level administrative support across a variety of staffing, rostering and operational tasks.
  • Assist with general administration associated with the role and day-to-day business operations.
  • Respond professionally and efficiently to enquiries received by phone and email.
  • Support the broader team with additional administrative and coordination tasks as required.
  • Maintain confidentiality and comply with relevant organisational policies, procedures and privacy requirements.
  • Contribute to a positive, collaborative and client-focused workplace culture.

You'll be a great fit if:

  • You have at least 1 year of professional experience as a rostering, scheduling, administration, coordination, or a similar role in community aged care, NDIS or related industry handling AU clients.
  • You have a proven excellent client service manner and can establish relationships and build rapport with clients, their families, carers, and referral sources while maintaining effective professional communication at all times.
  • You have advanced time management and organisational skills and are highly efficient, reactive, and adaptive.
  • You are a forward planner and analytical thinker with high attention to detail.
  • You can thrive in a very fast-paced environment and work exceptionally well under pressure and within time restraints.
  • You have strong problem-solving, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills and are willing to learn and be coachable.
  • You can develop, implement, and evaluate organisational and client-focused documentation and systems.
  • You can create and promote a positive and supportive culture where all staff are valued.
  • You have excellent computer literacy, including Enterprise Management Software and sound knowledge of Microsoft Office, Office 365, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, and Adobe.
  • You have experience with Visual Care or similar rostering/client management software.
  • You are willing to work from 6:30 AM to 3:30 PM PH time and follow the DST schedule (5:30 AM t0 2:30 PM) during the first 1–3 months of training. Once you are sufficiently independent, you are willing to transition to the normal shift.

  • You are willing to follow Philippine holidays.

We will be absolutely thrilled if you also have the following:

  • Knowledge of the private pay aged care industry/issues or Community In-Home Care is desirable.

  • Previous experience in Aged Care or a related discipline is desirable.

  • Previous experience in an office management capacity is essential.

What you gain beyond the role:

  • Remote + Hybrid Flexibility: Enjoy the best of both worlds—collaborative office days when it counts, balanced with the freedom to work from home.
  • Achieve Work-Life Balance and Flexibility: Work in an environment where you're trusted and empowered to work independently, while still having the support you need to deliver your best. Here, flexibility isn't just a perk—its how we help you perform at your best, without sacrificing life outside of work.
  • Open Culture: Your voice matters, we encourage proactive communication and fresh ideas.
  • Supportive Team: From your very first day to every career milestone, we've got your back—with long-term growth and projects you can truly thrive in.
  • Learn and Grow: Training, coaching, and international opportunities to level up your skills and career
  • Be part of a B-Corp company that puts people and planet first while creating meaningful impact.

Please note: This role is remote; however, we require candidates to be based locally in the Philippines. This is to support occasional onsite activities such as team events, client meetings, or equipment handover. Additionally, local residency is necessary for compliance with Philippines labor laws and employment regulations.

Why work for Sharesource?

Our clients come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire hundreds of skillful individuals from a wide variety of backgrounds, genders, and personalities to live out our diverse culture and make a positive impact on the world!

Our 5 Values:

  • Make a social impact: We balance our work for client teams and for society by constantly making a positive impact.
  • Be proactive: We encourage brave thinking and continuous improvement, and drive change through action.
  • Create value: We create measurable values for our stakeholders: our teams, partners, suppliers, investors, and communities.
  • Be fair, open and honest: We foster equality and inclusivity in a supportive environment that embraces diversity and celebrates achievements.
  • Add fun, passion and love: We priorities fun and passion, fostering higher engagement and a positive can-do attitude.

What to Expect in the Process

  • You'll go through 2-3 interviews plus a possible assessment with our client partner. This includes an initial chat, a culture-fit interview, and 1–2 conversations with our awesome client. The whole process usually takes 2-3 weeks, but we'll let you know if things need to move quicker.
  • Our best advice? Be yourself and enjoy the conversations. Well keep you updated every step of the way, and you're always welcome to reach out for updates anytime.
  • If all goes well, well complete reference checks and requirements quickly—so we can get that job offer to you without delay.

We would be grateful if you have these already:

jobs.excerpt: English description below À propos d'IngenoIngeno est une firme de services professionnels basée au Québec, spécialisée dans le développement de solutions logicielles sur mesure et de solutions en intelligence artificielle, avec un focus sur les secteurs manufacturier et de la défense.
jobs.description:
English description below

À propos d'Ingeno

Ingeno est une firme de services professionnels basée au Québec, spécialisée dans le développement de solutions logicielles sur mesure et de solutions en intelligence artificielle, avec un focus sur les secteurs manufacturier et de la défense. Nous accompagnons nos clients dans la conception, la construction et la mise à l'échelle de systèmes critiques, en combinant une expertise technique pointue à une approche pragmatique axée sur la livraison et la valeur ajoutée.

Aperçu du poste

L'architecte principal(e) partage son temps entre le leadership technique sur les mandats clients les plus complexes et la standardisation des pratiques, des processus et de l'orientation technique à l'échelle de l'entreprise. À ce titre, ce rôle exerce une influence directe sur les décisions technologiques et l'orientation technique d'Ingeno.

Responsabilités

L'architecte principal(e) combine le leadership technique sur les mandats clients les plus complexes avec la responsabilité de standardiser les pratiques, les processus et l'orientation technique à l'échelle de l'entreprise, couvrant les domaines suivants :

1. Livraison client

  • Agir à titre d'architecte principal(e) sur les mandats clients les plus complexes et à plus haut risque d'Ingeno
  • Servir de point d'escalade technique pour les équipes de livraison confrontées à des enjeux d'architecture
  • Diriger l'architecture de solution durant les phases de découverte stratégique et de conception de solution pour les comptes stratégiques
  • Effectuer la révision des risques techniques et l'approbation des énoncés de travail (SOW) dépassant un seuil de complexité défini

2. Cycle de développement logiciel

  • Détenir et faire évoluer en continu le cadre de développement en cinq phases d'Ingeno (découverte stratégique, conception de solution, planification de livraison, développement itératif, déploiement et transition)
  • Diriger la révision d'architecture pour les projets dépassant un seuil de taille ou de complexité défini
  • Détenir le cadre de mesure de performance et d'indicateurs par phase; s'assurer que les leçons tirées des rétrospectives et post-mortems se traduisent en améliorations concrètes des processus

3. Estimation

  • Standardiser la méthodologie d'estimation à travers les équipes de livraison
  • Réviser et approuver les estimations dépassant un seuil défini avant leur communication aux clients

4. Utilisation de l'IA

  • Définir les stratégies d'utilisation de l'IA à l'interne et pour les projets clients
  • Optimiser les processus de développement produit et logiciel en faisant levier sur l’IA
  • Définir les garde-fous et les bonnes pratiques pour une utilisation sécuritaire et responsable de l'IA, incluant la gestion des données client sensibles
  • Établir les standards d'intégration et d'interopérabilité pour les composants d'IA (LLM, RAG, bases de données vectorielles, modèles de ML), tant à l'interne que dans les solutions clients
  • Superviser les décisions de type « bâtir ou acheter » pour les outils et l'infrastructure d'IA
  • Maintenir des standards d'utilisation de l'IA cohérents à travers l'organisation

5. Stratégie technologique

  • Établir, en collaboration avec la haute direction, les stratégies technologiques de l'entreprise et participer à leur implantation

6. Développement des compétences

  • Contribuer à l'évolution de l'échelle de compétences techniques (la propriété demeure celle des chefs d'équipe et de la direction)

7. Soutien aux ventes

  • Fournir, au besoin, un appui à la solution technique et à la révision des risques des SOW pour les opportunités complexes

Qualifications requises

  • Baccalauréat ou maîtrise en informatique, en génie logiciel ou dans un domaine connexe, ou expérience équivalente
  • 12 années ou plus d'expérience en génie logiciel, incluant une portion significative en architecture
  • Feuille de route éprouvée dans la conception de systèmes complexes de niveau production, en contexte de services-conseils
  • Expérience concrète d'intégration de composants d'IA/ML (LLM, RAG, bases de données vectorielles) dans des systèmes en production
  • Expérience de standardisation des pratiques de génie logiciel à travers plusieurs équipes (cycle de développement, estimation, qualité du code)
  • Bilinguisme (français/anglais), à l'oral et à l'écrit — Ingeno opère dans les deux langues
  • Expérience dans des secteurs réglementés ou à haute conformité (p. ex. défense, santé) constitue un atout
  • Excellentes habiletés de communication, à l'aise autant avec les équipes de livraison qu'avec la haute direction

Attributs clés

  • Pragmatique — sait équilibrer la rigueur de standardisation avec l'autonomie et la rapidité des équipes de livraison
  • Leader technique crédible qui demeure impliqué sur le terrain, au-delà d'un rôle purement stratégique
  • À l'aise de porter un double mandat et de protéger le temps alloué à chacune des deux facettes du rôle
  • Bon instinct de gestion du changement pour favoriser l'adoption de nouveaux standards sans lourdeur excessive

========================================================================

About Ingeno

Ingeno is a Québec-based professional services firm delivering custom software and AI solutions, with a focus on the manufacturing and defence sectors. We partner with our clients to design, build, and scale mission-critical systems, combining deep technical expertise with a pragmatic approach focused on delivery and added value.

Position Overview

The Principal Architect splits their time between hands-on technical leadership on Ingeno's most complex client engagements and standardizing practices, processes, and technical direction across the firm. In this capacity, the role has a direct impact on Ingeno's technological decisions and direction.

Responsibilities

The Principal Architect combines hands-on technical leadership on Ingeno's most complex client engagements with responsibility for standardizing practices, processes, and technical direction across the firm, covering the following areas:

1. Client Delivery

  • Serve as principal/lead architect on Ingeno's most complex and highest-risk client engagements
  • Act as the technical escalation point for delivery teams facing architecture-level challenges
  • Lead solution architecture during the Strategic Discovery and Solution Design phases on flagship accounts
  • Provide technical risk review and sign-off on statements of work (SOWs) above a defined complexity threshold

2. Software Development Lifecycle

  • Own and continuously evolve Ingeno's five-phase Development Process Framework (Strategic Discovery, Solution Design, Delivery Planning, Iterative Development, Deployment & Transition)
  • Run architecture review for projects above a defined size/complexity threshold
  • Own the phase-level KPI and performance measurement framework; ensure lessons from project retrospectives and post-mortems translate into concrete process improvements

3. Estimation

  • Standardize estimation methodology across delivery teams
  • Review and approve estimates above a defined threshold before they are communicated to clients

4. AI Usage

  • Define AI usage strategies for internal operations and client projects
    • Define guardrails and best practices for safe, responsible AI use, including handling of sensitive client data
    • Establish integration and interoperability standards for AI components (LLMs, RAG, vector databases, ML models), across both internal and client-facing solutions
    • Oversee build-vs-buy decisions for AI tooling and infrastructure
    • Maintain consistent AI usage standards across the organization

5. Technology Strategy

  • Establish the company's technology strategies in collaboration with senior leadership and participate in their implementation

6. Competency Development

  • Contribute to the evolution of the technical competency ladder (ownership remains with team leads and leadership)

7. Sales Support

  • Provide technical solutioning and SOW risk review for complex opportunities, as required

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience
  • 12+ years of software engineering experience, including significant time in architecture roles
  • Proven track record architecting complex, production-grade systems in a client services / consulting environment
  • Direct experience integrating AI/ML components (LLMs, RAG, vector databases) into production systems
  • Experience standardizing engineering practices across multiple teams (SDLC, estimation, code quality)
  • Bilingual (French/English), spoken and written — Ingeno operates in both languages
  • Experience in regulated or high-compliance sectors (e.g., defence, healthcare) is an asset
  • Strong communication skills, comfortable working with both hands-on delivery teams and executive leadership

Key Attributes

  • Pragmatic — balances standardization rigor with delivery-team autonomy and speed
  • Credible technical leader who remains hands-on, not purely strategic
  • Comfortable holding a dual mandate and protecting time for both sides of the role
  • Strong change-management instincts to drive adoption of new standards without heavy-handedness

The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking an experienced, visionary entrepreneur to co-found its next B2B AI venture with us. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

This opportunity is open to repeat entrepreneurs who may already have an early-stage idea they're exploring, or who want to partner with FutureSight to validate, shape, and launch a new venture together. You will work alongside our team to test and refine ideas, kill the ones that don't hold up, and lead the one that does from inception through fundraising and beyond.

This is a full-time, exclusive commitment to building and owning a single B2B AI venture from the ground up.

About FutureSight

FutureSight is a leading venture builder that co-creates world-class software companies with values-driven entrepreneurs from inception to exit. We are a team of founders, operators and designers with experience successfully bringing software to market at scale.

You’ll co-create with a proven studio team, led by John Carbrey (4x entrepreneur, $100M ARR), Krista LaRiviere (3x exited, E&Y Top Women Entrepreneur), Alan Smith (Strategyzer co-founder, $120M in products built), Prathna Ramesh (former MD of Maple Leaf Angels, $275M in follow-on capital), and Johnny Tong (0-to-1 builder, acquired by SAP and Stripe) bring a rare combination of operator exits, institutional investing, and AI product depth.

The Partnership

  • Founder equity with meaningful ownership from inception
  • Pre-seed capital committed by FutureSight for early hires and MVP development, with potential for follow-on funding
  • Venture building resources, including embedded design, engineering, growth, and fundraising support from day one
  • Investor and advisor network across vertical AI and early-stage capital markets
  • A true co-creation model in which you operate as CEO with FutureSight's cross-functional team as your partner

What you'll own

As Co-Founder & CEO, you will set the venture's direction and lead its execution.

  • Validation — Partner with our team on early-stage testing, validation, and refinement of the business idea, including prototyping to validate and sell potential solutions, with the readiness to kill ideas that don't hold up before committing to the one that does
  • Strategy — Define the ICP, pricing model, and product positioning for the validated opportunity
  • Customer Development — Lead pilots, convert them to paid engagements, and build the go-to-market motion
  • Product — Partner with the FutureSight product and engineering team to ship V1 and iterate on user feedback
  • Capital — Lead the pre-seed and seed raises, supported by FutureSight's network and traction
  • Team — Recruit and lead the founding team, and establish the cultural foundation of the company

  • Previous founding experience at a venture-backed company

How to Apply

Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, and a brief note on why this venture aligns with your goals as a founder. We will move quickly for the right candidate.

FutureSight is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Solution Innovation
jobs.excerpt: Our team members are at the heart of everything we do.
jobs.description:
Our team members are at the heart of everything we do. At Cencora, we are united in our responsibility to create healthier futures, and every person here is essential to us being able to deliver on that purpose. If you want to make a difference at the center of health, come join our innovative company and help us improve the lives of people and animals everywhere. Apply today!

Job Details

The Program Manager, Solution Innovation is responsible for managing the solution innovation workstreams, governance process, and operating pathway that moves ideas, concepts, pilots, and solution opportunities through disciplined evaluation, prioritization, stage-gate review, roadmap alignment, and execution tracking. Reporting to the Group Product Owner – Solution Innovation and Design, this role ensures the solution innovation pathway is clearly documented, consistently applied, transparent to stakeholders, and aligned with CPS product and solution development priorities.

This role supports product strategy execution by translating innovation priorities, market insights, customer needs, and leadership decisions into structured program plans, committee routines, stage-gate deliverables, roadmap updates, and implementation requirements. The role maintains the operating infrastructure that enables the Group Product Owner, Product Development Committee, solution teams, commercialization partners, analytics, legal/compliance, operations, and other stakeholders to evaluate and advance innovation opportunities in a repeatable and measurable way.

This role does not own product strategy or final product prioritization decisions; instead, it owns the program management discipline, governance administration, process documentation, stakeholder coordination, dependency tracking, and reporting routines required to support timely and effective solution innovation decisions. The Program Manager ensures innovation items are organized, stage-gate materials are complete, committee decisions are captured, roadmap and backlog data are maintained, and risks, issues, decisions, and follow-ups are visible and actionable.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities:

Solution Innovation Pathway Management

  • Implement, maintain, and continuously improve the Solution Innovation pathway from idea intake through discovery, validation, pilot/proof-of-concept, scale recommendation, roadmap transition, and post-decision follow-up.

  • Translate the priorities of the Group Product Owner – Solution Innovation and Design into structured program plans, operating routines, meeting cadences, decision checkpoints, documentation requirements, and stakeholder deliverables.

  • Define and maintain pathway documentation including process maps, stage-gate expectations, intake criteria, readiness checklists, decision rights, artifacts, intake forms, governance calendars, and communication protocols.

  • Ensure the innovation pathway is applied consistently across solution workstreams while remaining flexible enough to support different types of innovation opportunities, pilots, prototypes, and business cases.

  • Identify process bottlenecks, ambiguous handoffs, inconsistent documentation, and decision delays; recommend and implement improvements to increase clarity, speed, accountability, and stakeholder alignment.

Product Development Committee Operations and Governance

  • Coordinate and manage the Product Development Committee operating rhythm, including agenda planning, materials intake, pre-read preparation, meeting facilitation support, decision documentation, action tracking, and follow-up communication.

  • Support the Group Product Owner in preparing innovation concepts, backlog recommendations, stage-gate materials, and roadmap updates for Product Development Committee review.

  • Ensure committee decisions, open questions, risks, approvals, deferrals, and next steps are captured accurately and communicated to appropriate stakeholders.

  • Maintain governance records and decision logs to support transparency, traceability, and accountability across innovation pathway decisions.

  • Monitor adherence to Product Development Committee processes and recommend refinements to governance structure, meeting cadence, decision standards, and escalation pathways.

Innovation Backlog and Roadmap Administration

  • Maintain the innovation backlog with current information on opportunity status, owner, strategic theme, stage-gate status, customer value, business rationale, dependencies, risks, target timing, and next actions.

  • Support roadmap administration for solution innovation initiatives by tracking milestones, sequencing, stage transitions, prioritization inputs, and linkage to CPS solution strategy.

  • Partner with the Group Product Owner and product stakeholders to ensure innovation backlog and roadmap data reflect current priorities, leadership decisions, capacity constraints, and dependencies.

  • Develop and maintain reporting views that allow leadership to understand backlog health, pathway throughput, stage-gate progress, pipeline constraints, and upcoming decisions.

  • Identify stale, duplicative, misaligned, or blocked backlog items and coordinate with owners to recommend disposition, refresh, escalation, or removal.

Stage-Gate Process Execution and Artifact Management

  • Manage stage-gate execution across solution innovation workstreams, including intake readiness, discovery documentation, problem statements, VOC summaries, pilot objectives, success criteria, feasibility inputs, risk assessments, and transition recommendations.

  • Ensure required artifacts are developed, updated, reviewed, and stored in the appropriate location before stage-gate reviews and committee discussions.

  • Coordinate with Product Owners, Product Managers, solution development teams, analytics, operations, commercialization, legal/compliance, finance, and other stakeholders to gather required stage-gate inputs.

  • Track gate decisions and follow-up actions, ensuring workstream owners understand expectations required to progress to the next stage.

  • Continuously evaluate whether stage-gate criteria and artifacts are fit for purpose and recommend changes that improve decision quality, speed, and consistency.

Innovation Workstream Program Management

  • Manage multiple solution innovation workstreams by developing and tracking workplans, milestones, deliverables, dependencies, risks, issues, communications, and stakeholder commitments.

  • Support cross-functional teams in defining scope, timelines, deliverables, resource needs, sequencing, decision points, and escalation paths for innovation initiatives.

  • Coordinate workstream planning and execution across Product, Solution Development, Commercialization, Enablement, Analytics, Operations, Legal/Compliance, Finance, and customer-facing functions.

  • Develop clear status updates and program views that communicate progress, blockers, decisions needed, upcoming milestones, and risks to the Group Product Owner and relevant stakeholders.

  • Proactively anticipate risks, dependency conflicts, resource constraints, and scope creep; present mitigation options and escalation recommendations to leadership.

Requirements, Business Case, and Product Lifecycle Support

  • Support development of product and solution requirements, enhancement plans, business cases, and lifecycle recommendations by coordinating inputs from product, strategy, analytics, customers, and cross-functional stakeholders.

  • Help translate innovation strategy, market insights, customer needs, and committee decisions into actionable product plans, implementation requirements, stage-gate deliverables, and roadmap updates.

  • Coordinate operating cost, ROI, risk, readiness, adoption, and performance inputs needed to support innovation prioritization and product lifecycle decisions.

  • Support transition of validated innovation concepts into product roadmaps, commercialization planning, operational readiness, enablement planning, or scale recommendations as appropriate.

  • Ensure service expectations, operational readiness requirements, customer support implications, and risk considerations are documented for innovation opportunities moving toward pilot or launch.

Stakeholder Communication and Executive Reporting

  • Develop and maintaintimely, accurate, and concise reporting on innovation pipeline status, Product Development Committee decisions, stage-gate progress, roadmap updates, risks, issues, and action items.

  • Facilitate stakeholder discussions to build alignment on innovation priorities, process expectations, implementation approaches, dependencies, and next steps.

  • Prepare materials, dashboards, status reports, decision summaries, and executive updates for the Group Product Owner, Product Development Committee, CPS leadership, and cross-functional stakeholders.

  • Use appropriate communication tools and formats to keep stakeholders informed and aligned across complex and interconnected innovation workstreams.

  • Translate complex process, product, and dependency information into clear summaries for both technical and non-technical audiences.

Continuous Improvement, SOPs, and Process Discipline

  • Develop, maintain, and improve standard operating procedures, templates, process documents, governance tools, communication practices, and stage-gate artifacts supporting the Solution Innovation pathway.

  • Conduct periodic process reviews and lessons-learned sessions to identify successful and unsuccessful pathway elements and apply improvements to future workstreams.

  • Identify opportunities for efficiency, process improvement, documentation quality, tool optimization, governance simplification, and improved stakeholder experience.

  • Implement repeatable program management practices that improve visibility, accountability, decision quality, data integrity, and workflow speed across solution innovation activities.

  • Promote consistent use of program management and product management tools, ensuring information is complete, current, and usable for decision-making.

Risk, Issue, Dependency, and Resource Tracking

  • Maintain risk, issue, dependency, and decision logs for solution innovation workstreams and governance processes.

  • Partner with stakeholders to identify mitigation plans, escalation needs, and alternative approaches when timelines, resources, scope, or dependencies are at risk.

  • Track resource needs, capacity constraints, and cross-functional dependencies that impact workstream progression or stage-gate readiness.

  • Use judgment and discretion in escalating issues to the Group Product Owner and relevant leadership when innovation progress, stakeholder commitments, or decision timing are at risk.

  • Ensureinnovation workstream risks and dependencies are visible in roadmap, backlog, and committee reporting.

Compliance and Other

  • Ensure solution innovation governance, documentation, and workstream processes comply with applicable company policies, privacy/security expectations, legal/compliance standards, and documentation requirements.

  • Perform related duties as assigned.

Experience and Educational Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree required in business administration, marketing, product management, project/program management, healthcare administration, information systems, engineering, or a related field; equivalent experience may be considered.

  • 6+ years of experience in product management, product strategy, program management, project management, business operations, innovation operations, or a related field required.

  • Experience managing cross-functional workstreams, governance processes, stage-gate models, product roadmaps, innovation pipelines, or product lifecycle processes preferred.

  • Experience supporting senior stakeholders, committees, governance forums, and executive reporting preferred.

  • Experience in healthcare, pharmacy services, technology-enabled services, product development, or portfolio/program management preferred.

  • Certification in agile, scrum, product management, project management, or program management preferred.

Minimum Skills, Knowledge, and Ability Requirements

  • Strong program and project management skills, including scope, schedule, milestone, dependency, risk, issue, and communication management.

  • Ability to manage multiple related workstreams directed toward common strategic objectives while maintaining reliable reporting and stakeholder alignment.

  • Strong understanding of product management concepts, including product strategy, roadmaps, requirements, business cases, lifecycle planning, go-to-market readiness, value metrics, and operational readiness.

  • Ability to facilitate stakeholder discussions, build alignment across competing priorities, and translate decisions into action plans and implementation requirements.

  • Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to maintain accurate documentation, decision logs, process artifacts, and governance records.

  • Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing with technical and non-technical audiences, senior stakeholders, cross-functional teams, and business partners.

  • Strong analytical, conceptual, and problem-solving skills with ability to evaluate program risks, process gaps, dependencies, and potential solutions.

  • Ability to create clear executive summaries, roadmap views, committee materials, status reports, dashboards, process documentation, and presentations.

  • Ability to use collaboration, product management, and program management tools to track work, communicate status, manage documentation, and maintain stakeholder visibility.

  • Ability to work independently, exercise judgment, manage ambiguity, prioritize effectively, and escalate issues appropriately.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including PowerPoint, Excel, Word, Outlook, and related project / program management or collaboration tools such as Jira, Confluence, Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Planner, or similar platforms preferred.

What Cencora offers

We provide compensation, benefits, and resources that enable a highly inclusive culture and support our team members’ ability to live with purpose every day. In addition to traditional offerings like medical, dental, and vision care, we also provide a comprehensive suite of benefits that focus on the physical, emotional, financial, and social aspects of wellness. This encompasses support for working families, which may include backup dependent care, adoption assistance, infertility coverage, family building support, behavioral health solutions, paid parental leave, and paid caregiver leave. To encourage your personal growth, we also offer a variety of training programs, professional development resources, and opportunities to participate in mentorship programs, employee resource groups, volunteer activities, and much more. jobs.title: Group Chief Compliance & Legal Officer
jobs.excerpt: Reporting LineReports directly to the CEO.  Leads a compliance function that includes the Group Paralegal (direct report) and all compliance personnel embedded across the CXM Group of Companies.
jobs.description:
Reporting Line

Reports directly to the CEO.

Leads a compliance function that includes the Group Paralegal (direct report) and all compliance personnel embedded across the CXM Group of Companies.

Location

Remote (EU timezone preferred)

This is a fully remote role. EU timezone alignment is preferred to ensure effective overlap with key offices across the CXM Group. Occasional travel may be required for regulator meetings and visits to regional teams.

General Purpose

CXM Group is building a compliance architecture across six business lines and multiple jurisdictions simultaneously — this role owns that build.

The group is at an inflection point: multiple licensing processes are running in parallel, including a Norwegian crypto exchange being structured for MiCA passporting, a South African broker-dealer acquisition, a VARA application in the UAE, and prospective acquisitions in LATAM and Southeast Asia. The CCO exists to hold this together — ensuring that a fast-moving, multi-asset, multi-jurisdictional expansion programme stays regulatorily sound, that new entities are acquired and integrated without compliance exposure, and that the group's licensing pipeline converts into durable, operating authorisations across FX, CFDs, crypto, prediction markets, prop trading, and education.

This is a role for someone who has operated across tier-one and emerging-market regimes simultaneously and has the regulator-facing credibility to show for it.

Specific Objectives

Build and deploy a group-wide compliance reporting framework

Within the first three months, establish a structured compliance reporting framework covering all regulated entities across the CXM Group — including defined reporting lines, cadences, and escalation paths that give the CEO and board clear, timely visibility of the group's regulatory posture.

Create an AI-enabled legal document database

Within six months, deliver a searchable, indexed, and cross-referenced repository of all legal documentation across the group — structured for AI-assisted retrieval so that agreements, licences, policies, and regulatory correspondence can be surfaced and compared at speed.

Establish and embed internal legal SLAs

Within the first three months, define and operationalise service-level agreements for all internal legal workflows: standard contract reviews turned in 24 hours; new contract drafting completed within 48 hours; policy creation on agreed timelines. Compliance with these SLAs to be tracked and reported.

Deploy legal and compliance risk monitoring tools

Within six months, implement risk monitoring tooling across all business verticals and target markets — covering FX, CFDs, crypto, prediction markets, prop trading, and education — providing structured, ongoing visibility of regulatory and legal risk exposure across the group.

Drive the live licensing and acquisition pipeline to defined milestones

Own delivery against the group's active regulatory and M&A programme: South African broker-dealer acquisition and VARA (UAE) licence obtained by Q3 2026; VARA application submitted by Q4 2026 and licence granted by Q3 2027; MiCA passporting for the Norwegian crypto exchange secured by Q2 2027; LATAM and Southeast Asia acquisition targets scoped and structured by Q1 2027.

Key Activities

Oversee group-wide legal and compliance communications

Manage all inbound and outbound communications across the compliance and legal function — ensuring consistency of position, appropriate escalation, and clear audit trails across all CXM Group entities.

Monitor brand, regulatory, and compliance risk

Run ongoing monitoring of online brand exposure and regulatory risk signals across all business verticals and target markets, using dedicated tooling to surface issues before they become regulatory events.

Research target markets and emerging regulatory requirements

Conduct structured research on new and existing jurisdictions — tracking legislative developments, regulatory guidance, and enforcement trends across FX, CFDs, crypto, prediction markets, prop trading, and education to keep the group's risk exposure visible and current.

Build and maintain reporting infrastructure with Ops and IT

Work cross-functionally with Operations and IT to design, implement, and maintain the compliance reporting systems and dashboards needed to give leadership real-time visibility of the group's regulatory posture.

Inventory, organise, and analyse all group legal agreements

Own the end-to-end legal document function: audit existing agreements across all entities, build and maintain the AI-enabled document repository, and ensure all contracts are indexed, cross-referenced, and accessible for rapid retrieval.

Manage regulatory relationships and respond to inquiries

Serve as the primary point of contact for regulators across all jurisdictions — preparing responses, managing ongoing dialogue, and coordinating regulator visits or meetings with appropriate precision and consistency.

Set and enforce contract throughput standards

Define the SLA framework for all internal legal workflows — 24 hours for standard contract reviews, 48 hours for new contract drafting — and hold the Group Paralegal and compliance staff accountable for delivery against those standards. The CCO personally handles high-stakes, novel, or regulator-facing agreements; standard throughput runs through the team.

Requirements

Key Competences

Two competences are non-negotiable (and typically take a decade of multi-jurisdictional work to build) — everything else can be ramped. If you don't have these, the rest of the profile doesn't matter.

Non-negotiable

Multi-jurisdictional regulatory knowledge

Demonstrated command of tier-one regimes (CySEC, FCA, NFA, ASIC) and offshore/emerging-market frameworks (UAE, Mauritius, Seychelles, SVG, Cambodia), with working knowledge of MiCA and crypto licensing regimes globally. This is the core of the mandate — live deals are already in motion.

Regulator-facing credibility

Confidence and competence in direct regulator engagement — managing inquiries, coordinating responses, and representing the group's compliance posture with consistency across jurisdictions. The group has active regulator relationships that need an owner from day one.

Strong advantage

M&A and licensing fluency

Ability to support acquisition structuring and entity integration from a compliance perspective — assessing regulatory exposure, coordinating with external counsel, and managing parallel licensing processes without dropping threads.

AI-enabled legal operations

Experience deploying AI tooling in legal workflows — document retrieval, contract review acceleration, risk monitoring — is a strong advantage. Candidates without a deployment track record must demonstrate a concrete plan for rapid adoption and the aptitude to execute it.

Function leadership and SLA ownership

Ability to set standards, delegate effectively, and hold a team accountable for throughput — running the contract and compliance function at scale without becoming the bottleneck. Personal involvement reserved for high-stakes, novel, or regulator-facing matters.

Likely Current Job

Chief Compliance Officer (multi-jurisdictional broker or crypto exchange)

The closest equivalent — already holding a CCO title across FX, CFDs, or crypto at a group with multiple regulated entities and active regulator relationships. If your current seat is steady-state and you're ready to own a live build across six asset classes and a dozen jurisdictions, this is the step up.

Head of Compliance (tier-one regulated broker)

One level below CCO at a CySEC, FCA, or ASIC-regulated firm — strong regulatory depth, ready to move into group-level ownership. If you've hit the ceiling of what a single-jurisdiction, single-entity compliance role can teach you, this is where the complexity scales.

Regulatory Affairs Director (fintech or crypto)

Licensing and regulator-facing experience across multiple jurisdictions, possibly without the full compliance function remit yet. If you've been the technical expert behind the licensing programme and want to own the outcome end-to-end, this is the mandate.

M&A Compliance Lead (financial services)

Embedded in acquisition structuring and entity integration at a PE-backed or multi-entity financial services group. If you've been supporting deals from the compliance side and want a seat where M&A fluency is a core expectation rather than a secondary contribution, this is it.

Senior Legal Counsel / Head of Legal (retail broker or crypto exchange)

Contract-heavy, regulator-facing, with compliance responsibility baked in — a common feeder at smaller multi-jurisdictional groups where legal and compliance sit close together. If you've been carrying both functions informally and want a title and mandate that reflects the actual scope, this role makes it official.

Benefits

Employer Value Proposition

Most CCO roles at this level are maintenance jobs — one regulator, one entity, one asset class. This one is not.

Genuine architectural ownership across six asset classes and a dozen jurisdictions

FX, CFDs, crypto, prediction markets, prop trading, and education — running simultaneously, across tier-one and emerging-market regimes, with live licensing and M&A deals already in motion. The compliance architecture doesn't exist yet at group level. You're building it. By the end of year one, you'll be able to say you built a multi-jurisdictional compliance architecture from scratch, closed live licensing deals across MiCA, VARA, and emerging markets simultaneously, and stood up an AI-enabled legal ops function before almost anyone in the segment has done it. That is a résumé paragraph no single-jurisdiction maintenance role can produce.

Direct line to the CEO — and the mandate authority that comes with it

This role reports directly to the CEO, not to a CLO or CFO. In a live licensing and M&A environment where decisions need to move fast, that access matters: no layers between compliance judgment and executive action. Many group-level CCO seats don't offer this — this one does.

A live deal pipeline, not a hypothetical one

MiCA passporting, VARA in the UAE, a South African broker-dealer acquisition, and prospective acquisitions in LATAM and Southeast Asia — these are active, not aspirational. You'll be in the room on deals that will define the group's regulatory footprint for the next decade.

A first-mover opportunity in AI-enabled legal ops

The mandate includes building the AI-enabled legal ops function at group level — document retrieval, contract throughput acceleration, risk monitoring — in a segment where almost nobody has done it yet at this scale. If you've started deploying AI in legal workflows and want a seat where that capability shapes the entire function, this is it.

Group-level mandate, not a function-level seat

Functional authority over compliance personnel across all CXM Group entities. The scope matches the title — and the title reflects the actual job.

Fully remote

No relocation. No commute. Occasional travel when it matters — regulator meetings, regional teams — and otherwise, work from wherever you do your best thinking.

A genuinely uncommon opportunity

Multi-asset, multi-jurisdictional, M&A-active, AI-forward, fully remote — and at a scale that is still early enough for you to leave a visible mark. Roles with this combination of complexity and ownership don't come up often.

Compensation

Compensation is bespoke to the hire. We'd rather understand what you bring to the table and have a direct conversation about expectations than anchor the discussion prematurely. The package will be competitive with the scope of the mandate and consist of base + bonus that is tied to hitting agreed KPIs.

Assessment Process

This process is designed to match the weight of the mandate. A seat with this scope — live licensing, active M&A, and a compliance architecture being built from scratch — deserves a rigorous hire, and we make no apology for that. Every stage is purposeful, and every interviewer is there for a reason.

Group Legal Counsel — regulatory and legal technical depth across jurisdictions, plus practical M&A case questions to assess acquisition structuring judgment.

CHRO — leadership style, function-building track record, and cultural alignment with CXM Group's operating style.

CEO — strategic judgment, mandate clarity, and the candidate's vision for the compliance architecture they'd build and own.

Board members — select Board involvement at final stage, focused on governance credibility and long-term fit at group level.

The full process is designed to run within one month. We move quickly and respect that your time is finite — every stage is as much your opportunity to assess CXM as ours to assess you. If you take your next move as seriously as we take this hire, that's exactly the kind of conversation we want to have.

The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Weli, a B2B WealthTech venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

Weli is an AI-native operations platform purpose-built for wealth management firms. It plugs directly into the CRM, portfolio management, and custodian systems firms already run, and executes the back-office work behind every account, account opening, money transfer, trade coordination, and compliance routing. Every wealth management firm already staffs an Operations function to do this work, typically at a ratio of roughly one Operations person to every three advisors, and that function is chronically stretched: slow, error-prone, and unable to give any single advisor's book the full attention it deserves. Weli is built for the firm's back office.

Market Context

Weli's customers are independent and hybrid RIAs, firms built around senior advisors who own their own client books and lean on a small, shared operations team to execute everything behind the scenes. It's a large and fast-growing world. There are roughly 300,000 wealth and financial advisors in the US, and the independent channel has been on a two-decade climb, from under a fifth of the industry's assets in 2007 to 27% today, on track for nearly a third by 2028.

Growth is outpacing the operations layer built to support it. The industry's leading benchmarking study found 78% of RIA firms were actively hiring last year just to keep up with capacity constraints, and most firms add a full new hire for every $360,000 of revenue growth, an expensive, linear way to scale a business that should compound. In our own interviews, one managing partner put a number on it directly: his firm could roughly triple its assets under management with its current advisor headcount if operations could keep pace. That gap, real, quantifiable, and largely unaddressed by today's AI tools, is Weli's opportunity.

About FutureSight

FutureSight is a leading venture builder that co-creates world-class software companies with values-driven entrepreneurs from inception to exit. We are a team of founders, operators and designers with experience successfully bringing software to market at scale.

You’ll co-create with a proven venture building team, led by John Carbrey (4x entrepreneur, $100M ARR), Krista LaRiviere (3x exited, E&Y Top Women Entrepreneur), Alan Smith (Strategyzer co-founder, $120M in products built), Prathna Ramesh (former MD of Maple Leaf Angels, $275M in follow-on capital), and Johnny Tong (0-to-1 builder, acquired by SAP and Stripe) bring a rare combination of operator exits, institutional investing, and AI product depth.

The Partnership

  • Founder equity with meaningful ownership from inception
  • Pre-seed capital committed by FutureSight for early hires and MVP development, with potential for follow-on funding
  • Venture building resources, including embedded design, engineering, growth, and fundraising support from day one
  • Investor and advisor network across fintech and early-stage capital markets
  • A true co-creation model in which you operate as CEO with FutureSight’s cross-functional team as your partner

What You’ll Own

As Co-Founder & CEO, you will set the venture's direction and lead its execution.

  • Strategy — Refine the ICP, pricing model, and product positioning
  • Customer Development — Lead pilots with RIA and wealth management firms, convert them to paid engagements, and build the go-to-market motion
  • Product — Partner with the FutureSight product and engineering team to ship V1 and iterate on user feedback
  • Capital — Lead the seed raise, supported by FutureSight's network and traction
  • Team — Recruit and lead a cohesive founding team, and establish the cultural foundation of the company

Co-Founder Profile

  • Previous founding experience at a venture-backed company
  • Demonstrated success in B2B SaaS go-to-market, including sales and customer engagement
  • Fundraising fluency, with the ability to develop investor narratives and close capital
  • Proven ability to attract, develop, and retain top talent
  • Clear-eyed understanding of the risks and demands of co-founding a venture-backed company
  • Direct exposure to wealth management, RIA operations, and financial services compliance, with the credibility and relationships to navigate the industry's regulatory landscape and sell into established firms

How to Apply

Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, and a brief note on why this venture aligns with your goals as a founder. We will move quickly for the right candidate.

FutureSight is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences.
