jobs.description:
At Algolia, we’re proud to be a pioneer and market leader in AI Search, empowering 18,000+ businesses to deliver blazing-fast, predictive search and browse experiences at internet scale. Every week, we power over 30 billion search requests — four times more than Microsoft Bing, Yahoo, Baidu, Yandex, and DuckDuckGo combined.

In 2021, we raised $150 million in Series D funding, quadrupling our valuation to $2.25 billion. This strong foundation enables us to keep investing in our market-leading platform and serving incredible customers like Under Armour, PetSmart, Stripe, Gymshark, and Walgreens.

Algolia is seeking a detail-oriented and proactive GTM Data Operations Manager to join our Revenue Operations team to ensure our customer and prospect data is trusted, governed, and operationally sound across the entire GTM ecosystem.

The GTM Data Operations Manager owns the operational health, governance, and integrity of customer and prospect data across the company's go-to-market systems. The role is responsible for ensuring Leads, Contacts, Accounts, and related GTM data are accurate, enriched, synchronized, and governed to enable effective execution across Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, and Analytics.

The role partners closely with GTM Systems, Marketing/Sales Operations, Analytics, Customer Success Operations, and Data / Systems Engineering to maintain reliable data foundations, support automation and AI native workflows, and continuously improve data quality across the revenue technology stack..

About You

You're passionate about building high-quality data foundations that enable great business decisions, and you enjoy solving complex operational problems across systems and teams. You're organized, analytical, and detail-oriented, comfortable owning your area independently while collaborating across Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, Data / Systems Engineering, and Revenue Operations. You take pride in creating operational excellence behind the scenes, building reliable processes, documenting standards, and continuously improving the quality and integrity of GTM data. Above all, you understand that trusted data is the foundation for exceptional customer experiences, operational efficiency, analytics, AI, and business growth.

Key Responsibilities

  • Data Stewardship, Governance & Quality
    • Act as the operational steward for customer and prospect data (Leads, Contacts, and Accounts) across the GTM ecosystem, ensuring data is accurate, complete, consistent, and trusted.
    • Own operational governance for customer and prospect data across Salesforce, Marketo, Demandbase and related integrated GTM systems, including data quality standards, telemetry requirements, validation rules, field governance, and operational policies.
    • Execute recurring hygiene programs including deduplication, standardization, enrichment validation, and lifecycle management; partner with system owners to resolve data integrity issues.
    • Partner with business stakeholders to evaluate requests for new fields, objects, and data standards while maintaining integrity and consistency across the ecosystem.
    • Identify data quality risks, drive remediation efforts, and support the evolution of GTM data models as business needs change.
  • Data Enrichment & Identity Management:
    • Administer enrichment workflows across GTM platforms.
    • Monitor enrichment success rates and troubleshoot failures.
    • Maintain enrichment mappings and integrations.
    • Partner with GTM Technology on vendor implementations and improvements.
  • Data Operations:
    • Monitor critical integrations between Salesforce, Marketo, Demandbase and other GTM systems.
    • Investigate synchronization failures and scope / support implementation to minimize future failures.
    • Ensure customer and prospect data flows reliably across systems.
    • Support operational readiness for new fields, objects and integrations as well as deprecation of those no longer needed.
  • Operational Excellence:
    • Support complex audience segmentation requests requiring deep knowledge of GTM data structures.
    • Provide operational data support for strategic GTM initiatives as required.
    • Ensure GTM data is structured and governed to support scalable reporting, automation, and AI-powered workflows.
    • Document data processes and governance standards.
    • Develop dashboards to monitor data quality health.
    • Identify automation opportunities that improve operational efficiency.
    • Support audit and compliance requests.

Qualifications

  • 3+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, Marketing Operations, Sales Operations, CRM Administration, Data Operations, or a related GTM operations function.
  • Located in US ET or CT
  • Strong working knowledge of Salesforce and CRM data management principles, including Leads, Contacts, Accounts, and related data structures.
  • Experience working with marketing automation platforms (e.g., Marketo) and GTM data platforms and enrichment technologies.
  • Familiarity with SQL and data warehouse concepts (e.g., Hex, Databricks, ThoughtSpot, etc) is a plus.
  • Understanding of CRM architecture, lead lifecycle management, data enrichment, and system integrations across the GTM technology stack.
  • Experience maintaining data quality through governance, validation rules, deduplication, standardization, and operational data hygiene.
  • Working knowledge of APIs, webhooks, and system integrations, with the ability to troubleshoot data synchronization issues across multiple platforms.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and root cause analysis skills with exceptional attention to detail.
  • Excellent organizational, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities independently.
  • Experience documenting processes, identifying automation opportunities, and continuously improving operational workflows.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Salesforce Administrator certification or equivalent hands-on experience.
  • Experience with GTM data platforms such as Demandbase, 6sense, ZoomInfo, Clearbit, Apollo, or similar technologies.
  • Experience supporting enterprise B2B SaaS go-to-market organizations.
  • Familiarity with AI-enabled workflows, modern data governance practices, and enterprise GTM technology ecosystems.

The above is not an exhaustive list of duties and behaviors expected of this role. The company reserves the right to amend or delete with or without notice in line with change in business needs.

Algolia does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, military status, veteran status, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law.

$120,000—$148,000 USD

Algolia’s flexible workplace model is designed to empower all Algolians to fulfill our mission to power search and discovery with ease. About Energy Exemplar

In an era where the world is rapidly advancing towards a cleaner future through decarbonization, Energy Exemplar’s mission lies in ‘Empowering Transformative Energy Decisions’. Founded in 1999 in Adelaide, Australia, our award-winning software portfolio encompassing the modeling and simulation platform PLEXOS®, Aurora, and Adapt2, is trusted by innovative organizations across the globe. Through our technology and people, we strive to enable stakeholders from across the entire energy value chain to revolutionize the energy ecosystem and to collaboratively plan and execute for a sustainable energy future with unprecedented clarity, speed, and innovation.

Our impact is global and is being recognized across the industry. Some of our recent accolades include:

  • SaaS Company of the Year (2025) – Global Business Tech Awards.
  • Environmental Impact Award (2025) – E+E Leaders Awards.
  • IPPAI (Independent Power Producers Association of India) Power Awards (2025) - Winners
  • Finalist: Platts Global Energy Awards (2024) – Grid Edge category
  • Finalist: Reuters Global Energy Transition Awards (2024) – Technologies of Change
  • Top 50 Marketing Team (2024) – Voted by the public at the ICON Awards.

How We Work

Energy Exemplar is growing fast around 30% year on year and, that growth is driven by how we work. We trust our team to deliver great results from wherever they work best, whether that’s at home, in the office, or on the move.

We’re a global team that values ownership, integrity, and innovation. You’ll be supported to balance work and life in a way that works for you, and empowered to take initiative, solve problems, and make an impact, regardless of your background, location, or role.

Our four core values, Customer Success, One Global Team, Integrity & Ownership, and Innovation Excellence aren’t just words. They show up in how we collaborate, how we solve, and how we grow together.

About the Position

The Senior Energy Market Analyst, part of the Americas – Data and Insights team, will support Energy Exemplar’s growth in North America by identifying customer use cases, shaping go-to-market strategies, and providing thought leadership. Acting as a subject matter expert, they will understand customer challenges, propose solutions and develop products using Energy Exemplar tools and dataset.

The role is heavily focused on modelling, requiring expertise in energy market fundamentals. The analyst will build and oversee production of energy market models using PLEXOS. Candidates should have strong modelling skills, fundamental nodal modelling experience, customer engagement abilities, and a proactive, adaptable mindset.

  • Hands on modeling experience in several ISOs (eg ERCOT)
  • Experience with nodal power flow modeling and ability to discuss nodal concept such as LMPs, congestion, contingencies, LODF, etc.
  • Self-Starter and ability to work independently
  • 7+ years of experience with direct Energy Modeling and Power Market Analysis
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to research and learn new techniques
  • Experience in creating and analyzing energy data sets for power models
  • Production cost market modeling knowledge and experience
  • Experience with nodal market modeling is required

Remote | Full-time | 40-hours/week
Rate: $7 to $8/hour, with the final rate to be determined during the final interview.

About Pillar Health Solutions ()

Pillar Health Solutions is a growing healthcare company that partners with medical practices to provide insurance-supported dietary and exercise counseling programs for patients.

Our model connects physicians and their patients with dietitians, virtual trainers, and operational support designed to improve patient engagement and continuity of care.

We are entering an important growth stage and are looking for a Business Development & Operations Lead who can help expand our physician partnerships while strengthening the operational systems and client experience supporting that growth.

This is not a traditional back-office Operations Manager position.

We are looking for someone who can operate as a trusted extension of the leadership team: part business developer, part client success leader, part operator, and part strategic problem solver.

What You Will Own

Physician Acquisition & Business Growth

A major priority for this role is helping Pillar Health Solutions grow its network of physician and medical-practice partners.

You will:

  • Develop and execute practical strategies for attracting new physician and clinic partnerships

  • Identify opportunities to reach physicians, practice owners, office managers, and other healthcare decision-makers

  • Support organic marketing and local-market growth initiatives

  • Help develop physician-facing messaging, success stories, testimonials, and other materials that strengthen Pillar's value proposition

  • Research new channels, tools, partnerships, and approaches for increasing qualified opportunities

You do not need to be a career marketer, but you should understand how businesses grow and be able to contribute thoughtful, executable ideas.

Discovery Calls & Client Conversion

You will help convert interested medical practices into active Pillar partners.

Responsibilities will include:

  • Conducting or facilitating discovery calls with prospective physician partners

  • Explaining Pillar's services and patient-support model confidently

  • Communicating fees, billing structure, workflow, and partnership expectations clearly

  • Understanding the prospective practice's needs and identifying how Pillar can support them

  • Following up on opportunities and moving qualified prospects toward partnership

  • Continuously improving the discovery and conversion process based on feedback and results

Success in this position requires someone who is comfortable speaking directly with physicians, business owners, and senior decision-makers.

Physician, Patient & Program Operations

Once partnerships are established, you will help ensure that the experience remains strong for physicians and patients.

You will:

  • Serve as a key operational contact for physician partners

  • Monitor feedback from physicians and patients and take appropriate action

  • Coordinate with dietitians, virtual trainers, administrative staff, and virtual assistants

  • Support thoughtful matching between patients, dietitians, and virtual trainers when appropriate

  • Monitor patient engagement and identify concerns before they become escalations

  • Address service issues, complaints, and operational breakdowns

  • Help establish appropriate check-ins across the patient, dietitian, trainer, and physician relationship

Because patient experience can directly affect program continuation and business performance, this role requires someone who notices problems early and acts on them.

Founder Partnership & Executive Communication

You will work closely with Pillar Health Solutions leadership and should be comfortable communicating directly with a founder.

Initially, this may include a short daily business update meeting.

You will be expected to:

  • Prepare and drive the agenda rather than waiting for leadership to determine what should be discussed

  • Provide concise updates on projects, priorities, wins, risks, and unresolved issues

  • Explain not only what happened, but why it happened

  • Present recommended next steps and anticipated outcomes

  • Bring thoughtful options instead of open-ended problems

  • Negotiate priorities, expectations, and timelines when necessary

  • Provide respectful pushback when an idea may not be practical or when another priority should come first

  • Maintain transparency even when progress is slower than expected

We are looking for someone who can disagree professionally, communicate difficult information tactfully, and remain levelheaded under pressure.

AI & Technology Integration

Pillar wants AI to become a practical part of how the business operates.

You will:

  • Identify opportunities where AI can improve existing workflows

  • Research tools independently when a business problem arises

  • Use AI for research, analysis, documentation, communication, marketing support, and process improvement

We are looking for practical AI literacy, not simply someone who has used ChatGPT occasionally.

Operational Excellence

Although growth is an immediate priority, you will also help strengthen Pillar's operational foundation.

This may include:

  • Monitoring business and client KPIs

  • Improving workflows as operational gaps become visible

  • Maintaining accurate client, physician, patient, billing, and reporting information

  • Supporting consistent naming conventions and documentation

  • Reviewing processes for accuracy and efficiency

  • Creating or improving SOPs when a documented process is genuinely needed

  • Supporting scheduling, invoicing, reporting, and administrative coordination

  • Helping the company prepare operationally as the number of physician partners and patients increases

As Pillar grows, the scope of the position may expand into greater leadership and team-management responsibilities.

Required Qualifications

  • 2+ years of relevant experience across business operations, executive support, business development, customer success, healthcare operations, or a related field

  • Demonstrated experience working directly with senior leaders, founders, executives, physicians, or business owners

  • Strong client-facing communication and relationship-management skills

  • Ability to manage several responsibilities simultaneously in a startup or rapidly changing environment

  • Experience solving problems independently without waiting for detailed instructions

  • Strong written and verbal communication

  • Confidence facilitating meetings and business conversations

  • Ability to organize information and communicate progress clearly

  • Strong judgment when dealing with sensitive or difficult conversations

  • Comfortable learning unfamiliar systems and processes independently

  • Practical experience using AI tools for business or productivity

  • High attention to detail, particularly where client information, billing, reporting, or financial accuracy is involved

Highly Preferred

  • Experience supporting a startup founder or small-business owner

  • Experience conducting discovery, sales, partnership, or client-conversion calls

  • Exposure to physician acquisition or healthcare business development

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead Closeline, an AI-native mortgage origination venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

Customer discovery validates a real, recurring cost problem in this segment: lenders spend thousands of dollars to originate a single loan today, a cost that's climbed roughly 35% over the past three years, with up to 80% of that time spent on manual document review.

The US mortgage market processes roughly 6.5 million loans a year across close to 5,000 lending institutions, an estimated $3.25B in addressable software spend at Closeline's pricing. AECOM is seeking a highly motivated Authorized Special Status Species Field Biologist for immediate employment in the southern California desert regions.

This is a field-based, fully remote, on-call position requiring the ability to be local on field assignments for extended periods but linked to a Southern California-based office.

This position would support numerous natural resource projects with a focus on biological surveys and regulatory compliance monitoring primarily for Crotch’s Bumble Bee, Quino checkerspot butterfly, western spadefoot, and/or Stephen’s kangaroo rat with potential to assist with vegetation mapping, wildlife assessments, habitat restoration, and/or permitting implementation with support from junior biologists. Training and/or experience conducting surveys for listed species local to southern California, particularly Crotch’s Bumble Bee, Quino checkerspot butterfly, western spadefoot, and/or Stephen’s kangaroo rat, is preferred.

The responsibilities of this position could include a subset of those listed below based on relevant experience:

  • Lead protocol and pre-construction Crotch’s Bumble Bee, Quino checkerspot butterfly surveys and monitoring.
  • Lead and conduct focused western spadefoot surveys and monitoring, including implementation exclusionary fencing, artificial watering to elicit a movement response, and relocation.
  • Lead and conduct focused Stephen’s kangaroo rat trapping surveys and monitoring, including implementation exclusionary fencing, trapping, and relocation.
  • Conduct general wildlife and/or botanical surveys, including vegetation and habitat mapping.
  • Identify and record native and non-native fauna and/or flora in the field.
  • Conduct other special-status species surveys, following established protocols or guidelines as relevant.
  • Conduct avian species nesting surveys and avian mortality monitoring.
  • Support project execution, including pre-construction surveys and construction monitoring.
  • Assist with environmental compliance monitoring.
  • Provide oversight of restoration crew work and restoration vegetation performance monitoring.
  • Perform other related duties assigned, such as coordination with team members, scheduling of work, etc.
  • Utilize electronic data collection methods in the field; manage, interpret, and analyze data, as needed.
  • Conduct monitoring and survey fieldwork as part of a team and independently in inland and desert environments, which can include rugged terrain.
  • Work under the supervision of a senior project manager or senior-level team member.
  • Ensure assigned tasks stay on schedule and budget.
  • Elevate compliance concerns to project or construction managers.
  • Provide clarification of resource project requirements to the compliance and construction teams.
  • Promote safety culture and adherence to Safe Work Plans.

Join AECOM to be part of an expert global team who is connected through a well-developed, worldwide, internal technical practice network through which you can learn from and brainstorm with the best in the world. AECOM is an industry-leading, world class environmental firm, and we want you to succeed within it. We respect and encourage your own pathway to excellence via our Freedom to Grow initiative.

AECOM is known for our award-winning technical excellence, leading-edge science and innovative project delivery. We provide sustainable solutions for some of the world’s most challenging issues. Our global clients and their projects span a variety of market sectors and geographies and require innovative technical solutions to solve wide-ranging environmental problems.

Minimum Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in related field (biology, ecology, etc.)
  • 4 years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education working in southern California ecoregions focused on conducting surveys for listed species local to southern California, particularly Crotch’s Bumble Bee, Quino checkerspot butterfly, western spadefoot, and/or Stephen’s kangaroo rat.
  • Valid US Driver's License and pre-employment driving record verification are required.
  • Due to the nature of the work, US Citizenship is required.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Prior consulting experience is preferred, but non-consultant candidates with relevant experience will be considered.
  • Experience conducting biological surveys and/or environmental compliance monitoring and biological construction oversight.
  • Experience implementing the terms and conditions of USFWS biological opinions or Habitat Conservation Plans, CDFW incidental take permits, and/or California Environmental Quality Act Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Programs.

  • Analyze donor data and giving trends to refine approach

6. Internal Collaboration

  • Work closely with marketing/communications to align messaging
  • Partner with program staff to understand funding needs and impact
  • Coordinate with leadership, board members, and volunteers on donor engagement

7. Reporting & Accountability

  • Provide regular updates to leadership on pipeline and performance

and meet deadlines; manage and motivate volunteers effectively and efficiently; identify problems and develop creative, timely, and efficient solutions; adopt an entrepreneurial approach to developing and executing personal donor engagement strategies; and exercise a high level of discretion in dealing with confidential donor and prospect information.

We are looking to recruit an experienced educator to join the Raspberry Pi Foundation. The role will contribute to the development of high-quality educational materials and professional learning experiences across our programmes for young people aged 8 to 18.

You will have a background in computing science education or a closely related field, with a track record of having created curricula, resources, learning experiences, or teacher professional development activities.

Artificial intelligence and machine learning applications are already changing many aspects of our lives. Young people who understand how AI works will be better equipped to engage with the world around them, make informed decisions about using and creating AI applications, and choose what role AI will play in their futures.

A central part of this role will be supporting and advancing Experience AI, an educational program that offers cutting-edge resources on artificial intelligence and machine learning for teachers and students aged 8–18. Developed in collaboration by the Raspberry Pi Foundation and Google DeepMind, Experience AI supports teachers in this exciting and fast-moving area of AI and gets young people passionate about the subject. You will play a key role in adapting, delivering, and scaling this program in the US, while contributing to its ongoing development.

This is a remote role with a national scope. Our US team is primarily based in Metro Atlanta, Georgia, and the Twin Cities, Minnesota, so we have a preference for candidates based in or near those areas. We are also open to candidates elsewhere in the Eastern or Central time zones. The role will involve periodic travel to meet with colleagues and partners across the country.

We work hard to make sure that the Foundation is a place where everyone is supported to do the best work of their careers. We have a flexible and collaborative approach to all aspects of our work. If you're the right person for the job, we’ll make it work for you, and you can be confident that you’ll be joining an exceptional team of people who care about our mission and each other.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and deliver learning experiences, content, resources, and training for the Foundation's educational programmes and products.
  • Ensure that learning experiences, content, resources, and training reflect evidence-based pedagogy and the Foundation's agreed approaches to teaching and learning.
  • Plan and deliver engaging professional learning for educators in a range of formats, including webinars, workshops, and in-person events, adapting approaches to meet the needs of different audiences and contexts.
  • Engage positively with the Foundation's systems for quality assurance, including in relation to agreed policies for inclusion and accessibility.
  • Contribute to the development of the Foundation's teaching and learning strategy and approaches. Actively engage with research and best practice, and identify areas for improvement and innovation.
  • Proactively utilise user feedback and data to drive improvement.
  • Work collaboratively with colleagues across the organisation and external partners.
  • Represent the Raspberry Pi Foundation to external audiences and stakeholders as required.
  • Contribute to the Foundation's thought leadership through writing articles and blogs, public speaking, and contributing to research and evaluation.

Experience and personal attributes

We recognise that everyone has the potential for growth. We welcome applications from candidates who can demonstrate that they have some, but not necessarily all, of the experience and personal attributes listed here.

  • A thorough understanding of computing, with a degree or equivalent qualification in Computer Science or a related subject.
  • A teaching qualification or significant experience of teaching with at least 3 years experience of teaching computing science or a closely related field at middle and/or high school level.
  • Experience in designing and implementing AI literacy curriculum for students, combined with a demonstrable interest in the latest developments in AI for education.
  • Experience of delivering and designing high quality learning experiences, content, resources, or training in a variety of different settings and contexts.
  • Comfortable with a broad range of technologies, including hardware and software platforms, and the ability and willingness to learn new technologies as required.
  • An understanding of computing pedagogy within formal education and informal learning.
  • A commitment to the Foundation's mission and values, including on diversity, equity, and inclusion.
  • Flexibility, adaptability, and a collaborative approach to working with colleagues and external partners. Openness to working across the Foundation's programmes and products.
  • Highly organized and proactive with ability to manage multiple work streams at different stages.
  • Willingness to travel in the US and potentially internationally.

About us

The Raspberry Pi Foundation is an independent nonprofit with a global mission to enable young people to realize their full potential through the power of computer science and digital technologies. In the US we operate through Raspberry Pi Foundation North America which is a registered 501(c)(3) organization.

We empower schools to teach computing and AI literacy through free curricula, classroom resources, purpose built software tools, and professional development for teachers. We inspire young people to become tech creators through the world's largest networks of coding clubs. We undertake original research that informs our work and which we use to advance the field of computer science education more broadly.

All of our resources and learning experiences are available for anyone to use at no cost. We are particularly focused on creating opportunities for young people who experience educational disadvantage and those who come from backgrounds traditionally underrepresented in technology industries.

Over the past decade, we have supported hundreds of thousands of educators and tens of millions of students. We have teams in six countries (India, Ireland, Kenya, South Africa, the UK and US) and partnerships with mission-aligned non-profit organisations in over 60 countries.

We are at the forefront of the global educational movement to expand access to computer science education and AI literacy. You can learn more about our work in our latest Annual Report.

Benefits

In addition to competitive salaries, we offer a range of benefits for all of our colleagues, including:

  • Paid time off. In addition to public holidays, full-time employees in the US receive 15 days of paid time off, plus 3 additional days of paid time off for the company-wide closure at the end of each year.
  • Retirement Savings Plan (401)(k). We match 100% of employee contributions up to the first 5%.
  • Private Healthcare. We provide private healthcare (including dental and vision) for you and for your dependents through United Healthcare and Guardian.
  • Flexible working. We have clear policies to provide flexibility over when and where you work, helping you balance work responsibilities with the rest of your life.
  • Support for parents and carers. We provide generous family leave and flexibility for parents and carers.
  • Group term life insurance & disability insurance. We provide insurance and income protection schemes to provide peace of mind for you and your family.
  • Investing in learning and development. We invest in your growth and development, including through access to learning resources and training, with dedicated time for all employees.

Timetable for applications

Closing date: 28 September 2026, 9.00am ET

Phone screen: Week of 05 October 2026

We will cover reasonable expenses to attend the in person interview.

Our recruitment process

All of our workplaces are inclusive spaces where we want people to feel respected, valued, and able to do their best work. We are committed to building teams that bring together people with a broad range of backgrounds, skills, and perspectives. That starts with our recruitment process.

Here's what you can expect:

  • As part of your application, you will be asked to respond to a small number of questions that we will use to screen your eligibility for the role. You will also be asked to provide your resume.
  • Eligible applications will be reviewed by our recruitment team and the hiring manager. We review all applications for authenticity. While we embrace the use of AI tools to assist you, all content must genuinely represent your own work, and have been reviewed and personalised by you.
  • A small number of candidates will be invited to a phone call with the hiring manager. The purpose of this call is to check our understanding of your application and to answer any questions you have.
  • We normally have two interviews, which may take place in-person. Interviews will be with the hiring manager and at least one other colleague.
  • You will usually be asked to undertake a work-based assessment in advance of your interviews. This will be an opportunity for you to show how you would perform some part of the role. You will be given advance notice and clear instructions.
  • If you have any questions about or feel that you need any adjustments to the recruitment process, including adjustments for neurodiversity, please contact our People and Culture team at .

We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people, and we expect all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. Further background checks will be made at regular intervals thereafter.

jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

‎

Mosaic Health is seeking an Assistant Vice President of AI Strategy & Transformation to own the enterprise-wide AI strategy, governance, and portfolio execution across Mosaic Health, CareMore, Vera Whole Health, and Millennium. This is a high-visibility, high-accountability role at the center of one of the most consequential transformation programs in the organization's history: an enterprise AI value creation mandate for 2026-27 and a newly established three-tier governance structure built to deliver it.



The AVP, AI Strategy & Transformation serves as the primary AI strategy executive for the enterprise, partnering directly with the CIIO and enterprise IT leadership to translate AI investment into measurable clinical, operational, and financial outcomes. This leader chairs the AI Transformation Hub, serves as the AI Executive Council's Lead by owning its agenda, materials, and decision-drive alongside the Co-Chairs, owns the Horizon Framework execution discipline, drives the 90-day gate process, holds named decision rights within the Transformation Hub's authority threshold, and is the named accountability anchor for AI portfolio performance across all four business units.



This is not a research or exploratory role, and it is not a program-management role. It functions as the operating executive for enterprise AI transformation: bringing recommendations to the AI Executive Council for input and sign-off rather than simply reporting status upward, and holding direct decision rights within defined thresholds. The AVP will be expected to move the portfolio forward with speed, discipline, and business partnership: eliminating bureaucracy, enforcing fixed-fee cost discipline, and holding the organization accountable to outcomes that justify every dollar of AI investment.

‎

How will you make an impact & Requirements

‎

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise AI Strategy

  • Own and advance the enterprise AI strategy in partnership with the CIIO and enterprise IT leadership: translating the Horizon AI Framework into a prioritized, funded, and accountable initiative portfolio
  • Define the annual AI investment roadmap aligned to H1, H2, and H3 objectives; present recommendations to the AI Executive Council with clear ROI models and risk assessments
  • Ensure AI strategy is built with the business, not imposed on it, by maintaining active partnerships with clinical, financial, and operational leaders across all four BUs
  • Evaluate and recommend adoption of new AI capabilities and emerging technologies, balancing innovation appetite with fixed-fee cost discipline and enterprise standardization

Governance Execution

  • Chair the AI Transformation Hub: owning the bi-weekly cadence, initiative registry, intake discipline, and all in-threshold go/no-go decisions within the authority bands
  • Own the operating rhythm of the monthly AI Executive Council, co-chaired by the CIO and Jon Porter: setting the agenda, preparing portfolio scorecards, escalation packages, and ROI progress reports, and driving Council input and sign-off against the enterprise value creation framework
  • Enforce the 90-day gate process for all active initiatives: making scale, stop, or pivot decisions within the Transformation Hub authority threshold and escalating above-threshold decisions to the AI Executive Council with structured recommendations
  • Maintain the enterprise AI initiative registry across all four BUs; ensure every initiative has a named owner, a Horizon designation, and an active gate status
  • Manage the HIPAA/compliance gate as a mandatory stop for all initiatives touching PHI, clinical workflows, or patient data, no exceptions

Governance Effectiveness & Continuous Improvement

  • Own evaluation of how the AI governance and execution structure itself is performing, not just the initiatives running through it
  • Design and run the After Action Report (AAR) / retrospective cadence and structure across the Transformation Hub, Executive Council, and Solutions Team tiers
  • Execute that structure on a defined cadence, identify structural and process improvements, and build buy-in with the AI Executive Council before implementing changes
  • Drive improvement recommendations to resolution with measured, before/after outcomes: the governance model is expected to get faster and more effective release over release, not remain static

Portfolio Performance & ROI

  • Own delivery against the enterprise AI value creation framework for 2026: tracking initiative-level ROI, surfacing risks with 30-day advance notice to the AI Executive Council, and driving corrective action on underperforming initiatives
  • Build and maintain the enterprise AI ROI tracking framework, connecting initiative outcomes to financial, clinical, and operational metrics
  • Ensure every active initiative has a clear 90-day performance signal before any H2 or scale investment is authorized
  • Partner with Finance to validate AI ROI claims and ensure savings attributed to AI initiatives are recognized in the financial plan

Business Partnership & Cross-BU Coordination

  • Serve as the enterprise AI strategy partner to business unit leaders across CareMore, apree/Vera Whole Health, Millennium, and Mosaic Health: translating AI capabilities into domain-specific value
  • Partner with clinical, operational, and financial leaders to identify and prioritize AI use cases with the highest ROI and lowest risk profiles
  • Manage the AI Solutions Team engagement model across the Delivery tier: ensuring named reps in each BU and function are engaged, accountable, and delivering initiative-level outcomes
  • Escalate persistent Solutions Team Rep disengagement to the CIIO; coordinate interim ownership for high-ROI initiatives at risk

Vendor Strategy & Procurement Discipline

  • Evaluate AI vendor proposals and make selection recommendations for contracts within the Transformation Hub authority threshold
  • Enforce the enterprise default posture of fixed-fee, defined-scope contracting for all AI vendors; open-ended T&M arrangements require AI Executive Council approval
  • Coordinate with Procurement, Legal, and IT Security on vendor due diligence, contract terms, data use agreements, and BAA requirements
  • Maintain awareness of the AI vendor landscape across clinical AI, operational automation, ambient documentation, revenue cycle, and population health to inform the strategic roadmap

Responsible AI & Clinical Safety

  • Ensure all AI initiatives governed under the charter comply with the enterprise Responsible AI framework: clinical safety, algorithmic bias review, explainability, regulatory compliance, data minimization, and human oversight
  • Partner with Clinical Affairs and Compliance to ensure clinical AI tools complete mandatory safety assessments before go-live
  • Identify FDA SaMD-qualifying tools early and ensure regulatory counsel involvement before any clinical deployment
  • Monitor and report AI-related compliance, safety, and reputational risks to the AI Executive Council

Team Leadership & Organizational Capability

  • Lead, develop, and hold accountable the Director of Emerging Technology; set clear expectations, maintain a high standard of portfolio rigor, and create conditions for the team to execute with excellence
  • Build organizational AI fluency across the enterprise: developing training, communication, and change management approaches that accelerate adoption across clinical and business teams
  • Recruit and develop AI talent, including data scientists, AI product managers, and clinical AI specialists, as the portfolio scales from H1 pilots to H2 transformation
  • Represent Mosaic in the external AI ecosystem: vendor partnerships, industry working groups, and peer network engagement, to keep the enterprise at the frontier of healthcare AI

Qualifications

Experience

  • 10+ years of progressive experience leading large-scale business transformation, from ideation through delivery, scale, and measured results, with at least 5 years owning transformation programs with enterprise-wide, multi-entity scope
  • Proven track record taking transformation initiatives from concept to operating reality in organizations where technology, field/frontline operations, and data were central to the outcome, not purely a technology deployment
  • Demonstrated experience owning governance and prioritization discipline for a complex initiative portfolio in a regulated or compliance-intensive environment: including intake, gating, vendor selection, and resource allocation
  • Experience leading cross-functional governance bodies: committees, working groups, or enterprise boards/councils, with the ability to drive alignment, decisions, and resolution of C-suite-level conflicts without relying on direct line authority
  • Demonstrated ability to deliver results primarily through influence and cross-functional leadership rather than positional power, operating effectively in complex, matrixed, multi-entity organizations
  • Experience in healthcare, health plan, or another highly regulated industry is a differentiator, not a requirement; genuine interest in and working familiarity with how AI applies to enterprise transformation is expected
  • Demonstrated ability to manage large, complex vendor relationships with fixed-fee commercial discipline

AI & Technology Fluency

  • Strong working knowledge of AI and ML technologies, including large language models, generative AI, predictive analytics, and NLP, with the ability to evaluate vendor claims, assess technical risk, and guide build vs. buy decisions
  • Familiarity with healthcare AI platforms and vendors relevant to Mosaic's portfolio (ambient clinical documentation, clinical decision support, care management AI, revenue cycle automation)
  • Understanding of data governance and data infrastructure requirements that underpin reliable AI deployment: data pipelines, model lifecycle management, monitoring, and drift detection
  • Awareness of FDA SaMD regulatory pathway and HIPAA requirements as they apply to AI tools in clinical and patient-facing contexts

Skills & Competencies

  • Executive presence: able to communicate AI strategy, risk, and portfolio performance clearly to an AI Executive Council accountable for enterprise AI value creation and to clinical, financial, and operational leaders who are not technologists
  • Governance instincts: comfortable designing and operating governance structures, not just participating in them: owns the framework, enforces the discipline, eliminates the ambiguity
  • Business partnership orientation: earns credibility with business and clinical stakeholders by delivering outcomes they can measure, not AI concepts they have to interpret
  • Commercial discipline: approaches every vendor engagement, build decision, and resource allocation with a fixed-fee, defined-ROI mindset: cost discipline is not a preference, it is the standard
  • Portfolio management: able to hold 14+ concurrent initiatives in view simultaneously: tracking status, surfacing risk, sequencing decisions, and maintaining stakeholder visibility without losing momentum
  • Change leadership: drives adoption across a complex, multi-entity organization where authority is federated and results depend on named accountability at the BU level

‎

jobs.excerpt: The OpportunityFutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead LucentAI, an AI-native litigation operations venture in build at FutureSight.
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to lead LucentAI, an AI-native litigation operations venture in build at FutureSight. This offers meaningful founder equity, not a salary.

LucentAI serves as an autopilot for medical-records and discovery operations in small-to-mid insurance-defence firms. Embedding in case-management systems, it retrieves and reviews records, flags key facts with confidence links, checks billing reasonableness, and chronologically triages discovery. This human-gated system excludes legal drafting, externalizing review capacity so firms can scale case volume without adding headcount.

Market validation through FutureSight’s discovery interviews confirmed strong demand:

  • Operations is the wedge; autopilot is the vision. All buyers wanted managed operations. LucentAI provides end-to-end automation, earning trust incrementally by handling routine work silently while keeping legal drafting human.
  • The pain is in the dollars, not the dashboards. One lead costs the middle phase at ~$1M/year in time and errors; a partner noted only ~$200K of a $1M medical bill was reasonable. With zero AI currently used, the ROI-driven payback case is immediate.
  • Capacity is the ceiling, and the record is the moat. Manual partner review caps case capacity and revenue. Defence records and billing patterns form a proprietary dataset that plaintiff-focused incumbents lack.

Market Context

We target underserved small-to-mid US insurance-defence firms.

The Phase-1 beachhead SAM is $150M–$600M across 1,500–3,000 firms; the full roadmap reaches a ≥$100M obtainable market (SOM ≈ $110M–$360M).

With 71% of legal AI funding flowing to plaintiff-focused companies, the defence market remains underserved, creating a need for technology purpose-built for litigation defence and risk management.

About FutureSight

FutureSight is a leading venture builder that co-creates world-class software companies with values-driven entrepreneurs from inception to exit. We are a team of founders, operators and designers with experience successfully bringing software to market at scale.

You’ll co-create with a proven studio team, led by John Carbrey (4x entrepreneur, $100M ARR), Krista LaRiviere (3x exited, E&Y Top Women Entrepreneur), Alan Smith (Strategyzer co-founder, $120M in products built), Prathna Ramesh (former MD of Maple Leaf Angels, $275M in follow-on capital), and Johnny Tong (0-to-1 builder, acquired by SAP and Stripe) bring a rare combination of operator exits, institutional investing, and AI product depth.

The Partnership

  • Founder equity with meaningful ownership from inception
  • Pre-seed capital committed by FutureSight for early hires and MVP development, with potential for follow-on funding
  • Venture building resources, including embedded design, engineering, growth, and fundraising support from day one
  • Investor and advisor network across vertical AI and early-stage capital markets
  • A true co-creation model in which you operate as CEO with FutureSight's cross-functional team as your partner

What you'll own

As Co-Founder & CEO, you will set the venture's direction and lead its execution.

  • Strategy — Refine the ICP, size-tiered pricing model, and product positioning
  • Customer Development — Lead pilots with managing partners and claims/litigation-operations leads at small-to-mid insurance-defence firms, starting from the confirmed design partner, convert them to paid engagements, and build the go-to-market motion

jobs.excerpt: NVIDIA's Product Security organization is looking for a Senior Offensive Security Engineer to push the frontier of AI-driven offensive security.
jobs.description:
NVIDIA's Product Security organization is looking for a Senior Offensive Security Engineer to push the frontier of AI-driven offensive security. We already run language model agents that audit source code and attack live web applications at fleet scale. These include multi-agent orchestration, adversarial verification, exploit-confirmation harnesses, and sandboxed execution. Your job is to make these agents meaningfully better attackers: new attack capabilities, new target classes, higher true-positive rates, and safer autonomy. This is a hands-on role for someone who is both a strong offensive security practitioner and a builder of agentic systems. Join us!

What you'll be doing:

  • Crafting and building new red team agents: autonomous and semi-autonomous LLM agents that perform reconnaissance, hypothesis-driven exploitation, and evidence capture against NVIDIA-owned targets

  • Extending our existing agent harnesses (multi-phase orchestration, parallel specialist subagents, judge/verifier stages, out-of-band callback infrastructure) across multiple agent runtimes and model providers

  • Encoding real operator tradecraft into prompts, tools, and playbooks — web app exploitation, auth bypass, SSRF/deserialization chains, cloud and Kubernetes attack paths — so agents find what a skilled human would

  • Building the verification layer: exploit-confirmation harnesses that prove findings are real before a human ever sees them, driving false-positive rates down

  • Engineering the safety side of autonomy: sandboxing, scope enforcement, tool allowlists/blocklists, credential isolation, and prompt-injection defenses for agents operating with offensive capability

  • Evaluating and benchmarking frontier models for offensive tasks; partnering with our human red team to turn their engagements into repeatable agent capabilities

  • Mentoring engineers on the team and setting the technical bar for agentic offensive tooling

What we need to see:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience

  • 12+ years in security engineering, with at least 4 years in offensive security: penetration testing, red teaming, exploit development, or vulnerability research

  • Deep, hands-on exploitation skill in at least one domain (web application, cloud/Kubernetes, or systems/binary) — you can build and prove an exploit chain, not just run a scanner

  • Strong software engineering ability in Python; you ship production code, not just PoCs

  • Practical experience building with LLMs: agent frameworks, tool use/function calling, multi-agent orchestration, or coding agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, or similar)

  • Sound judgment about autonomous offensive tooling — scoping, authorization, and blast-radius thinking are second nature

  • Respectful, responsible approach to offensive testing — we break things carefully and fix them fast

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Published security research, CVEs, conference talks, or notable CTF results

  • Certifications like OSWE, OSEP, OSCP, or GXPN

  • Experience with SAST/DAST internals, fuzzing, or program analysis

  • Experience red-teaming AI systems themselves (prompt injection, jailbreaks, model evaluation) or contributing to AI-security research

  • Familiarity with Kubernetes/OpenShift, GitOps, and operating worker fleets at scale

With competitive salaries and a generous benefits package, NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world's most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and talented people in the world working for us and, due to unprecedented growth, our elite engineering teams are rapidly growing. If you're a creative and autonomous engineer with a real passion for technology, we want to hear from you!

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 224,000 USD - 356,500 USD for Level 5, and 272,000 USD - 431,250 USD for Level 6.

jobs.excerpt: Our team members are at the heart of everything we do.
jobs.description:
Our team members are at the heart of everything we do. At Cencora, we are united in our responsibility to create healthier futures, and every person here is essential to us being able to deliver on that purpose. If you want to make a difference at the center of health, come join our innovative company and help us improve the lives of people and animals everywhere. Apply today!

Job Details

The Group Product Owner – PSAO Solutions is responsible for defining the long-term vision, product strategy, roadmap, and execution priorities for the PSAO solution base within Community Pharmacy Solutions. Reporting to the VP, Solution Development and Innovation, this role owns product direction and product lifecycle outcomes for Central Pay, Audit and Compliance, Reconciliation, and Pharmacy Quality and Performance solutions. The role ensures these solutions are customer-centered, operationally scalable, compliant, commercially viable, and continuously improved based on voice-of-customer, market dynamics, internal performance insights, and evolving payer/PBM requirements.

This role focuses on product ownership of PSAO solution capabilities and the development of adjacent offerings that support pharmacies in navigating payer/PBM environment complexity, including a direct contract support offering and other related PSAO and PBM contracting solutions. The role partners closely with dedicated provider network contracting, legal, compliance, operations, finance, technology, commercialization, and customer-facing stakeholders, but does not directly manage the contracting lifecycle.

The Group Product Owner also supports Elevate's transition into medical payer contracting by identifying solution requirements, workflow needs, pharmacy enablement capabilities, data/reporting requirements, operational dependencies, and product implications associated with medical payer participation. This work is performed in close partnership with the Sr Director, Elevate Provider Network and internal and external stakeholders responsible for medical payer relationships, network strategy, contracting, operations, compliance, and commercialization.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities:

Product Vision, Strategy, and Roadmap – PSAO Solutions

  • Define and own the product vision, strategic priorities, roadmap, value proposition, and business outcomes for the PSAO Solutions product group.

  • Maintain an outcome-focused roadmap for Central Pay, Audit and Compliance, Reconciliation, and Pharmacy Quality and Performance capabilities.

  • Prioritize product investments, enhancements, and backlog items based on customer value, business impact, operational feasibility, compliance considerations, financial performance, and alignment to CPS and Elevate priorities.

  • Translate payer/PBM, pharmacy, regulatory, operational, and customer insights into product strategy and roadmap decisions for the PSAO solution base.

  • Ensure PSAO solutions are designed and evolved to improve pharmacy experience, payment reliability, reconciliation transparency, audit/compliance readiness, quality program performance, and measurable business outcomes.

Central Pay Product Ownership and Platform Evolution

  • Oversee product strategy and roadmap priorities for Central Pay capabilities, including user experience, workflow efficiency, payment visibility, exception handling, risk controls, reporting, and platform enhancements.

  • Partner with finance, treasury, operations, technology, customer support, and vendor partners to ensure Central Pay processes are reliable, timely, scalable, and customer-centered.

  • Identify opportunities to improve payment workflows, user access governance, exception resolution, reporting transparency, and operational controls.

  • Define Central Pay success measures and monitor adoption, utilization, issue resolution, customer satisfaction, payment timeliness, and operational performance.

  • Build feedback loops with pharmacies, internal users, operations, finance, and customer-facing teams to continuously improve Central Pay capabilities.

Audit and Compliance Solution Ownership

  • Oversee product roadmap and enhancement priorities for PSAO Audit and Compliance solutions, including tools, workflows, reporting, communications, readiness materials, and pharmacy-facing support capabilities.

  • Partner with compliance, legal, operations, audit support, customer-facing teams, and technology stakeholders to ensure audit and compliance solutions are accurate, scalable, well-documented, and aligned to applicable requirements.

  • Translate compliance trends, audit patterns, pharmacy pain points, and operational insights into product requirements and improvement opportunities.

  • Support development of audit readiness and compliance enablement capabilities that help pharmacies understand obligations, respond effectively, reduce risk, and improve performance.

  • Define success metrics for Audit and Compliance solutions, including issue resolution, pharmacy engagement, compliance readiness, customer satisfaction, and risk mitigation indicators.

Reconciliation Solution Ownership

  • Oversee product strategy and roadmap priorities for reconciliation capabilities that support payment transparency, issue identification, exception tracking, dispute support, and customer-facing visibility.

  • Partner with finance, operations, technology, analytics, and customer support teams to define reconciliation workflows, data requirements, reporting needs, and scalable resolution processes.

  • Identify opportunities to improve reconciliation accuracy, speed, transparency, customer usability, exception management, and reporting consistency.

  • Ensure reconciliation capabilities are connected to Central Pay, audit/compliance, customer support, and broader PSAO solution workflows where appropriate.

  • Define and monitor reconciliation KPIs, including cycle time, issue volume, resolution rates, customer adoption, reporting usage, and operational efficiency.

Pharmacy Quality and Performance Product Ownership

  • Oversee product strategy and roadmap priorities for Pharmacy Quality and Performance solutions, including quality measures, performance reporting, clinical or payer program requirements, pharmacy enablement, and outcomes-based performance opportunities.

  • Translate payer/PBM program requirements, quality measure changes, performance trends, and pharmacy customer needs into actionable product requirements and enablement capabilities.

  • Partner with analytics, quality, operations, clinical, commercialization, adoption, and customer-facing stakeholders to ensure pharmacies receive clear, actionable, and measurable performance support.

  • Develop and scale solution capabilities that help pharmacies understand requirements, identify barriers, prioritize interventions, and improve quality and performance outcomes.

  • Define KPIs and performance routines for pharmacy quality and performance solutions, including measure performance, customer engagement, adoption, program impact, and payer/PBM value.

Direct Contract Support and Related PSAO / PBM Contracting Solutions

  • Lead product discovery, strategy, and roadmap development for a direct contract support offering designed to help pharmacies navigate payer/PBM contracting opportunities and requirements.

  • Define customer problems, target users, service model requirements, workflow needs, data/reporting requirements, value proposition, commercialization inputs, and operational implications for direct contract support capabilities.

  • Develop and prioritize related PSAO and PBM contracting solutions that support pharmacy understanding, decision-making, readiness, tracking, analytics, support workflows, and customer enablement.

  • Partner with provider network contracting, legal, compliance, operations, sales, commercialization, finance, and customer-facing stakeholders to ensure direct contract support concepts are feasible, compliant, supportable, and differentiated.

  • Establish pilot, proof-of-concept, and scale recommendations for direct contract support and adjacent PSAO/PBM contracting solutions, including success criteria and measurable customer/business outcomes.

Support for Elevate Medical Payer Contracting Transition

  • Support Elevate's transition into medical payer contracting by identifying product, workflow, data, reporting, pharmacy enablement, and operational capabilities required to support medical payer participation.

  • Partner with the Sr Director, Elevate Provider Network on medical payer contracting strategy implications, pharmacy readiness needs, support model requirements, and solution gaps.

  • Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders, including provider network, legal, compliance, operations, finance, analytics, commercialization, sales, technology, and payer-facing partners, to define product needs associated with medical payer contracting.

  • Translate medical payer contracting requirements into product backlog items, roadmap themes, stage-gate inputs, enablement requirements, and solution design recommendations.

  • Monitor customer and operational feedback from medical payer contracting transition activities and use insights to refine PSAO solution priorities and support models.

Backlog Ownership, Requirements, and Product Delivery

  • Maintain and prioritize the PSAO Solutions backlog across Central Pay, Audit and Compliance, Reconciliation, Pharmacy Quality and Performance, direct contract support, and related PSAO/PBM contracting solutions.

  • Lead requirements development and validation with internal and external customers, operations, compliance, finance, technology, provider network, commercialization, and customer-facing stakeholders.

  • Partner with Product Owners, Product Managers, UX/design, technology, analytics, and delivery teams to translate customer needs into user stories, acceptance criteria, release goals, and measurable outcomes.

  • Identify and manage dependencies, risks, resource conflicts, compliance considerations, operational readiness needs, and cross-functional impacts across PSAO solution initiatives.

  • Ensure delivery priorities support roadmap strategy and are coordinated with commercialization, enablement, support, and operational teams.

Commercialization Readiness, VOC, and Performance Measurement

  • Partner with commercialization, product marketing, enablement, operations, and customer-facing teams to prepare PSAO solutions and new offerings for launch, adoption, and ongoing optimization.

  • Define launch goals, success metrics, customer readiness needs, support model expectations, training inputs, communications requirements, and adoption barriers for PSAO solution releases.

  • Establish voice-of-customer and feedback mechanisms across pharmacies, internal users, payer/PBM stakeholders, operations, support teams, and customer-facing teams.

  • Monitor product performance, customer adoption, operational outcomes, issue trends, financial indicators, compliance signals, and customer satisfaction to guide roadmap and corrective actions.

  • Provide regular leadership updates on PSAO solution health, backlog priorities, roadmap progress, risks, and recommendations.

Cross-Functional Leadership and Stakeholder Alignment

  • Provide product leadership across PSAO solution domains while coordinating closely with dedicated contracting, provider network, operations, finance, compliance, legal, technology, analytics, commercialization, and enablement teams.

  • Promote collaboration and alignment across teams responsible for Central Pay, Audit and Compliance, Reconciliation, Pharmacy Quality and Performance, direct contract support, and medical payer contracting transition workstreams.

  • Create clear role boundaries and handoffs between product strategy, operational execution, contracting lifecycle management, legal/compliance review, customer support, and commercialization activities.

  • Facilitate decision-making, prioritization, and issue resolution across matrixed stakeholders to support timely delivery and measurable outcomes.

  • Serve as the PSAO Solutions product thought partner to CPS and Elevate leadership on customer needs, solution gaps, product performance, and future capability opportunities.

Compliance and Other

  • Ensure PSAO solution development, product documentation, customer-facing capabilities, and support models comply with applicable company policies, legal requirements, regulatory standards, payer/PBM requirements, privacy expectations, and compliance obligations.

  • Perform related duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred in business, healthcare administration, pharmacy, product management, finance, operations, or related field.

  • 8+ years of experience in product management, PSAO operations, managed care, pharmacy services, PBM/payer programs, payment operations, compliance, quality performance, or related healthcare/pharmacy services roles.

  • Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional product or solution initiatives with measurable customer, operational, compliance, financial, or adoption outcomes.

  • Experience with Central Pay, reconciliation, audit/compliance, pharmacy quality programs, PSAO, managed care, payer/PBM contracting support, or pharmacy network operations preferred.

  • Experience developing new offerings, service models, pilots, proofs of concept, or product capabilities from concept through launch preferred.

  • Experience working with internal and external stakeholders across legal, compliance, finance, operations, technology, commercialization, provider network, and customer-facing teams preferred.

Minimum Skills, Knowledge, and Ability Requirements

  • Strong product management discipline, including product vision, strategy, roadmap ownership, backlog prioritization, requirements definition, launch readiness, and post-launch measurement.

  • Strong understanding of PSAO solutions, pharmacy payment operations, audit/compliance support, reconciliation workflows, pharmacy quality performance programs, and payer/PBM dynamics.

  • Ability to translate pharmacy, payer/PBM, operational, compliance, and customer needs into product requirements, roadmap priorities, and scalable support models.

  • Strong analytical skills and ability to use data, customer insights, operational performance, financial indicators, and risk signals to guide product decisions.

  • Strong cross-functional leadership skills with ability to influence without authority across operations, finance, legal, compliance, contracting, technology, commercialization, analytics, and customer-facing teams.

  • Strong communication skills, including ability to synthesize complex product, operational, contracting, payer/PBM, and compliance topics into clear recommendations and executive-ready updates.

  • Knowledge of medical payer contracting, pharmacy services, Elevate Provider Network strategy, and direct contracting support models preferred.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and ability to interpret dashboards, product performance reports, workflow analytics, and roadmap/backlog management tools.

Work Environment

jobs.description:
About Dutchie

Founded in 2017, Dutchie is a comprehensive technology platform powering dispensary operations, while providing consumers with safe and easy access to cannabis. Dutchie aims to further support the positive societal change the cannabis industry brings to the world through wellness benefits, social justice, and empowering local communities through tax revenue. Powering thousands of dispensaries across 40+ markets throughout the United States and Canada, Dutchie is the leading technology company in the cannabis space and was named in Fast Company’s 10 Most Innovative Companies in North America and listed two years in a row on LinkedIn’s Top 50 Startups.

Dutchie has raised over $600M in funding to date, backed by D1 Capital Partners, Tiger Global, Dragoneer, DFJ Growth, Thrive Capital, Howard Schultz, Snoop Dogg’s Casa Verde Capital, Gron Ventures, members of the founding team at DoorDash, Kevin Durant’s Thirty Five Ventures, and other notable angel investors.

About This Job

The Senior Project Manager, GTM Launch owns the launch management system that gets Dutchie’s feature and product launches from ready-to-launch through adoption and measurable impact across our full product suite. This is a senior, autonomous role within Revenue Operations, acting as the connective tissue across Product, Engineering, Enablement, Marketing, Support, go-to-market teams, and most importantly, our customers.

You will lead complex launches with minimal oversight, proactively surface risk before it becomes an escalation, and own change management for both internal teams and customers. You’ll be equally comfortable driving a cross-functional operating cadence, influencing senior stakeholders when scope or timing is at risk, and pulling adoption data yourself to measure success and impact.

Success is not simply shipping on time; it is ensuring teams are ready, customers understand the value, adoption follows, and each launch makes the next one better.

What You'll Do…

  • Own end-to-end project management for assigned feature and product launches — scoping, sequencing, timelines, dependencies, go/no-go criteria, and post-launch follow-through — in partnership with Product and Engineering leads.
  • Maintain the launch board as the single source of truth, ensuring active launches have clear status, ownership, dependencies, risks, decisions, and next steps.
  • Establish and run efficient, action-oriented launch cadences that keep cross-functional teams aligned, surface decisions early, and drive clear accountability.
  • Design and run internal change management for each launch, including readiness plans for Sales, CSM, Support, Implementation, Marketing, and Enablement, with clear ownership of what must be true before GA.
  • Design and run customer-facing change management, including rollout sequencing, customer communications, pilot or cohort strategy, and coordination with Marketing and Support.
  • Proactively identify blocked or at-risk work, clarify tradeoffs, and coordinate solutions before stakeholders have to escalate.
  • Translate changes in scope, timing, or dependencies into clear downstream business and customer impact, and drive the right stakeholders toward decisions.
  • Develop working product knowledge deep enough to answer audience, functionality, and semi-technical questions on each launch without unnecessary escalation, connecting feature-level detail to customer and business impact.
  • Partner closely with Technical Writing and Enablement, validating that release notes, training materials, internal guidance, and customer communications accurately reflect product functionality and positioning.
  • Define success metrics before launch across internal readiness and external outcomes such as adoption, activation, usage, customer sentiment, and support volume.
  • Monitor post-launch performance and proactively engage pilot, alpha, or early-adopter customers to identify friction, validate value, and surface emerging risks.
  • Build feedback loops that turn launch data and customer signals into action — flagging underperformance quickly and driving retrospectives that result in clear owners and follow-through.
  • Continuously improve the launch operating system by identifying high-leverage process, tooling, or automation opportunities and driving stakeholder alignment through implementation.
  • Use AI and the broader tool suite to accelerate research, synthesize launch signals, improve documentation and reporting, identify risk patterns, and reduce manual work — while applying judgment and validating outputs.

What You Bring

  • 5+ years of project or program management experience, with meaningful ownership of feature or product launches in a SaaS or technology GTM environment.
  • Demonstrated ownership of change management for both internal teams and external customers, including readiness, communications, rollout strategy, and adoption.
  • Strong analytical orientation: able to define launch success metrics, pull and interpret product or usage data, and translate findings into action.
  • Proven track record of proactive communication and risk management — surfaces issues early, frames tradeoffs clearly, and drives toward resolution.
  • Strong facilitation and operating-rhythm skills: keeps cross-functional groups focused, drives decisions, and creates clear accountability without relying on formal authority.
  • Demonstrated curiosity and follow-through: builds enough product and domain expertise to represent launches credibly with stakeholders and customers, and validates rather than assumes.
  • Experience improving cross-functional processes, systems, or tooling and driving those changes through adoption.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication; able to influence senior stakeholders, hold a line on scope or timeline with empathy, and adapt communication for technical, GTM, and customer audiences.

It’s a Bonus if You…

  • Experience with SQL, Excel/Sheets, and BI or product analytics tools such as Hex or Pendo for pulling and interpreting launch data directly.
  • Experience using AI/LLM tools to improve research, synthesis, documentation, reporting, workflow automation, or decision support.
  • Cannabis, regulated industry, or other multi-segment (SMB / Mid-Market / Enterprise) GTM experience.
  • Background working in or alongside a Revenue Operations function structured around the full customer lifecycle.

You’ll Get…

We are targeting a starting salary of $102,000 - $138,000 based on the intended level for this role.

In addition to cash compensation, our total rewards package includes:

  • Full medical benefits including dental and vision plans to ensure you always have the best care.
  • Equity packages in the form of stock options to all employees.
  • Technology (hardware, software, reading materials, etc..) allowance
  • Flexible vacation and sick days

At Dutchie, we’re committed to providing an environment of mutual respect where equal employment opportunities are available to all applicants and teammates without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, age, national origin, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Dutchie believes that diversity and inclusion among our teammates is critical to our success, and we seek to recruit, develop and retain the most talented people from a diverse candidate pool.

Senior Copywriter

Our Company

Adobe Creative is Adobe’s in-house brand-creative engine, developing the ideas, campaigns, and assets that power Adobe’s brand and business. We are part of the broader Content & Creative (“C&C”) organization. We work alongside Adobe Content, which focuses on publishing and audience development through owned, earned, and partner channels; an Experiences team, which oversees Adobe’s real-world moments; and shared service teams spanning Video, Talent, Partnerships, and Production.

The Opportunity

Adobe makes the tools the world uses to create. Our own writing and storytelling should set the standard for what those tools make possible. Adobe Creative is looking for an exceptionalSenior Copywriterto create clear, original and culturally relevant work across Adobe Creative’s output.

You will write across campaigns, multi-platform storytelling, product narratives, brand films and live experiences, moving confidently between a sharp headline, a product narrative, a script, and a multi-platform idea. Working alongside Copy leaders, Creative Directors, Designers, Strategists and Product partners, you will help turn complex briefs and technologies into language people can understand, feel and remember.

You will be part of a new copywriting practice built for how brands communicate today. You will contribute to copywriters’ rooms, help develop narratives and verbal systems, and use AI-enabled tools to expand creative exploration without giving up human judgment, originality, or craft.

You are a writer first. You still search for the unexpected line, challenge the first answer, and care deeply about every word.

What You’ll Do

Write Across the Work

  • Create original copy across campaigns, multi-platform storytelling, product narratives, brand films, and live experiences.

  • Move fluidly between headlines, scripts, manifestos, product narratives, multi-platform ideas and longer-form storytelling.

  • Translate complex product capabilities and audience insights into simple, human, and compelling language.

  • Develop writing that feels recognizably Adobe without becoming corporate, repetitive or predictable.

  • Carry copywriting work from early concept through final copy, maintaining quality across every stage.

  • Partner with Creative Directors, Copy leaders and Strategists to develop campaign platforms, creative territories and narrative frameworks.

  • Challenge language that feels generic, overly technical or disconnected from culture.

  • Partner with Brand and Copy leadership to bring Adobe’s verbal identity to life across real work.

  • Help develop voice frameworks, messaging systems, naming approaches, and reusable writing tools.

  • Create systems that help teams work faster without losing personality, clarity, or craft.

  • Identify inconsistencies and opportunities to strengthen Adobe’s voice through application.

  • Share writing practices, references, and learning with the broader creative community.
